rule: Anchor a minimal hero on one large rendered 3D object with a short uppercase headline beside it and small monospace/labelled navigation.
do: Grey/neutral page, one glowing 3D centerpiece, headline like 'WE'RE A FULL-SERVICE AI AUTOMATION AGENCY.' left-aligned

rule: Keep the interface near-monochrome (greys/white) and let a single warm accent (orange/amber glow) carry the brand.
Use an interactive 'drag to reveal' control on a hero image to invite exploration of the product.
do: Circular drag handle with label 'DRAG TO REVEAL' over a covered car

rule: Structure a SaaS landing page as: hero with value proposition + single CTA, 3-step how-it-works, old-way vs new-way comparison, use cases, pricing (3 tiers, middle highlighted), FAQ accordion, integrations, final CTA, footer.
values: Pricing: Free / $9 / $49

rule: Remove friction: one clear value proposition, strong visual hierarchy, trust signals at the right moments and one focused CTA.
Show an 'old way vs our way' side-by-side card: muted light card with crossed-out pain points next to a dark highlighted card with checkmarked benefits.
Build a home page for exploration (multiple CTAs, navigation, broad brand overview) and a landing page for one specific goal with a single focused CTA.
Update the UI immediately on tap (optimistic update) and save in the background instead of waiting for the server.
do: setLiked(); save()
dont: await save(); setLiked() with a pending spinner
values: waits for server 730 ms vs optimistic 16 ms

rule: Use one aspect ratio for all cards in a row so images and text baselines line up.
dont: Mixing 1:1, 16:9 and 4:3 cards in one row

rule: Tint your dark grays slightly toward the brand hue instead of using pure neutral gray.
values: 4% teal tint

rule: Put form labels outside/above the input as a real <label>; do not rely on placeholder text as the label because it disappears when typing.
do: <label for="email">Email</label>
dont: placeholder="Email" only

rule: Use familiar layout patterns and common icons so users can transfer what they know from other products; avoid forcing them to relearn basics.
do: Use familiar patterns, keep common icons recognizable, reuse expected interactions
dont: Unusual patterns that feel confusing

rule: For a trustworthy fintech app, pair an off-white background with a navy primary and a mint-green accent.
values: Background off-white #F5F7FA; Primary navy #1E3A8A; Accent mint green #10B981

rule: Make the outer corner radius equal to the inner radius plus the padding between them so nested corners look concentric.
do: Inner 16 + padding 8 = outer 24
dont: Outer radius = inner radius (16 and 16)

rule: Use a bottom tab bar as the primary navigation in mobile apps (as in Instagram, WhatsApp), with ~5 icon destinations.

Structure an ecommerce homepage for discovery: clear value proposition, primary CTA above the fold, shop by category, featured products, how it works, personalized discovery, promotions with a reason to act, FAQ for objection handling, strong final CTA.

Structure a product page for the buying decision: strong product hero, CTA impossible to miss, social proof near the buying decision, benefits not just features, reviews and ratings, evidence supporting claims, comparison to reduce decision friction, cross-sell at the right moment, FAQ after the evidence.
Prefer a conversion-focused product page over a purely beautiful one: clear product information, visible social proof, easy product selection, strong information hierarchy and benefit-driven content.
dont: Weak product info, missing social proof, limited purchase guidance, poor hierarchy, decorative imagery without benefits

rule: Design OTP verification as separate digit boxes with the focused box highlighted, a visible expiry countdown, a resend link and one full-width primary button.
do: 4 digit boxes, 'Code expires in 02:45', 'Didn't receive the code? Resend', 'Continue' button
values: 4-digit code

rule: Simplify cluttered app screens: fewer competing banners and cards, clear visual hierarchy, prominent search and navigation, large imagery and legible typography with ample spacing.
dont: Too many competing banners, text overlaps, hidden navigation/search, too many tiny elements

rule: In a sidebar, show only essential items, make the active state obvious (filled highlight), group items into clear sections, and use one icon style with the same size and colour.
dont: Too many elements, no clear active state, inconsistent icons, weak visual structure

rule: Use real-app screen libraries for mobile UI research: Appshots, Screensdesign, Refero (iOS screens/flows), Pageflows (user journeys), Gummble (onboarding/paywalls), Collectui, Revyl.
Build a liquid-glass pill in Figma from a rounded rectangle with near-transparent fill and a background blur.
do: Fill opacity 1%, background blur 50
values: fill opacity 1%; background blur 50

rule: Stack 3 progressively smaller copies of the glass shape (each 2-5% smaller, smaller ones higher in the layer order) and blur them more the larger they are.
do: Layer/background blur pairs 10/1, 15/5, 20/10
values: 2-5% smaller per copy; blur 10/1, 15/5, 20/10

rule: Give the top glass layer two white inner shadows (one top-left highlight, one opposite) without background blur to fake the refractive edge.
do: Inner shadow X3 Y-2 blur 7 #FFFFFF 50%; inner shadow X-6 Y6 blur 17 #FFFFFF 80%
values: X3 Y-2 B7 S0 FFFFFF 50%; X-6 Y6 B17 S0 FFFFFF 80%

rule: Add a bottom shadow layer to the glass element: a duplicate with a dark inner shadow and heavy layer blur.
do: Layer blur 74; inner shadow X0 Y4 blur 64 spread 12 #000000 25%
values: layer blur 74; X0 Y4 B64 S12 000000 25%

rule: Reduce the number of visible options so users decide faster: group related choices, recommend a default and reveal advanced options later.
dont: A flat list of 8 equal options

rule: Make key actions large and place primary CTAs inside the thumb zone; avoid tiny targets far from the thumb.
do: Full-width Continue button in lower screen area
dont: Small icon button in the top corner for the main action

rule: Break long content into small chunks (overview, key points, examples, takeaway) to reduce memory load.
dont: One long undivided text block

rule: Group form labels with their fields and separate unrelated groups with extra space so layout communicates structure.
do: Separate 'Personal information' and 'Billing address' blocks with clear gaps
dont: Uniform spacing between all fields

rule: Make the one recommended option visually different (colour, badge, size) and keep everything else neutral; if everything stands out, nothing does.
do: Pricing: middle 'Pro' plan with RECOMMENDED badge and filled primary button, others outlined
dont: Equal emphasis on all tiers

rule: Put the most important items and the strongest benefit first and last in a list or flow; do not hide essentials in the middle.
Move complexity from the user to the product: use smart defaults, auto-fill name/email/phone, suggest addresses, save payment, offer one-tap confirm.
Respond instantly to every action: show a loading state (e.g. 'Saving...') immediately, then confirm success ('Saved successfully!'); never leave users guessing.
Design a peak moment (milestone achieved) and a strong ending (clear confirmation and thank-you) because users judge the experience by them.
do: Delightful milestones, clear checkout confirmation, useful empty states after success

rule: Use serif fonts (e.g. Playfair Display) for editorial, luxury-brand and long-read contexts.
values: Playfair Display example

rule: Build a scroll-driven hero animation from an image sequence: generate a reference image, turn it into a short video, trim it, export every frame as images, then have code scrub the frames on scroll.
do: ChatGPT image -> Google Flow video -> InShot/VN edit -> framepeel.com frames zip -> Antigravity/Copilot builds scroll animation

rule: Structure a service page as: menu bar, hero, featured clients, service overview, selected work, work process, more proof, team introduction, relevant testimonial, FAQ, final CTA.
dont: Burying the service under long copy with unclear value

rule: Present a dashboard redesign as a split before/after view on the same screen to make the improvement obvious.
Audit typography, spacing, scale, alignment and CTA prominence so users know what to look at first; make the important things look important.
do: Large serif headline with an italic accent line, one dark filled 'Get Started' CTA, a proof row (50+ projects, 3x faster, 100% satisfaction)
dont: Same-size grey heading, two equal grey buttons and a placeholder image

rule: Remove generic gradients, excessive cards, pills and predictable layouts; build a distinctive visual system instead.
dont: 'All your business tools in one place' hero with three icon feature cards and pill badges

rule: Make the hero explain what it is, who it is for, why it matters and what to do next above the fold, and pass a 5-second test.
values: 5 sec test

rule: Review the running site, find the 10 highest-impact design problems, fix them and review again; ask what to remove rather than what to add.
do: Build -> review -> refine loop

rule: Design the mobile version first: single column, larger tap targets, readable type and one clear CTA; test at 375px width.
values: 375px test width
dont: Desktop layout squeezed onto a phone

rule: Use section-specific inspiration galleries when designing navbars, footers, CTAs and landing pages.

rule: Choose a bottom tab bar variant that fits the app: icon fill for active state, mini player docked above tabs, split dock, search that morphs from the bar, long-press menu, swipe tabs, liquid indicator, or a 'More' sheet for overflow.

rule: Pick the pagination pattern by content: dots or pill for short carousels, a counter with arrow for galleries, stories bars for full-screen sequences, load-more or infinite scroll for feeds, page numbers for search results, thumbnails for image galleries.
values: 8 styles: dots, pill, counter, stories, load more, infinite, page numbers, thumbnails

rule: Apply 60-30-10: a light neutral as the dominant background, a mid-tone secondary and a vivid accent only for the primary CTA and selected chips.
do: Lavender #E6E6FA 60%, Slate Blue #6A5ACD 30%, Chartreuse #7FFF00 10% (Add to order button, selected chip)

rule: Pick a named text-reveal animation for headlines instead of a generic fade.
do: Typewriter, mask rise, scramble decode, gradient flow, word stagger, blur in, letter bounce

rule: Use a branded loader animation (dot ring, triple arc, Newton's cradle) for page or content loading on expressive sites.
Use scroll effects such as layered parallax, pinned heading, 3D card zoom and line-by-line text reveal for immersive pages.

rule: Give the coding agent design skills that set a direction and audit for AI slop before and after it builds UI.
do: Frontend Design (github.com/anthropics/skills), Impeccable (impeccable.style), Taste Skill (tasteskill.dev), Hallmark (usehallmark.com), UI UX Pro Max (uupm.cc), Hue (hueapp.io), Stitch DESIGN.md (stitch.withgoogle.com), shadcn/ui skill (ui.shadcn.com/docs/skills), Interface Design (interface-design.dev), jakub.kr/skills

rule: Pick a clear aesthetic direction before writing any UI code, and record design decisions in a design-system file so they are applied consistently.
do: Save decisions to .interface-design/system.md and state choices before each component

rule: Set type scale, line height, measure and font loading per text role rather than ad hoc.
Start immersive sites from a proven reference prompt (single self-contained index.html reproducing a layout, motion and interactions), then swap copy, brand, sections and motion to make it unique.
do: getlayers.ai/layer/auralis, /brewns, /codescan, /dantora, /evolve

rule: Use skeleton loaders instead of spinners and optimistic updates (UI changes before the server answers) in app UIs.
Add a command menu (cmd+K) and keyboard shortcuts to productivity apps.
Use a cinematic website template prompt (every section, value and scroll timing written down) as a starting point, then swap brand and copy.
do: scrolltide.co/templates/eagle, /pouterby, /cortex, /valmora, /vesper

rule: Lead a dashboard with the one number users open the app for, shown large with context, instead of a row of equal KPI boxes.
do: '$1,284 left of $3,200 · 12 days to go' as a big hero number with a segmented progress bar
dont: Income/Expenses/Savings/Balance in four equal small boxes with the key number last
values: caption: key number at 10 px in the last of four equal boxes (before)

rule: Replace a many-slice pie chart with per-category progress bars showing spent vs limit.
do: Food $412 of $600, Rent $1,100 of $1,100, Fun $186 of $300 as coloured bars
dont: Pie chart with 8+ thin slices and a legend table

rule: On mobile, render transactions as a list with avatar initial, merchant, category subline and right-aligned signed amount (income in green) instead of a dense table.
dont: 5-column table (date, merchant, category, method, amount) on a phone

rule: Simplify the mobile app header to brand, a large period selector and one or two actions (notification, add).
dont: Hamburger + brand + 'Dashboard' label + date dropdown + download + bell all in one row

rule: Show the price format users decide on; for multi-day bookings show the total with its duration rather than only a per-day rate (A/B comparison shown).
do: '$448 · 7 days total' vs '$64 per day'

rule: In profile/dating cards, lead with a large photo and a personal prompt in readable serif type, moving stats into a compact icon row.
dont: Small photo with a dense grid of attribute chips and tags

rule: Simplify a music player: large artwork, title/artist left-aligned with a like action, one progress bar and core controls; drop secondary buttons rows.
For a premium dark fintech/dashboard look, use a near-black green-tinted background with one luminous mint-green accent for charts, active icons and key figures.

do: $198,400 with .00 dimmed

rule: Show multiple payment cards as a layered stack peeking above a balance pocket, with the available balance and quick-action icon buttons below.
values: 3 quick actions

rule: In dashboards, present AI insights as cards with a small coloured tag (Anomaly, Prediction, Opportunity), a timestamp, a one-line explanation and a single action button.
do: Tag Anomaly + "Operating expenses +18% above normal" + "Review expenses"

rule: Lay out KPI cards in a 2-column grid: label, big number, and a small coloured delta line (green up, red down) with the period.
do: Followers 48.2k / +2.4% this week; Impressions 34.8k / -1.2% this week

rule: Use a floating rounded bottom tab bar with icon-only tabs and a separate circular + button for the primary create action.
Open a home screen with a greeting plus a 3-figure stat strip (count + label) summarising today before the content lists.
do: 3 clients / 2 due today / 5 in queue

rule: When an assistant answers from user data, give a direct verdict, the reason with numbers, a mini chart and one concrete action chip.
do: "Not quite. You missed your target on 4 of the last 6 days..." + chip "Add eggs to breakfast"

rule: Choose the sidebar type by context: overlay drawer for simple mobile apps, push drawer when the page should stay visible, reveal menu for a premium feel.

rule: Pick a mobile pagination pattern that fits the content: dots, pill or counter for carousels, stories for immersive media, load-more or infinite scroll for feeds, page numbers for results, thumbnails for galleries.
values: 8 styles: Dots, Pill, Counter, Stories, Load more, Infinite, Page numbers, Thumbnails

rule: Apply 60-30-10: a pale neutral background 60%, a mid-tone brand colour 30%, and a vivid contrasting accent 10% reserved for CTAs, active chips and highlights.
do: Lavender #E6E6FA 60%, Slate Blue #6A5ACD 30%, Chartreuse #7FFF00 10% (Add to order button)

rule: Choose mobile navigation from the standard set (tab bar, drawer, floating pill, top tabs, bottom sheet, speed dial, full-screen menu, command search) to match the number and frequency of destinations.
values: 8 patterns

rule: Match the notification to its weight: toast for quick confirmations, inline alert for contextual issues, badge for counts, dialog only for blocking decisions, progress toast for running tasks.
dont: Interrupting with a dialog for minor info
values: 8 types: Toast, Push banner, Live pill, Badge, Inline alert, Dialog, Stacked, Progress toast

rule: Pick the loader by wait type: spinner for short waits, progress bar or ring when progress is known, skeleton screen for content, shimmer for AI generation, pull-to-refresh for feeds.
values: 8 styles: Spinner, Typing dots, Progress bar, Skeleton, AI shimmer, Progress ring, Pull to refresh, Shape morph

rule: Design onboarding to reach the first win fast: carousel to sell value, coach marks to point at UI, checklist for setup, permission priming before system prompts, interest picker, helpful empty states or a setup wizard.
values: 8 patterns

rule: Make a UI memorable with a single unexpected accent colour used sparingly against an otherwise restrained palette.
Before designing a page, define who it is for, what you want them to do, and why they are not buying yet, then write the page to answer that.
On profile screens let the photo be large and pair it with one personal prompt in expressive type instead of a dense grid of attribute chips.
dont: Small photo with tiny text and many tag chips

rule: When users pick a near-term date, show a horizontal week strip (day + date) with a See Month link instead of a full month calendar.
do: November / Mon 9 ... Sun 15, selected day as a filled tile
dont: Full month grid filling the middle of the screen

rule: Group time slots under Morning and Afternoon, use short labels, strike through unavailable slots and fill the selected one.
do: 9:30 / 10:00 struck through / 10:30 selected
dont: Uniform grid of 16 "9:00 AM"-style buttons

rule: Replace stacked Confirm, Add to calendar and Cancel buttons with one summary row (price + details) and a single primary button that names the action and the choice.
do: "$50 visit" + "Book 10:30 AM"
dont: Three full-width buttons of similar weight

rule: Use ready animation libraries for smooth, springy motion: Motion, Anime.js, Motion Primitives, React Bits.
For content apps, put a prominent filled circular Create (+) button in the bottom nav, visually distinct from the other tabs.
do: Home, My Network, (+), Notifications, Jobs

rule: Use a pill-shaped bottom nav where only the active tab shows its label inside a filled pill and the others are icon-only.
do: Home pill + icons + separate black (+) circle

rule: In AI-centric apps, make the AI action the centre item of a short pill nav, highlighted with a glowing gradient pill.
do: Home / sparkle (gradient) / Search

rule: Give AI builders quality component libraries instead of designing from scratch: Bencho (micro-interactions), BoardUI (dashboards, agent tools), Transitions.dev (UI state transitions), Beautiful UI (agent workflows); Mobbin for real app references.
Make nested rounded corners concentric: inner radius = outer radius minus the padding between them.
dont: Same radius on inner and outer elements
values: inner = outer - padding

rule: Use semi-transparent borders instead of solid hex so they blend into any background.
dont: Solid grey hex borders

rule: Build colour palettes in OKLCH.
For editorial event sites, use a three-colour palette: a very dark brand tone, a warm off-white, and one saturated accent that matches the hero image.
do: Petrol Blue #002D37 / Ivory #FEF0DD / Saffron Gold #F7A724; Deep Teal #012A23 / Bone #F9EFDB / Magenta #C12589

rule: Pair a full-bleed hero illustration with oversized condensed italic serif headline words split across opposite corners, a small-caps nav and a circular-arrow Book tickets link.
do: "RIBBON ... FINALS", "FLAMENCO ... NIGHTS"

rule: Order landing page sections to build trust within the first five seconds; section sequence matters as much as visual polish.
values: first five seconds

rule: Replace indeterminate spinners on long tasks with honest progress showing percent, time left and speed so users can decide to wait or walk away.
do: 71% bar + '5s left' + '1.9 MB/s' on a file upload
dont: A spinner with 'Uploading...' and no progress or time estimate

rule: Use curated galleries for UI inspiration: Behance, Dribbble, Awwwards, SiteInspire, Land-book, Mobbin, UI Movement, Godly, Collect UI, Lapa Ninja.
Build a warm monochrome palette as a 6-step tonal ramp of one brown hue from near-black to cream.
Structure a SaaS landing page as navbar, hero, product video, social proof, benefits, how it works, testimonials, FAQs, final CTA, footer.
do: Hero headline + phone mockup; logo strip under hero; final CTA block with phone mockup above footer

rule: Keep the navbar to the main links only plus a sticky CTA button.
Make the hero heading state your USP and what you sell in benefit-driven language, with a subheading that explains the claim with product features and one CTA for the next step.
dont: Vague, clever words in the headline

rule: Place a short product video under the hero that explains how the product works.
values: 2-3 minutes max

rule: Write the benefits section around outcomes, not features: features tell, but benefits sell.
Break the product's functionality into a short numbered 'How it works' section.
values: 3-5 easy steps

rule: Back claims with case studies, prestigious company logos, verified badges and testimonials with name, position and company.
End with an accordion FAQ of simple answers, a high-contrast action-oriented CTA band, and a footer with logo, copyright, privacy policy, contact info, social icons and email sign-up.
Choose the mobile menu pattern deliberately from the standard set: grid/card, side drawer, tab bar, FAB, bottom sheet, three-dot overflow, rectangular side rail, or rudder (floating centered bar).
Reduce decision time by cutting unnecessary options, grouping related choices, recommending a default and revealing advanced options later.
do: 3 focused choices with one marked 'Best for you / Recommended'

rule: Make key actions large enough, place CTAs within the thumb zone, separate important actions clearly and avoid tiny hard-to-hit targets.

rule: Break content into smaller chunks, group related information and use short sections and steps to reduce memory load.
do: Overview / Key points / Examples / Takeaway blocks

rule: Offer recent or saved entries (e.g. recent locations) as one-tap options above manual input to save users time.

rule: For calm, trustworthy fintech UI limit colour to one navy plus two accents; build hierarchy from size and weight, and reserve red/green only for trend direction.
dont: Using colour to separate features

rule: On immersive product sites let users interact with the product before buying (e.g. click a seat to see the view, try an item on the product, scroll-driven scene changes).

Review the running site to find the highest-impact design problems and what should be removed, fix them, then reopen and review again (build, review, refine).

rule: Design the mobile version first with a single column, larger tap targets, readable type and one clear CTA, and test at 375px width.

rule: On a mobile profile, lead with a large photo and one personal statement in readable type, moving stat chips into a compact row below, instead of a dense grid of data tags.
