rule: For a scroll-animation website, generate a reference image in ChatGPT, derive a prompt from it and turn that exact image into a short video to scrub on scroll.
In fintech UIs use a rounded, geometric sans (e.g. Helvetica Neue) for headlines and balance figures so large numbers feel approachable, limited to four weights.
values: Regular, Medium, SemiBold, Bold

rule: Define a fixed type scale from headline to caption and use only those sizes.
Make every padding, gap and margin a multiple of one 4px base unit, picked from a fixed spacing scale.
Use soft corners and soft shadows with named radius and shadow tokens; avoid hard 90-degree corners anywhere in the product.
values: radius xs 8px, md 16px, lg 24px, full pill; shadows sm, md, lg
dont: Hard 90Â° corners

rule: Use real-app screen libraries for mobile flows, states, onboarding and paywall patterns.
do: Appshots, Screensdesign, Refero, Pageflows, Gummble, Collectui, Revyl

rule: Build the home page around: clear brand positioning, primary CTA above the fold, social proof, case studies with results, a conversation path and a lead magnet / free resource.

Build each service page around: service-specific value proposition, clear service expectations, concrete deliverables, process transparency, results and proof, clear differentiator, objection handling (FAQ).
Give a floating mobile tab bar a translucent blurred background so content scrolls visibly beneath it while icons stay legible.
dont: Opaque or no-backdrop tab bar clashing with content

rule: Make the close button on modals and paywalls clearly visible with a contrasting circular background.
dont: Faint, low-contrast X hidden in the corner

rule: Confirm a completed action by turning the button into a coloured success state with a checkmark and a small celebratory burst.
dont: Grey button with no feedback after submit

rule: Morph a copy icon into a checkmark (with accent colour) after copying so users know it worked.
Animate the selected rating star with a scale pop and sparkle, filling stars in accent colour up to the selection.
Have a FAB expand its secondary actions out of the button itself and turn its + into an X to close.
dont: Actions stacked statically above a grey + button

rule: Use section-specific inspiration galleries (navbars, footers, CTAs, landing pages, mobile animations) before designing a section.
do: scrolltide.co, navbar.gallery, footer.design, cta.gallery, minimal.gallery, 60fps.design, collectui.com, posts.design, landdding.com

rule: Build product pages on a 60-30-10 palette: 60% warm neutral main, 30% deep secondary, 10% loud accent reserved for what users click and key highlights.
values: Mascarpone Cream 60% / Highland Green 30% / San Marzano 10% #EF4229 (RGB 239,66,41); Crema Ivory 60% / Pine Velvet 30% / Coral Rocket 10% #FF5A4A (RGB 255,90,74); Biscotti Cream 60% / Graphite Enamel 30% / Tangerine Laser 10% #FF6A14 (RGB 255,106,20)

rule: Use the 10% accent only on the buy button, active indicators and a highlighted headline word; keep everything else in the main and secondary colours.
do: 'What's inside.' with only 'inside.' in accent; orange 'Buy now' and active dot

rule: Show a physical product as an exploded 3D view with labelled callouts (part name + one-line benefit) linked by thin leader lines.
Give coding agents design skills that fix generic AI UI: brand design-language, token extraction, component, dashboard-hierarchy and typography (scale, line height, measure, font loading) skills.
do: Hue (hueapp.io), Extract DESIGN.md (Google Stitch), shadcn/ui skill, interface-design.dev, jakub.kr/skills (Better Typography)

rule: Bookmark design-skill repos for AI-built interfaces, e.g. Emil Kowalski's skills for refining motion and interaction details.
do: UI UX Pro Max, Impeccable, github.com/emilkowalski/skills

rule: Lead a budget/finance app home screen with the one number users open it for, large at the top with its context, followed by a segmented bar breakdown, per-category progress bars and recent transactions.
do: '$1,284' + 'left of $3,200 Â· 12 days to go'; stacked category bar with legend; budget bars 'Food $412 of $600'
dont: Pie chart and four equal stat boxes with the key number at 10 px in the last box

rule: When building UI with an AI coding agent's frontend-design skill, give it a brief and one clear visual direction before it writes code.
do: github.com/anthropics/skills (Frontend Design)

rule: For a premium liquid-glass look, make glass surfaces refract the backdrop (bend light, chromatic dispersion, crisp edges) rather than only applying a flat CSS backdrop blur, and place them over a rich, colourful background.
values: IOR 1.50; refraction Snell 3D; dispersion RGB prism; bundle 16 KB

rule: When a card opens a detail page, morph the card into the page (shared-element transition) and reverse it on back, so nothing just appears without an origin.
dont: Hard cut that makes users find their place again

rule: Give instant visual feedback on press for slow actions (e.g. payment); identical load times feel faster when the UI responds immediately.
values: button takes 2.0 s; 'one second too long'

rule: Show a visible indicator as soon as the user pulls to refresh so they know something is happening.
Animate a like (fill, scale, ripple) instead of swapping the heart state in a single frame.
dont: Heart that 'swaps in 1 frame'

rule: Never answer a search with a bare 'No results'; handle typos and offer suggestions or a next step.
dont: Query 'hedphones' -> 'No results'

rule: Build a liquid-glass shape in Figma from a stack of 4 copies of the same rounded rectangle, each 2-5% smaller than the previous, with smaller copies placed higher in the layer group.
values: each copy 2-5% smaller

rule: Apply layer blur plus background blur to the stacked glass copies, stronger on larger shapes.
values: layer/background blur 10/1, 15/5, 20/10

rule: Add a top glass layer (copy of the largest shape, no background blur) with two white inner shadows to create the bright refractive edge.
values: inner shadow 1: X 3, Y -2, blur 7, spread 0, #FFFFFF 50%; inner shadow 2: X -6, Y 6, blur 17, spread 0, #FFFFFF 80%

rule: Add a bottom shadow layer (copy of the largest shape) with a heavy layer blur and a dark inner shadow to ground the glass element.
values: layer blur 74; inner shadow X 0, Y 4, blur 64, spread 12, #000000 25%

rule: Structure a SaaS landing page as: sticky navbar with logo, hero with clear next-step CTA and product preview, client logos, benefit-led features, how it works, 3 pricing plans, testimonials, short FAQ, problem-stating CTA block, footer with logo and newsletter.
Offer 3 pricing plans and visually spotlight the middle one to guide the choice.
values: 3 plans

rule: Write the final CTA headline so it states clearly what problem the product solves.
Keep the landing-page navbar sticky so navigation and the primary CTA stay visible while scrolling.
Use client logos near the hero and natural-sounding real testimonials further down to build trust.
dont: Overpolished, fake-sounding testimonials

rule: Design a home page for exploration (navigation to sub-pages, several CTAs, overview copy, footer links) and a landing page for a single goal (one Get Started CTA, focused service details, minimal navigation).
Use free asset libraries for illustrations, icons, stock media, animation and 3D instead of making everything from scratch.
do: Illustrations: Storyset, unDraw, DrawKit, ManyPixels, Humaaans, Open Doodles, Blush; Icons: Phosphor, Heroicons, Feather, Remix, Lucide, Iconoir; Stock: Pexels, Unsplash, Pixabay, Mixkit, Coverr; Motion: LottieFiles, Rive, Jitter, Animista, Loading.io; 3D: Spline, Blender, Sketchfab, Vectary, Poly Pizza

rule: Use optimistic UI: update the interface instantly on tap and save in the background instead of waiting for the server.
do: setLiked(); save()
dont: await save(); setLiked()
values: waits for server 730 ms vs optimistic 16 ms

rule: Use one consistent media aspect ratio across cards in a row so the rows line up.
dont: Mixing 1:1, 16:9 and 4:3 cards in the same grid
values: 1:1, 16:9, 4:3 (mixed = wrong)

rule: For a scroll-driven product animation, generate a video from a product image (e.g. Google Flow), trim it (InShot/VN), export it to an image sequence (FramePeel) and have the coding agent bind the frames to scroll.

Give AI coding agents design guidance repos: UI UX Pro Max (styles, palettes, typography for planning), Impeccable (critique/audit/polish an existing screen), Oil UI (explore and compare directions), Awesome DESIGN.md (analysed site styles/tokens as a starting reference), Mobbin (real app references).
Avoid the typical AI-generated UI tells: small uppercase 'kicker' labels above every heading, italic serif accent words in headlines, colored side-tab borders on cards and default beige backgrounds.
dont: AI kicker, Italic serif, Side-tab border, AI beige

rule: On a booking screen show a horizontal week strip instead of a full month calendar, group time slots by Morning/Afternoon, strike through unavailable slots and keep a 'See Month' link for longer ranges.
dont: Full month grid plus a dense grid of all slots

rule: End a booking flow with one sticky bottom bar holding the price and a single primary button that states the chosen action, instead of stacked Confirm/Add to calendar/Cancel buttons.
do: '$50 visit' + 'Book 10:30 AM'
dont: CONFIRM BOOKING + ADD TO CALENDAR + CANCEL stacked

rule: Cut profile/list cards down to the few facts users decide on, with a larger photo and clear name hierarchy.
do: 'Cardiologist Â· 15 years' / '4.9 (312) Â· $50 visit'
dont: 'MBBS, MD, FACC, Cardiology, 15 yrs exp, City Heart Hospital, Downtown' in one small line

rule: In player screens keep only the core controls prominent (large play/pause, prev/next, shuffle/repeat) and move secondary actions (EQ, lyrics, share, download, queue) out of the main view.
Give every icon-only button an accessible label.
Keep a visible keyboard focus ring on interactive elements; never remove it without a replacement.
Respect the user's reduced-motion setting for drawers, transitions and other animations.

Use agent design skills by stage: Taste Skill for art direction of a new site, UI/UX Pro Max for planning styles/palettes/font pairings, Impeccable to critique and polish an existing UI, Vercel Web Design Guidelines to audit accessibility/usability before handoff.
Use a floating rounded bottom tab bar with 4-5 icon destinations, a clearly highlighted active item with its label, and numeric badges for unread counts.
De-slop a dashboard: drop dark purple gradients, glowing stat cards and generic 'Welcome back' banners; use a real type scale, one card style, and grouped hierarchy with primary actions at the top.
dont: Dark purple gradients, glowing stat cards, 'Welcome back' banner

rule: Prompt the AI explicitly for button styling details (e.g. remove default box-shadow, clear primary vs secondary pair such as filled 'Get started' next to outlined 'Log in').
values: box-shadow: none

rule: Fix a generic-looking site with four basics: one headline per view (cut noise), generous spacing, everything aligned to one edge, and one primary button instead of many.
dont: Eight competing buttons

rule: For admin dashboards avoid purple gradients, use real icons, a clear hierarchy, soft shadows and copy that says something specific.

Pick a bottom tab bar pattern to fit the app: icon fill for the active tab, mini player above tabs, split dock, search that morphs from the bar, long-press menus, swipe tabs, liquid style, or a 'More' sheet for overflow destinations.
values: 8 styles: icon fill, mini player, split dock, search morph, long press, swipe tabs, liquid, more sheet

rule: Choose mobile pagination by content: dots or pill for short carousels, a counter (3/4) for longer sets, stories for immersive sequences, load more or infinite scroll for feeds, page numbers for search results, thumbnails for galleries.
values: 8 styles: dots, pill, counter, stories, load more, infinite, page numbers, thumbnails

rule: Build a mobile palette as 60% light neutral, 30% secondary and 10% vivid accent reserved for the main CTA and active states.
do: Lavender #E6E6FA 60%, Slate Blue #6A5ACD 30%, Chartreuse #7FFF00 10% (Add to order button)

rule: Match screen transitions to navigation meaning: slide for drilling into content, shared element for continuity between a card and its detail, modal sheet for temporary tasks; other options are fade, zoom, flip, circle reveal and card stack.

Treat the button style as the tone-setter of the interface and choose one treatment deliberately (glassmorphism, liquid glass, neumorphism, neo-brutalism, aurora glow, claymorphism, tactile 3D, morphing).
Make button horizontal padding optically equal to vertical padding by compensating for line-height vs cap height.
do: font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; --py: 0.5em; --px: calc(var(--py) + (1lh - 1cap) / 2); padding: var(--py) var(--px);
values: visible 14 = 14

rule: Do not place the sidebar collapse/resize handle where it blends with the scrollbar; give it a distinct position and appearance, and keep it from jumping when the sidebar toggles.
dont: Handle visually merging with the scrollbar

rule: When tabs overflow, add previous/next arrow buttons at the edges and scroll the active tab fully into view.
Keep the gap between an avatar/icon and its text consistent with the padding around the icon instead of squeezing it.
do: 11.2 padding around icon and matching gap
dont: 11.2 outer padding with a 6 gap to the text

rule: Use an 8-point grid for component sizes and for both vertical and horizontal alignment.
values: 8pt

rule: Keep the column count even (12, 8 or 4) and define columns in percentages so content adapts to any screen.
values: 12, 8 or 4 columns

rule: Keep gutter width fixed while column width flexes; on an 8pt system use a 32px gutter (16px each side).
values: 32px gutter (16px each side); libraries typically 30px

rule: Align text to a 4pt baseline for vertical rhythm; text centred inside a button or list row does not need to sit on the baseline.
values: 4pt baseline
do: label-to-field gap 4

rule: Establish consistent keylines across screens as a simpler alternative to nesting columns.
Make all spacing, margins and element dimensions multiples of 8; drop to 4pt increments when more precision is needed.
values: 8-64px in steps of 8; 4pt half-step

rule: Use a 5px grid when working with fixed Bootstrap column layouts that need compact spacing; use 8px for fluid layouts that benefit from more breathing room.
values: 5px vs 8px

rule: Start desktop web designs on a 12-column grid with 100px side margins and 20px gutters in a 1440px frame (about 1240px content width).
values: 12 columns, 100px margins, 20px gutters, 1440px frame, ~1240px content

rule: Use row grids (e.g. 8px height, 8px gutter, 8px offset, high count) for structured vertical layout in complex web and mobile dashboard views.
values: row height 8px, gutter 8px, offset 8px, count 800

rule: For mobile layouts use a 6-column grid with 16 margin and 24 gutter.
values: count 6, margin 16, gutter 24

rule: Space form fields on multiples of 8 (e.g. 16 side padding, 16 between label groups, 24 from header).
do: Edit Profile form: 24 top, 16 sides, 16 between fields

rule: When a device width is not divisible by 8, pick a sensible middle ground rather than forcing the grid.
Present product features as a bento set of soft white cards, each with a small live UI vignette on top and a bold title plus one muted descriptive line below.
Use multiples of 8 (8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56...) for layout, dimensions, padding and margin so designs hand off consistently to development and scale across devices.
Set the desktop layout grid as a 1440px frame, 12 stretch columns, 96 margin and 24 gutter.
values: W 1440, 12 columns, stretch, margin 96, gutter 24

rule: Reserve at least 44px at the top for the iOS status bar and place nothing else in that zone.
values: 44px

rule: Give a mobile navigation bar about 56px height with a 44x44px tap target for the back button and 8px gap to the content below.
values: 56px bar, 44x44 tap target, 8px gap

rule: For a screen title use about 28px font with 8px between title and description, and start the text block about 96px from the top.
values: 28px title, 8px gap, ~80px block, 96px from top

rule: Leave 24px between the heading block and the input; make a full-width mobile input 343x56px, leaving 16px side margins, with 16px to the next element.
values: 24px, 343x56px, 16px margins

rule: Design the 404 page as a full-bleed hero with a big playful headline (e.g. 'Lost Direction?', 'Hmmm... you're lost'), a strong photographic image, a small 'Error 404' label and one clear 'Take me home' button.
Use progressive blur (smooth transition from sharp to blurred) behind overlays to guide attention while keeping text readable.
Use bento grids (lunch-box style tiles of varied size) for responsive feature sections that stay consistent across devices.
Use detailed illustrations or 3D renders to communicate information and brand personality, not just decorate.
Keep layouts minimal: simple structure, limited colour palette, clear typography and strategic whitespace.
Design responsive layouts against standard breakpoints: mobile <=480px and <=768px, tablet <=834px and <=1024px, laptop/desktop <=1440px.
Make every gap an 8pt multiple, use a bigger gap to start a new content chunk, and align edges and text baselines.
do: card: icon, title, body lines, full-width CTA on shared left edge
values: 8pt multiples; 16pt padding; 4pt baseline (caption)

rule: Study design-system references such as designsystems.com (Figma's design systems publication).
Reduce the number of visible choices to speed decisions; show few options as radio buttons instead of hiding them in a dropdown.
do: 4 visible radio options
dont: long select dropdown

rule: Make primary action targets large and close to where the user is working; small targets take longer to hit.
do: large buttons
dont: tiny buttons

rule: Chunk information into small groups because working memory holds about 7 (plus or minus 2) items.
Design a memorable peak and a positive ending (e.g. a celebratory success screen) because users judge an experience by its peak and its end.
do: 'You did it! Congratulations!' completion screen

rule: Pick the grid type for the job: radial grid for a single focal point, modular grid for consistent but flexible tiles, column grid for readable cross-screen layouts, hierarchical grid to steer visual flow, baseline grid for typographic rhythm.
For liquid-glass / glassmorphism components use a translucent surface with background blur, a thin bright inner highlight edge and a soft shadow, and keep radius tokens consistent.
do: Glass blur 24, Highlight 12%, Shadow soft; radius tokens 4/12/16/24/32
values: blur 24, highlight 12%

rule: Build a full glass component set (buttons, inputs, select, toggles, tabs, toasts, modals, cards) from the same glass recipe so the style stays coherent.

Before designing, find why users fail (e.g. interview about 10 users who abandoned checkout), identify the main friction points, wireframe several solutions, test, iterate and measure impact after launch.
do: Interview 10 users, identify 3 friction points, wireframe 5 solutions
dont: Open Figma, design pretty screens, add animations, ship
values: 10 users, 3 friction points, 5 solutions

rule: Ask before, during and after designing: what problem and for whom; can anything be removed without losing value, what will confuse users; how to validate and which metrics prove success.

Build a premium hero with an oversized faded serif wordmark behind a striking subject image, a short two-line headline with a muted second line, a primary pill CTA plus a secondary outline button, and floating frosted stat/feature cards.
do: 'Innovation & security', 'Our Solutions' + 'Contact us', cards with '42%' and avatar stack '+323'

rule: Add social proof near the hero: an overlapping avatar stack with a short 'Trusted by...' line and a large customer count.
do: 'Trusted by organizations around the world' + '1.2k+ Customers'

rule: Use CSS Grid (display: grid) for full-page layouts and complex sections where you need control over both rows and columns.
do: header / sidebar + content / footer

rule: Define equal flexible columns with fr units and space items with gap rather than margins.
do: .container{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr 1fr;gap:20px}
values: gap: 20px; 1fr 1fr 1fr

rule: Let featured items span multiple columns (grid-column: span 2) for hero or featured content inside a grid.
do: .item-large{grid-column:span 2}
values: span 2, span 3

rule: Lay out pages for scanning in predictable F and Z patterns, since people scan rather than read.
Make the page understandable at a glance: users must identify what matters, navigate without friction and recognise the next action instantly.
Use navigation labels people already understand and make every destination easy to predict.
do: Home, About, Work, Contact; dropdown: Our story, Our process, Values, Careers, FAQs
dont: clever or vague labels

rule: Express the hero message in one sentence, not a paragraph; if visitors need to figure it out, they won't.
dont: paragraph-long hero copy

rule: Start a design system with foundations before components: colour palette, typography, spacing, border radius and shadows.
do: 5-colour palette (blue, purple, near-black, light grey, white), Inter type specimen
dont: starting with a button library

rule: Turn foundations into named reusable tokens and reference them everywhere.
do: Primary-Color, Spacing-16, Heading-Lg

rule: Build essential reusable components first (buttons, inputs, cards, navigation) and give each the states default, hover, disabled and error.
do: outline button default -> filled on hover

rule: Document every token, component and state so the design system works as a shared language.

Study public design systems by need: GitHub Primer (tokens, consistency), Salesforce Lightning (dashboards, enterprise density), Microsoft Fluent (cross-platform), GOV.UK (accessibility, content, forms), Adobe Spectrum (complex tools, UI states).
Decide foundations before drawing any screen: colour ramps (primary + neutral, 50-900), a type scale, a 4pt spacing scale, radius and elevation steps.
do: Type scale Display 48 / Heading 32 / Body 16 / Caption 12; spacing 4,8,12,16,24,32,48; radius 4/8/16/full; elevation sm/md/lg
values: type 12-16-32-48; spacing 4-48; radius 4, 8, 16, full

rule: Stick to a 4pt grid: if a spacing number is not divisible by 4, it does not ship.
values: divisible by 4

rule: Use three token layers: primitive (raw value, e.g. orange/500 = #FF5B23), semantic (meaning, e.g. color/action/primary) and component (where it lives, e.g. button/bg/default), so a rebrand swaps one primitive and dark mode remaps only the semantic layer.
do: Figma variables: 2 collections, Primitives and Semantic with Light + Dark modes

rule: Specify the primary button with tokens: about 48 height, 24 horizontal padding, 12 radius, 8 gap to a 22 icon, semibold label; use only auto layout and tokens, no raw hex inside components.
do: fill color/action/primary, text color/text/on-action, radius radius/md, label body/semibold
dont: raw hex values inside components
values: height 48, padding 24, radius 12, gap 8, icon 22

rule: Start with the 5 components used on every screen (button, input, card, avatar, navigation), not 50.

Give every component all its states and sizes: primary/secondary/ghost buttons in default, hover, pressed, focus and disabled; inputs in default, focus and error with helper text; sizes sm/md/lg; name variants like Button · Type=Primary · Size=MD · State=Hover.
do: Error input: red border + 'Enter a valid email'

rule: Use one primary button per view; pair it with a secondary, never two primaries fighting for attention.
do: Cancel (secondary) + Save (primary)
dont: Save + Publish both primary

rule: Meet accessibility minimums per component: text contrast at least 4.5:1, a 2px focus ring, tap targets at least 44px.
values: contrast >= 4.5:1, focus ring 2px, tap target >= 44px

rule: Document each component on one page: when to use, do/don't, properties (type, size, state) and accessibility, with version and owner.
Use 8pt as the main system and 4pt for tiny adjustments, composing values like 12 = 8 + 4 and 20 = 16 + 4.
Space a simple product card with 16px padding, 8px title-to-body, 24px section gap and 32px outer margin.
do: card: image, title, subtitle, description, full-width 'Add to Cart' button

rule: Avoid random spacing values (10, 14, 23, 31) and inconsistent card padding; use one scale such as 4/8/16/24/32/48.
do: consistent 16px padding on all cards
dont: mixing 10, 14, 23, 31 for no reason

rule: Study public design systems (Uber Base, Pinterest Gestalt, Microsoft Fluent 2, Adobe Spectrum, Salesforce Lightning, Wise, Vercel) and compare how each handles the same component.
do: open one component (button, card, toast) in all of them

rule: Choose among radial (focal point), modular (consistent tiles with freedom), axial (structure along one clear axis), column (readability across screens) and hierarchical (guided visual flow) grids according to the layout's goal.

When generating a design system with an AI tool, feed it real references (brand assets, screenshots, documents, typography, colours, logos), review the generated colours, typography, components and layouts for inconsistencies, then test it by generating a real landing page or dashboard.
Use 8-multiples for component dimensions too: icons 16/24/32px, buttons 40/48px high, inputs 48/56px high, avatars 32/40/48px, card padding 16/24px.
values: icons 16/24/32; buttons 40/48; inputs 48/56; avatars 32/40/48; card padding 16/24

rule: Use a 48px touch target as a default for touch interfaces, checking the exact platform minimum.
values: 48px

rule: Treat the 8pt grid as a guideline: allow 4px between icons and labels, font sizes like 14/18/20px, 1-2px borders and fluid responsive widths that do not follow multiples of 8.
dont: forcing every measurement onto 8
values: 4px, 14/18/20px type, 1px/2px borders, width 100%

rule: In Figma define a spacing scale (4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64), apply it through auto layout padding/gaps and spacing variables (spacing/8, spacing/16, spacing/24), keep smaller gaps within groups and larger between sections, then review the full screen.
do: auto layout item spacing 16, padding 24
dont: manual positioning

rule: Use 8, 16, 24 and 32px for common layout spacing and 4px for finer adjustments; group related elements with smaller gaps.
Use one consistent stroke weight across all icons; avoid mixing too-thin and too-heavy icons in the same interface.
dont: mixing stroke weights

rule: Adjust icons for optical size: a circle, square and triangle on the same canvas look different in size, so scale shapes until they look equal.
Keep corner style consistent across icons; don't mix sharp and rounded corners from different sets.
Mix filled and outlined icons only under a clear rule, e.g. filled for the active tab and outlined for inactive tabs.
do: bottom nav: Home filled (active), Map/Saved/Insights outlined
dont: filled icons scattered randomly among outlined ones

rule: Align icons optically, not just by bounding box: nudge asymmetric glyphs (play triangle, bell) so they look centred.
Animated copy-paste component libraries: React Bits, Aceternity UI, Skiper UI, Magic UI, Animate UI, UI Layouts (ui-layouts.com), Kokonut UI (kokonutui.com, React + Tailwind + Motion, shadcn-ready).
Use monospace micro-labels and (001) numbering only where they carry information (time, index, coordinates, a real sequence); otherwise they read as template chrome.
dont: mono labels and numbering as decoration on every element

rule: Don't fade-in every section on scroll; reserve one orchestrated motion moment and trigger other motion on user action.
dont: scroll fade-ins on everything

rule: Use bento feature grids deliberately: modular card grids for long feature lists are now the SaaS default and edging into cliché, so vary them to avoid a template look.
Animated UI component sources: originkit.dev, uselayouts.com, evilbuttons.com (animated buttons), podie.dev, kokonutui.com (animated React components).
Design inspiration sources: Mobbin (real shipped iOS/web app screens and flows), are.na/fi 'cool websites' channel; caption also lists Inspora, Refero, Land-book, Godly, Minimal Gallery, Siteinspire.
Use 8pt increments for padding inside components so spacing stays consistent with the grid.
values: 8pt padding

rule: Make the heights of vertically stacked components multiples of 8pt as well, not just their padding.
Size component widths as a count of grid increments times the increment.
do: A card 24 increments of 16px = 384px wide

rule: Design desktop websites on a 1440px frame with side margins of at least 5% (typically 100px) and add padding inside the main container.
values: 1440px frame, 100px margins, 1240px safe area, 20px inner padding

rule: Start mobile app design on the smallest iPhone frame with at least 16px side margins, 8px gutters and a 4, 5 or 6 column grid.
values: 375px frame, 16+px margins, 8px gutter, 335+px content width

rule: Use vertical columns for horizontal placement and 4-8px spacing increments (soft grid) for vertical spacing instead of strict baseline grids.
values: 4-8px increments

rule: Build feature cards as a small illustrative UI vignette on top with a bold title and one-line muted description below, inside a rounded light card.
do: Keyboard-shortcut keys or a collaborative cursor mock as the visual

rule: Start button padding from 8px multiples and a 48px height, then adjust by eye.
values: 8px padding, 48px height

rule: Space adjacent buttons 12-48px apart, using more space for small buttons and less for large ones.
values: small ~42px buttons: 36-48px gap; medium ~60px: 25-36px; large ~72px: 15-24px

rule: Apply the 8pt rule to the type scale to get consistent vertical rhythm.
Set up the mobile layout grid as 2 stretch columns with 16px margin and 16px gutter on a 320px frame.
values: Frame W 320, Count 2, Type Stretch, Width Auto, Margin 16, Gutter 16

rule: Keep helper/acceptance text close to the button it belongs to so the relation is clear, and leave space above the keyboard.
values: 24px text-to-button, 16px button-to-keyboard, 56px button height, 343px button width on 375px frame, 80px gap above

rule: When designing iOS screens with a keyboard, resize the frame to fit it and leave about 34px for the home indicator.
values: 34px home indicator, 375px frame

rule: Learn spacing by replicating existing app screens and noting every spacing value.
Choose a 5px grid for compact fixed-column layouts and an 8px grid for fluid layouts that need more breathing room.
For fixed desktop grids use 12 columns of 65-80px with 15-30px gutters, giving about a 1100px box on a 1440px frame.
values: 12 columns, 65-80px columns, 15-30px gutters, 1100px box width, 1440px frame

rule: For fluid desktop grids use a 1440px frame, 96px side margins and a 12-column grid with 24px gutters.
values: 1440px frame, 96px margins, 1248px safe area, 12 columns, 24px gutters

rule: Skip row/baseline grids; fit elements into vertical columns and space them in consistent 8px or 5px increments.
Use glowing borders or light-ray gradients to add depth and draw attention to key elements such as the hero.
Inline emojis within paragraphs to add personality to body copy.
Make oversized bold headline typography the main visual element of the page when you want character and emotion.
Add interactive or 3D objects to the hero to break flat design and make the page feel alive.
Use scroll-driven animation and dynamic content to tell a story section by section.
Replace inconsistent arbitrary gaps (12, 27, 9px) with 8-pixel steps for all paddings and margins so hierarchy reads clearly.
dont: 12px / 27px / 9px gaps in one card

rule: Wrap card-like components in 16px inner padding.
values: 16px padding

rule: Put the title and subtitle 8px apart and the subtitle and CTA 16px apart, so related text groups tighter than the action.
values: title-subtitle 8px, subtitle-CTA 16px

rule: Lock text baselines and font sizes to 4pt increments for a crisp vertical rhythm.
values: title 20px, body 16px
do: Title 20 px, body 16 px

rule: Lay out a mobile dashboard on a 4-column stretch grid with 20px margins and 20px gutters on a 390px frame.
values: 390x844px frame, 4 columns, margin 20, gutter 20; header 60px, carousel 150px, chips 36px, device cards 200px

rule: Use soft ambient image-gradient backgrounds and a gradient-accented bottom navigation with a raised central action for a calm, premium smart-home style app.

Structure a sidebar top to bottom as: brand logo with collapse toggle, search, grouped main navigation with labelled sections, a CTA/upgrade card, settings and help, and the workspace/user block at the bottom.
do: Show active-item highlight, hover state, status badges/counters and dividers

rule: Size an expanded sidebar at 240px and the collapsed icon rail at 80px, with 40px nav items separated by 4px and section groups separated by 16-24px.
values: expanded 240px, collapsed 80px, item height 40px, 4px between items, 16px section label, 24px between groups, 44px top/bottom padding, 48px around CTA card

rule: In the collapsed icon-only sidebar, show the item label in a tooltip on hover.
Show inner pages as one expandable secondary level under a primary item, using leading lines to show hierarchy, and never nest deeper.
dont: Third-level nested navigation in the sidebar

rule: Use the bottom of the sidebar for a call-to-action card such as upgrade plan, usage meter or join waitlist.
Use place-items (shorthand for align-items + justify-items) to align content inside CSS grid cells on both axes in one line.
do: display:grid; place-items:center;

rule: Name page regions with grid-template-areas (header, sidebar, main, ads, footer) so complex layouts are readable and can be reordered without touching the HTML.
values: grid-template-columns: 200px 1fr 200px; grid-template-rows: 80px 1fr 80px

rule: Treat 8px as a base unit for a spacing scale where each step has a job, rather than applying 8px to every gap.
dont: All gaps = 8px: icon padding, section gap and list gaps identical, so there is no hierarchy
values: 4px tight internal gaps; 8px icon-to-label, inset; 12px related items, list rows; 16px card padding; 24px between card groups; 32px section breathing room; 64px page-level sections

rule: Use small gaps for the same idea and larger gaps for a new section, and never use the same spacing for different relationships.
values: gaps scale 4 -> 8 -> 16 -> 32

rule: Optically compensate padding around text and icons when equal pixel values look unbalanced.
do: 14px top / 18px bottom so the content feels centered
dont: 16px on all sides that looks top-heavy
values: 14px/18px vs 16px/16px

rule: Use multiples of 4, with 4px as a half-step for tight elements like icon plus label.
Order website sections to answer visitor questions in sequence: what you do, why trust you, what is in it for me, proof, and what to do next.
values: Confusion anywhere = drop-off everywhere

rule: Build design-system foundations (principles, scales, tokens, rules) before components; components inherit them.
dont: Starting the design system with buttons and cards

rule: Define a few product design principles before creating UI and use them as decision filters in design debates.
do: Clear over clever; accessible by default; fast to scan; consistent everywhere; mobile first

rule: Define colors by role (primary, secondary, success, warning, error, surface, border, text) and then generate a shade ramp for each.
dont: Creating random one-off colors

rule: Define a predictable type scale covering families, weights, sizes, line heights and letter spacing.
Use one spacing scale for all margins, padding, layouts and components so everything snaps to the grid.
values: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64; example card padding 16, gaps 24

rule: Use free resource sites for UI elements, SVG generators, icons and CSS gradients.
do: uiverse.io, fffuel.co, iconbuddy.com, webgradients.com

rule: Design mobile bottom navigation as a floating pill bar with the active item expanded into an icon+label chip and a prominent circular primary action (+) in a brand accent color.
do: Accent color per app type: calm orange for meditation, blue for workout, purple for finance, red for video

rule: Use AI as a critic, not a decision-maker: ask it to find research gaps, challenge your solution, list edge cases, tighten copy and prioritise issues.
do: Edge cases: bad internet, missing information, abandoned tasks, returning users, unexpected behaviour; prioritise by severity, user impact, frequency, business impact, effort

rule: Review interface copy to make it clearer and shorter, remove jargon and ambiguity, improve button labels and keep terminology consistent.
Never hardcode hex values; every color, spacing and radius comes from a token whose name matches the code.
Name tokens and components by purpose, not by looks.
do: button/primary
dont: blue-button

rule: Lock foundations and tokens first, then ship about 5 core components, instead of building 40 components on day one; give the system an owner, versioned releases and a changelog.
values: Order: color ramp + neutrals; type scale of 4 to 6 sizes; 4pt spacing, radius, elevation; primitive + semantic tokens; light + dark modes; 5 core components; variants, states and sizes; docs, owner, changelog

rule: Use curated libraries for product-screen references, UI components, motion inspiration and web 3D.
do: Refero Design, Watermelon UI, Motionsites, Three.js, Animaster Lib

rule: Study public design systems and compare how each handles the same component before building your own.
do: Microsoft Fluent 2, Adobe Spectrum, Uber Base, Pinterest Gestalt, Salesforce Lightning, Wise (wise.design), Vercel Geist

rule: When using a real-time explorable 3D scene as the hero, let it carry the story with one clear interaction, show a sharp poster frame while it loads and provide a lighter fallback for weak GPUs.
dont: A 3D world nobody knows how to move through

rule: Use inertial smooth scroll on immersive pages to keep WebGL and typography animation in sync.
Split headlines into letters and words that animate on load and hover instead of static headings.
Before shipping, check that all icons share the same stroke weight, optical size, corner style and fill-vs-outline style and are visually aligned.
Keep UI animations under 300ms and respond to input within 400ms (Doherty threshold).
values: <300ms animations, 400ms response

rule: Make popovers and expanding elements grow out of the point where the user clicked or tapped, not from an arbitrary center.
Stagger list and group entrances one after another instead of animating all items in unison, and use slow-in/slow-out easing so motion is less robotic.
Make animations interruptible so users can change their mind mid-animation, and add rubber-banding when pulling past the end of a scroll.
Animate frequently used interactions less; reserve exaggerated feedback for rare, meaningful moments.
Apply UX laws: make frequent targets bigger and closer (Fitts), limit choices (Hick), make the key item look different (Von Restorff), and polish the best moment and the ending (peak-end rule).
In scheduling UIs, mark conflicting slots on the calendar, offer the open times that fit the requested duration, and require explicit approval for overrides such as double booking.
values: Double booking should be a decision, not an accident

rule: Design dense operations dashboards in both dark and light themes with a visible theme toggle.
Use dedicated references for motion, scroll and shader work instead of defaults.
do: Craftwork skill, Emil Kowalski design-engineering skill (easing, durations, springs), GSAP ScrollTrigger guide, LottieFiles motion-design skill (duration and easing tables), MiniMax shader skills

rule: Use animated React component libraries to add polish quickly.
do: Vengeance UI, Animate UI (shadcn), Uiverse, Forge UI (Motion & GSAP), UI Lora

rule: Periodically audit screens for design-system drift (missing shared components, local overrides, unbound tokens) and replace one-off buttons and inputs with approved components.
do: Audit 20 dashboard screens to find inconsistencies

rule: Study spacing, hierarchy and interactions in curated galleries before designing.
do: 60fps (UI animations), Godly (web/app inspiration), Lapa Ninja (landing pages), Unsection (website sections), 21st.dev (components)

rule: Highlight the item in a project list or index that matches the content currently in view so users always know where they are.
Use scroll-driven section transitions (e.g. the page tearing open, headline changing color across the edge) so the story moves with the reader; every interaction must have a job, not decoration.
Make the background react to the cursor (shapes surfacing then fading) so the page feels like a material.
Turn the 404 page into something interactive (e.g. a small game) so a dead end becomes a reason to stay.
do: oaksun.studio: shoot broken pages while you wait

rule: Reveal headlines with a decode effect that scrambles through random characters before settling.
Give AI coding agents design skills and award-site references so output does not look generic; the human eye for quality remains the differentiator.
do: Stageshow, Impeccable, Dimensional Drawing, Oil UI, Emil Kowalski skills, Taste Skill, Brand Identity skill, Awwwards MCP

rule: Structure a mobile paywall as hero visual, short benefit headline, icon list of premium features and one full-width primary CTA with a quieter 'view plans' link below.
Build one page per real customer search (service x city, product, token) filled with unique facts such as prices, photos and reviews, link them together and submit a sitemap.
dont: The same text with only the city name swapped

rule: Use neutral backgrounds (soft grays, whites, light colours) so the content stays the focus.
do: Toned-down neutral screen with a single dark CTA for a serious look
dont: Loud gradient backgrounds with pink highlight unless you want a playful tone

rule: Choose legible, modern sans-serif fonts; lighter weights of Helvetica Neue, Inter or Manrope give a clean look, and Inter is the safe default when in doubt.
values: Helvetica Neue, Inter, Manrope

rule: Remove every element that does not add value and simplify the user flows before styling.
Use generous white space so content can breathe and the eye is guided to what matters.
do: Mobile hero: 32px and 40px vertical gaps between icon, headline and input, 86px input zone
values: 32px, 40px, 86px

rule: Show elevation with a very subtle drop shadow instead of adding borders or stronger fills.
do: Drop shadow X 0, Y 28, blur 28, spread 0, #000000 at 3%
values: X 0, Y 28, Blur 28, Spread 0, 000000 3%

rule: Use an 8-point grid for margins, padding and dimensions because 8 divides cleanly into 4, 2 and 1 without decimals.
dont: A 10-point grid that fractions into 5, 2.5 and 1.25 and makes elements look hazy at 1x

rule: Align icons, type and small elements to a 4-point grid for finer control while layout stays on 8.
do: Card: 16px padding, 72x72 avatar, 24x24 icon, 16x16 badge, 8px gap between avatar and text

rule: Prefer the soft grid method (space components relative to each other in 8pt increments) for flexible UIs; use the hard grid (snap everything to predefined 8pt cells) when strict rhythm is required.
values: 8 Pt, 16 Pt

rule: In a hard grid measure vertical text spacing baseline to baseline; in a soft grid measure it between line-height bounding boxes.
values: hard: 16pt / 24pt baselines; soft: 8pt / 16pt between boxes

rule: Make onboarding and login/sign-up screens match the visual theme of the app and keep them easy to navigate.
do: Social sign-in buttons stacked plus a short email form

rule: Never leave an empty state blank; add an illustration and a clear CTA that starts the first action.
do: 'When if not today?' + 'Create your first trip' button
dont: Plain 'You have no trips yet' text

rule: Use relevant icons, images and animation in onboarding to make clickable elements obvious and reduce cognitive load.
Make the key onboarding action prominent, explain why the user should accept a permission, and always offer a skip / 'Maybe later' option.
do: 'Enable Notifications and Never Miss a Good Deal' + secondary 'Maybe later'; 'Not now' link under 'Connect'

rule: Ask just enough questions (e.g. interests picked as chips) to personalise onboarding without being intrusive.
do: 'What are you interested in the most?' with selectable category chips and a progress bar

rule: Use a fixed grid on desktop and a fluid grid on tablets and phones.
Mobile column grid: 4 columns, 20px gutter, 24px margin, column width auto (fluid).
values: 4 cols, gutter 20px, margin 24px, column ~80px on iPhone 13 Pro Max

rule: Desktop column grid on a 1440 frame: 12 columns, 20px gutter, 100px margin.
values: 12 cols, gutter 20px, margin 100px, column ~85px, 1440x1080

rule: Tablet column grid: 8 columns, 24px gutter, 88px margin.
values: 8 cols, gutter 24px, margin 88px, column ~85px, iPad Pro 12.9

rule: Use CSS Grid alignment properties instead of floats/positioning: justify-items/align-items align items in their cells, justify-content/align-content align the whole grid in its container, justify-self/align-self override per item.
values: start | end | center | stretch | space-around | space-between | space-evenly

rule: Simplify grid templates with repeat() and fr units, and set gaps with the gap shorthand.
do: grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 15px 10px;
values: repeat(3, 1fr)

rule: Make outer-most containers span whole column widths aligned to the grid, and add padding inside them.
Inside containers you need not snap elements to columns, but use round numbers and at least 20-40px of inner padding so elements do not overlap when resized.
values: 20-40px inner padding

rule: Build a compact centred footer: round social icon buttons, a single row of nav links and a small legal line, over a layered wave SVG background.
do: Social icons 40x40, border-radius 50%, background rgb(255 255 255 / 6%) with backdrop-filter blur(10px), icon 24px; links gap 14px; legal 12px #a2b6e1; section gap 30px; body bg #0e121c text #d6dfed
values: 40px, 50%, 6%, blur(10px), 24px, gap 14px, 12px, gap 30px

rule: Use a web type scale with bold headings, tightening letter-spacing as size grows and keeping small text at 0.
values: H2XL Bold 70/80 -1.4; HXL Bold 64/72 -1.28; HLG Bold 48/56 -0.96; HMD Semibold 40/52 -0.4; HSM Medium 32/40 -0.32; HXS Medium 28/34 -0.28; Text XL Medium 24/34 -0.24; LG Medium 20/28 -0.2; MD Medium 18/24 -0.18; BASE Regular 16/24 -0.16; SM Regular 14/20 0; XS Regular 12/16 0 (px size/line-height, letter-spacing)

rule: Use an iOS-style mobile type scale with 16px body and 11px minimum caption.
values: Display Large 34/41 0.37; Title1 28/34 0.36; Title2 22/28 0.35; Title3 20/25 0.38; Headline Semibold 18/24 -0.41; Body 16/22 -0.41; Callout 16/21 -0.32; Subheadline 15/20 -0.24; Footnote 13/18 -0.08; Caption1 12/16 0; Caption2 11/14 0.07

rule: Check the contrast of every text level with a contrast plugin; keep secondary body text well above the minimum, not just the title.
values: examples: title 18.52:1, body 9.5:1 on light; 21:1 and 16.94:1 on black

rule: Test readability: set body copy large enough with generous line-height instead of tiny dense paragraphs.
dont: Tiny, tightly set paragraph text

rule: Scale typography with the screen using breakpoints so readability stays consistent on desktop, tablet and mobile.
Use size to signal priority: the biggest element is where users look first.
Choose symmetry for an orderly feel or asymmetry for a dynamic feel, keeping visual weight balanced either way.
Give strong saturated colour (high weight) only to primary CTAs and alerts; use neutral, low-weight colour for layout structure and secondary actions.
do: Saturated 'Add to cart' button with outlined grey 'No thanks, view cart'

rule: Create reading order with size, weight and spacing so users know what to read first and what to ignore.
Style related elements the same way (same button style, same card treatment) to signal relationships and reduce mental effort.
Resources for UI assets: lucide.dev and heroicons.com (open-source icons), flaticon.com (icons), pixels.market (illustrations), coolors.co (palettes), lummi.ai (AI images), Microsoft Designer.
Turn foundations into named reusable tokens (e.g. Primary-Color, Spacing-16, Heading-Lg) before building components.
Website type sizes: H1 80px, H2 56px, H3 32px, body 16-18px; landing display can be 64px semibold.
values: H1 80px; H2 56px; H3 32px; body-s 16px; display 64px semibold; body 18px regular; CTA 16px medium; subheading 16px

rule: Scale headings down per breakpoint desktop -> tablet -> mobile and keep sizes below 16px unchanged.
Use regular/medium for body text (16-20px), semibold/bold for body accents, and semibold/bold for headings 24px+.
values: body 16-20px regular/medium; heading 24+px semibold/bold

rule: Set line-height to 140-175% for body text and 100-120% for headings.
Limit body text to 50-60 characters per line.
values: 50-60 characters

rule: Define columns, gutters, margins, breakpoints and container widths as system rules: 4 columns on mobile, 8 on tablet, 12 on desktop.
values: Mobile 4, Tablet 8, Desktop 12 columns

rule: Define elevation as a fixed scale (shadow levels, blur values, radius scale, borders, opacity tokens), e.g. Elevation 1-4, so surfaces do not float inconsistently.
values: Elevation 1-4

rule: Define motion tokens for duration, easing, delays and enter/exit animations; use motion to explain change, not to decorate.
values: Fast 150ms, Normal 250ms, Slow 400ms

rule: Use one icon style: same stroke width, corner radius and filled-vs-outline choice, plus one illustration style.
dont: Mixing filled and outline icons

rule: Map design values to semantic tokens and CSS variables so design translates to code.
do: :root { --color-primary-500: #2563EB; --spacing-md: 16px; --radius-sm: 8px; }

rule: Build the rules first and the UI second: foundations -> principles -> tokens -> patterns -> components.

For mobile bottom navigation use a floating pill bar with 4-5 consistent outline icons, highlight the active tab with a filled pill (icon + label), and detach the primary action (search, compose, add) as a separate circular accent button.
do: Pill nav with active 'Home' chip + separate blue round search button; centre black '+' FAB in a walking app

rule: Use AI to question, challenge, check and refine your UX decisions, not to make them for you.
Tell product stories as visual chapters revealed on scroll.
do: Apple AirPods Pro product page

rule: Use floating navigation elements detached from the page edge to give a modern interface feel.
Set huge headline type over strong imagery in the hero.
do: Oversized 'Digital' word cropped at the bottom of a full-bleed photo

rule: For premium product sites, centre the product in 3D and move it through the page as the user scrolls.
do: Oryzo cork coaster site by Lusion

rule: Make carousel cards look clearly clickable with interactive hover states.

To keep AI-built sites from looking generic, give the coding agent design resources: TasteSkill, UI UX Pro Max, Awesome Claude Design (pre-built design systems), Design Motion Principles, Design.md Chrome (extracts a site's design system).
For premium tactile details, copy components from the Kitchen UI library (objects that behave physically: hold-to-confirm delete button, checkout that prints a receipt on payment).
For dark SaaS/AI interfaces use bento cards on near-black with a single warm or cool glow per card, big numeric KPIs, glassy beveled icons and small muted descriptive text.
do: Gauge card with '46.9% faster time to build'; glowing prompt input; checkmark tile 'Deploy with confidence'

rule: When designing with an AI agent, give it a concrete UI kit via Figma MCP so it builds from real components instead of guessing a style.

Layer tokens: primitive colours (orange-500 #FF3B00, indigo-500 #615FFF) map to a semantic token (color-primary) which maps to a component token (color-bg-btn-primary), so re-theming changes one reference.
values: #FF3B00, #615FFF

rule: Design every button with six states: Default, Hover, Pressed, Focused (visible ring), Loading ('Loading...') and Disabled (low-contrast, not-allowed cursor).

Compose complex patterns from tokens and components, e.g. a share modal with copy-link field, access-level dropdown, channel buttons, recipient chips and a full-width primary button stating the result ('Send to 2 people').
Use 60fps.design as a reference library for UI/UX designs and app animations.
Use ready-made animated product UI resources to make AI-built prototypes look designed (post shows a ready-made product UI kit applied to an AI prototype).
Right after the about line on a landing page, switch from words to proof: a bento row mixing big stats, a client-success quote card and a calm photo tile for breathing room.
values: 520,000 data points/month; 100% client success; 180+ industry leaders

rule: Give a headline social-proof number its own section in big type surrounded by floating customer faces so the number has people behind it.
Write section headlines in two tones: the key phrase in dark text and the continuation in light grey.
do: 'Transforming Businesses' dark + 'With AI & Innovation' grey

rule: Make every flow keyboard-operable following WAI-ARIA patterns, and give every focusable element a visible focus ring (prefer :focus-visible over :focus).
If a visual target is smaller than 24px, expand its hit area to at least 24px; on mobile the minimum target is 44px.
values: >=24px hit target; 44px mobile

rule: Set input font size to at least 16px on mobile to prevent iOS Safari auto-zoom on focus, and never disable browser zoom.
Never block paste in inputs or textareas, and make sure inputs keep focus and value after hydration.
Loading buttons show a spinner while keeping the original label; delay spinners/skeletons ~150-300ms and keep them visible ~300-500ms minimum to avoid flicker.
values: show-delay ~150-300ms; min visible ~300-500ms

rule: Persist UI state in the URL so share, refresh and back/forward work, and update the UI optimistically when success is likely, rolling back with an error or Undo on failure.

Design references for AI coding agents: Three.js Scroll Worlds (github.com/MengTo/Skills), diagramdesign.dev (44 editorial diagram types), Frontend Slides, Refactoring UI skill (skills.wondel.ai), Vercel Web Interface Guidelines (vercel.com/design/guidelines), plus GSAP ScrollTrigger, Emil Kowalski easing/durations, LottieFiles motion tables.
Give outer containers proportionally more spacing than inner elements, in 8px/4px increments taken from the spacing variables, and replace arbitrary spacing values with tokens.
values: 8px/4px increments

rule: Include screen-reader specifications in the handoff: VoiceOver (iOS), TalkBack (Android) and ARIA (web) annotations, e.g. for a checkout flow.
For premium portfolio/agency sites, reveal headlines by scrambling through random characters before they settle so text feels revealed, not loaded.
do: locomotive.ca

rule: Make a portfolio memorable by letting visitors play through it (e.g. drive a 3D car through projects) instead of browsing.
do: bruno-simon.com

rule: Keep flows tight and use gentle urgency so users decide faster.
do: Booking.com 'Only 1 room left!'; Duolingo 'Don't break your day streak'

rule: Place key actions or messages at the beginning and end of a sequence, where users recall them best.
do: Spotify Home/Search/Library at the bottom bar; Google Maps car/bike ETA at top

rule: Show progress indicators and checkpoints for incomplete tasks to keep users engaged.
do: MyFitnessPal '4,964 of 10,000 steps' progress ring; Netflix 'Continue watching'

rule: Use clear hierarchy and avoid clutter; put the element tied to the user goal in the most prominent spot because users miss what seems irrelevant.
do: Netflix autoplay hero at top; Amazon trending banner below nav

rule: Follow the patterns users already know from similar products to reduce friction.
do: Flight booking order From -> To -> Date -> Travelers

rule: Stick to one main colour and one accent, and keep strong contrast between the background and CTAs.
do: Neutral white/light-grey UI with black as the single accent for CTAs

rule: Use background blurs and subtle gradients (especially on iOS) behind floating bars and inputs to give the UI a modern, polished look.
do: Translucent blurred tab bar and input field over a photo background

rule: Use a zoomed-in, blown-up image as a full-screen background, tuned with opacity and blend-mode layers, for a dramatic artsy look.
do: Image fill at 80% opacity, adjust exposure/contrast, add layers with Multiply/Darken blend modes
values: 80% image fill opacity

rule: Prefer a soft point grid (spacing measured between elements) over a rigid hard grid, because it mirrors how elements are positioned in code.
do: Android 360dp and iOS 375pt screens with 16 margins
values: 360 DP / 375 Pt width; 16 DP / 16 Pt margins

rule: Size and position containers on the 8-point grid because most popular screen sizes are divisible by 8, so layouts can be subdivided without decimals.
values: 1280 width, 12 columns, 74pt column, 32pt gutter, 16pt margin + 4pt flexible margin

rule: In long onboarding flows show a progress bar or step counter so users know how much is left.
do: Thin progress bar at the top of each one-question-per-screen step

rule: Celebrate onboarding milestones with a micro-interaction (e.g. confetti) and a subtle badge so completion feels rewarding.
do: 'Congratulations, your profile is ready!' screen with confetti and an 'Approved' badge

rule: Treat onboarding as never finished: review behaviour and feedback and A/B test alternative onboarding screens.
Use a uniform grid of evenly spaced rows and columns to keep spacing and alignment consistent across the design.
Use a baseline (row) grid so typography and other elements rest on consistent horizontal alignment and spacing.
Align individual CSS grid items inside their cell with align-self (block axis) and justify-self, or both at once with the place-self shorthand.
do: align-self: start|end|center|stretch; place-self: center stretch;

rule: Build a bento grid by first laying a column/row layout grid on a rounded frame, then merging cells into tiles of different sizes so the overall shape stays a clean rectangle or square.
do: 1080x1080 rounded frame; 6 rows + 4 columns, stretch, margin 40, gutter 24; fill each tile with an image, type specimen or component
values: 1080x1080 px frame; rows 6, columns 4; margin 40; gutter 24

rule: Make every padding and margin an 8-px multiple; random gaps (12, 27, 9 px) confuse hierarchy.
dont: 12 px / 27 px / 9 px gaps inside one card
values: 8 px steps

rule: Wrap compact components such as cards in 16 px padding for breathing room.
values: 16 px padding

rule: Study open design systems as references when building your own.
do: modulor.design, thedesignsystem.guide, biings.design, orbit.kiwi, designsystem.morningstar.com

rule: For an immersive data dashboard, put a glowing 3D hero visual (e.g. a globe) at the centre of a dark UI and float translucent data cards and an AI-insights side panel around it.
do: Black background, cyan glow accents, glowing pill for the active nav item, KPI cards with mini bar charts along the bottom

rule: Justify every visual choice by purpose: add a colour, gradient or style only if it serves hierarchy or helps users, not to look modern.
dont: 'This needs more colors', 'Add a gradient here'

rule: Test with real users instead of assuming the UI is obvious; design so users succeed without reading instructions, since they scan rather than read.
do: Watch 5 users try the flow and count how many get confused
values: 5 users

rule: Remove everything that does not solve the core problem: fewer options mean faster decisions, and whitespace should not be filled just because it is empty.
dont: Adding 10 features; filling empty space

rule: Replace assumptions with evidence: interview users and prototype-and-test before committing to a feature.
do: Interview 10 users first; prototype and test
values: 10 users

rule: When designing for AI agents acting on the user's behalf, design trust signals, guardrails and a review UI that shows what the agent did at a glance, keeping the human in control without killing speed.
do: Confirmation steps, summaries of many agent steps in one view, signals that the AI was right

rule: Build a floating glass sidebar inset from the viewport edges with translucent fill, thin light border and backdrop blur, with collapsible sub-menus and subtle hover states.

values: width 260px; radius 34px; blur 30px; item height 50px; header 72px; transitions 0.3s/0.5s

rule: Prioritise hierarchy: make one primary action visually dominant and keep secondary actions muted, because if everything is important nothing is.
do: Solid black pill 'Primary' above a light-grey pill 'Secondary'

rule: Limit the palette to a primary, a secondary and a neutral colour; more colours create visual noise.
values: 3 colours max (caption)

rule: Keep typography consistent with few fonts and few sizes; many sizes and fonts create chaos.

rule: Pause canvas/WebGL `requestAnimationFrame` loops when the hero leaves the viewport, and do not start them at all when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is set.

dont: Do not leave an infinite rAF loop running under a scrolled-away hero; skip this for pure CSS animations the browser already pauses off screen.
values: zero rAF ticks while the hero is fully off screen.

rule: Keep interactive hero transitions (toggles, popovers, state switches) under about 300 ms, with an ease-out for entrances and exits and ease-in-out only for on-screen repositioning.

dont: Do not use ease-in for UI feedback; do not apply this cap to ambient backgrounds or long narrative transitions that do not block input.
values: candidate curves: ease-out `cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)`, ease-in-out `cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)`, drawer `cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)`; source is a practitioner guide, not a standard.
disagrees: practitioners disagree on hero flair: one camp favours whimsical, memorable CSS flourishes, another (Rauno Freiberg, Paco Coursey) strips motion from high-frequency triggers to 0 ms; do not mix bouncy hero physics with tools whose brand promise is speed.

rule: On cursor-reactive hero demos map pointer movement 1:1 immediately (feedback first), then settle with an interruptible spring or a CSS `linear()` spring.
do: Bind the element to pointer deltas without lag, and on release hand over to a spring that can be interrupted by the next input.
dont: Do not add an entrance spring to high-frequency utility triggers such as a repeatedly opened command bar; do not delay the drag start.
values: candidate spring: stiffness ~400, damping ~30, mass 1, or duration 0.5 s with bounce 0.2; 0 ms drag-start lag.

rule: Size oversized hero headlines with `clamp()`, balance wrapping with `text-wrap: balance` on short headings, and lock live counters or input-to-output numbers with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.

dont: Do not apply `text-wrap: balance` to long body paragraphs (use `text-wrap: pretty`); do not pick the headline size without checking the 320px width.
values: candidate `clamp(2.5rem, 1rem + 4vw, 4.5rem)`; the middle term mixes rem and vw so text still scales with zoom; tracking about -0.02em; balance only on headings of a few lines.

rule: When a headline is split into per-character or per-word spans for a staggered entrance, keep one complete accessible string and hide the animated fragments from assistive tech.

dont: Do not leave split spans as the only readable text; do not add a redundant `aria-label` to a headline that is not split.
values: stagger about 50 ms per character/word step.

rule: Honor `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` in hero and scroll scenes by removing or substantially reducing nonessential motion in both CSS and JS, and never let motion be the only carrier of product information.

values: MDN: reduce means minimize movement, preferably remove nonessential movement; `animation-timeline: none` is the documented opt-out for scroll timelines.

rule: Build live hero demos (command bars, code-to-preview, input-to-output transformers) with proper roles, a polite live region for output, modifier-gated keyboard shortcuts, and a visible focus ring.
do: APG roles; a native range input with `aria-valuetext` for scrubbed demos; `aria-live=polite` only for output the user triggered, never during autoplay; modifier-gated shortcuts; focus outline of 2px or more.
dont: Do not bind bare single-character shortcuts (WCAG 2.1.4); mark purely decorative hero visuals `aria-hidden="true"` with zero keyboard stops.
values: modifier + key; focus outline >= 2px.

rule: Prefer a real working input-to-output demo over a passive video or a gratuitous 3D load, and keep essential product content available without waiting for a pointer effect or a hidden interaction.
do: Show a pre-populated, editable or preset-switchable demo in the first viewport; state what the product does in text beside it.
dont: Do not gate the value proposition behind hover or a discovered gesture; do not let an entrance animation block clicks.
values: a blocking entrance should stay within about 300 ms; no source defines "wow" versus "gimmicky".
caveat: codex: no cited source validates a criterion for memorable versus gimmicky hero interaction; this is an inference from performance and reduced-motion guidance.

rule: Option: Show an input-to-output transformation in the hero (SQL to API, notes to brief, prompt to UI) with preset tabs, a pre-populated default and a short crossfade when the output changes, so a visitor grasps the mechanism without pressing play.
do: Paint the default input and output on load, offer 3-4 preset tabs, and swap output with a 200 ms opacity plus 6px translate transition.
dont: Do not use it for products whose value is passive media consumption; do not start with an empty input.
values: Option values: 200 ms swap, y 6px to 0, scale 0.98 to 1; "grasped in under 3 seconds" is an unverified target.
caveat: the under-3-seconds comprehension claim and the named-product demo archetypes were not verified on live pages.

rule: Hydrate interactive hero demos progressively: paint a static shell, attach handlers on idle or on first interaction, and keep input feedback within about 100 ms.
do: Render the demo markup server-side, bind keystroke and tab handlers on first pointer/keyboard event or idle, and defer heavy demo bundles.
dont: Do not ship heavy WebGL or demo bundles on the critical rendering path; skip hydration for CSS-only hover and focus effects.
values: feedback <= 100 ms after input (RAIL-style budget).

rule: Serve hero display fonts with a preloaded WOFF2 and a metrics-matched fallback (`size-adjust`, `ascent-override`) so a large headline neither hides nor shifts the product shell on swap.
do: Preload the one display font file, set `font-display: swap`, and define a fallback `@font-face` with `size-adjust` that matches the web font.
dont: Do not let the headline reflow the demo below it on swap; unnecessary when the stack is a system font.
values: CLS <= 0.1; `font-display: swap`.

rule: Set the scene scroll distance explicitly in pixels or as a measured fraction of the scroller (`end: "+=N"`), and treat a published example value as an example, not a universal duration.
do: Compute the pinned distance from state count (track height minus stage height), tune it with real wheel input, and keep it within a stated per-state budget.
dont: Do not copy 500px or 100vh per state as a default.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): GSAP examples: `end: "+=500"`, `end: "+=100%"`; the sticky runway pattern is `position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh` with stacked layers at `inset: 0`; runway about 100vh per beat (300vh-500vh for 3-5 states) is one candidate.
disagrees: gemini-hydrogen suggests roughly 100vh of runway per story beat; an earlier project review judged 67vh per state too long and cut to 47vh, and codex found only GSAP example values (+=500, +=100%); use the 100vh figure as an upper bound, not a default.

rule: When crossfading overlapping layers inside one shared runway, disable the injected spacer (`pinSpacing: false`) and give the runway an explicit overlap distance so no blank gap appears between panels.
do: Set `pinSpacing: false`, size the runway yourself in px or vh, and verify the next section starts exactly after the last state.
dont: Do not use it for sequential non-overlapping pinned sections that need the spacer; do not forget to add the runway height back, or the following content slides under the pin.
values: explicit overlap distance in px or vh.

rule: Normalize wheel input instead of hardcoding it: read `deltaMode` (pixel, line, page), never assume `deltaY` is pixels or equals 120, and tune scroll-scene lengths on a notched mouse and a trackpad.
do: Convert deltaY by `deltaMode` before using it in custom wheel logic, or delegate to native scrolling and CSS timelines that need no wheel listener.
dont: Do not encode a minimum transition length from an assumed wheel-notch distance; a notched wheel emits discrete steps and a trackpad a continuous stream of small deltas.
values: WheelEvent.deltaMode: DOM_DELTA_PIXEL = 0, LINE = 1, PAGE = 2; a notch is roughly 100px in some Chromium/Windows setups (not a standard).
disagrees: gemini-hydrogen reports a roughly 100px Chromium notch and 3 lines in Firefox; codex found no source establishing a standard notch distance or trackpad minimum; the MDN page documents deltaMode only, so treat the pixel values as device-dependent.

rule: Overlap the outgoing and incoming states of a pinned scroll scene across adjacent windows instead of switching all content at one threshold, so combined presence never drops to a blank frame.
do: Start the incoming fade (or place it with GSAP position `"<"` / overlapping `animation-range` phases) slightly before the outgoing fade ends, and give each transition its own range.
dont: Do not run fade-out and then fade-in sequentially; do not use a single-threshold class toggle for a scrubbed scene; keep deliberate dip-to-black only between unrelated acts.
values: text panels on a shared surface: the incoming fade starts at 55-65% of the outgoing window (v8: out 24-33%, in 29.5-38.5%). Near-total overlap (0.30-0.50 / 0.28-0.48) only for image layers. No source gives a best overlap.

rule: Give each scrubbed crossfade a pixel budget of its own so it cannot collapse into a hard cut: start around 200-400px of scroll per crossfade and treat anything under about 100px as a likely abrupt cut.
do: Express the window as an explicit px range (for example `animation-range: 200px 500px` or `start: "+=200"`) and test with a wheel, a trackpad and keyboard scrolling.
dont: Do not state 200px as a standard or derive it from a presumed notch size; do not leave a zero-change stretch longer than roughly 800-1000px between states.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate: 200-400px crossfade window, 100-200px overlap between adjacent states, dead-stretch ceiling about 800-1000px; all unverified. project evidence (DIRECT, one reviewer): fades of 2.5% of 140svh, about 31px, read as cuts in v7 (L687-689). v8 tests 9% per fade (122px at 900px height) and 14.5% per handoff (196px).
disagrees: codex found no source for a pixel crossfade window or a 100px minimum; gemini-hydrogen derives 200-400px from an assumed notch size and marks the thresholds UNVERIFIED.

rule: Fade the incoming layer in over a fully opaque outgoing layer and remove the outgoing one afterwards, rather than fading both linearly, because two half-transparent layers composite to less than full coverage in the middle of the transition.
do: Stack the incoming layer on top, animate only its opacity (and transform) from 0 to 1, then set the outgoing layer to hidden once the incoming one is opaque.
dont: Do not fade two stacked layers simultaneously over a visible background and expect constant brightness.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): compositing arithmetic: two layers at 50 percent each cover 75 percent; no external source.
scope: Only when the incoming layer paints an opaque background over the outgoing one. For transparent content on a persistent shell use offset fades (cgh-9).

rule: Option: Give each pinned state a readable rest plateau (transition in the first part of the step, then hold) and keep it truly still by default; add scroll-tied micro-drift only as an option.
do: Clamp the transition to roughly the first 40 percent of each step and hold the state for the rest; use a scroll-driven timeline so motion stops when scrolling stops.
dont: Do not add perpetual micro-motion by default; never keep micro-motion under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
values: Option values: candidate: transition 0-40 percent, plateau 40-100 percent; optional drift 1-5px translateY or scale 1.0 to 1.03, all through transform.
disagrees: gemini-hydrogen adds continuous micro-motion so the page never feels frozen; codex (MDN) says scroll-driven motion pauses when scrolling pauses and micro-motion should not be added by default or under reduced motion.
caveat: project evidence: fully still plateaus of 183-200px were scored as dead stretches in v7. v8 tests a scroll-tied drift of plus or minus 5px on the panel body.

rule: Option: For a hardware or multi-angle image-sequence scrub, preload compressed frames, draw them to a 2D canvas inside `requestAnimationFrame`, clamp the frame index, and scale the backing store for `devicePixelRatio`.
do: Compute `Math.min(frameCount - 1, Math.floor(progress * frameCount))`, draw once per rAF tick, and size the canvas by dpr.
dont: Do not swap `img.src` per frame; do not use a frame sequence for UI or vector stories that DOM or SVG can render at 0 KB.
values: Option values: candidate: 120-150 frames, total compressed sequence about 3-5 MB, smaller frame tier on mobile.
caveat: frame count and 3-5 MB are unsourced; a sequence of that weight must load after first paint or it breaks the 2.5 s LCP budget.

rule: Use linear progress for tweens inside a scrubbed timeline (`ease: "none"`), use `scrub: true` for direct linkage, and add smoothing only through the numeric `scrub` catch-up value, never as an extra easing curve.
do: Set `ease: "none"` on scrubbed tweens, start with `scrub: true`, and raise it to a small numeric value (0.5-1) only when motion feels brittle.
dont: Do not stack easing curves on top of scrub smoothing; use ease-out curves only for time-triggered onEnter/onLeave animations.
values: GSAP docs: `scrub: true` = direct link, `scrub: 1` = 1 s catch-up; snap duration 0.2-3 s and delay 0.2 s are doc examples, not defaults.
disagrees: applies to spatial mappings (position follows scroll). Short opacity handoffs in a CSS scroll timeline may carry per-keyframe easing (AR24).

rule: When ScrollTrigger runs on top of a smooth-scroll library such as Lenis, use `scrub: true` (or a very small value), sync the library to `ScrollTrigger.update`, drive it from `gsap.ticker`, and set `lagSmoothing(0)`.
do: Wire `lenis.on("scroll", ScrollTrigger.update)` and `gsap.ticker.add` for `lenis.raf`, then use `scrub: true`.
dont: Do not combine a numeric `scrub` of about 1 with smooth-scroll lag; the two smoothings stack into a rubber-band feel.
values: native scroll: scrub 0.5-1.0; with Lenis: `scrub: true` or 0.1-0.2, lerp about 0.1.
disagrees: numeric scrub smooths wheel notches on native scroll (documented), while with a smooth-scroll library it double-lags; the Lenis-specific values come from practitioner usage, not the GSAP page.

rule: Declare `animation-timeline` and `animation-range` after the `animation` shorthand (the shorthand resets them), gate scroll-driven CSS with `@supports`, and set `animation-timeline: none` under reduced motion.
do: Write `animation: name linear both; animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 0% exit 100%;` inside an `@supports` block and a reduced-motion override.
dont: Do not rely on CSS timelines where you need snapping, runtime height recalculation, or coverage of browsers without scroll-driven animations and no fallback.
values: order: shorthand first, then `animation-timeline`, then `animation-range`.

rule: If GSAP snapping is used, snap to explicit timeline labels or progress stops, consider directional snapping, and never prevent users from keeping their natural scroll position.
do: Define snap stops from labels in the timeline and let user interaction cancel the snap.
dont: Do not treat the documented delay and duration examples as universal values.
values: GSAP doc examples: delay 0.2 s, duration 0.2-3 s.

rule: Compute scroll-scene offsets as functions of live layout (function-based `start`/`end`/tween values with `invalidateOnRefresh`) and call `ScrollTrigger.refresh()` after fonts or lazy images change the document height.
do: Write `end: () => "+=" + container.clientWidth * 0.5` with `invalidateOnRefresh: true`, and refresh on `document.fonts.ready` and image load.
dont: Do not assume positions update continuously after arbitrary DOM changes; do not mix a one-time mount measurement with static `calc()` offsets.
values: ScrollTrigger calculates on creation and resize; function-based values and `refresh()` recompute.

rule: Wrap breakpoint-specific scroll scenes and reduced-motion variants in `gsap.matchMedia()` so unmatched queries revert pins and inline styles automatically.
do: Create one `matchMedia` context per breakpoint and put the pin and its tweens inside it.
dont: Do not use it for animations a plain CSS `@media` query can control.
values: GSAP 3.11+ matchMedia reverts on mismatch.

rule: In ResizeObserver and FLIP handlers batch all geometry reads before any DOM or SVG writes, and keep per-callback work well inside one frame.
do: Collect every `getBoundingClientRect` first, then write attributes and transforms in a second pass.
dont: Do not interleave reads and writes; skip this for isolated transforms driven natively by CSS timelines or anchor positioning.
values: 16.6 ms frame budget at 60 FPS; total interaction setup within about 100 ms.

rule: Use FLIP (First, Last, Invert, Play) to animate between measured layouts: measure both boxes, apply the inverse transform, then play it to identity so only transform runs.
do: Capture the first box, apply the layout change, capture the last box, set the inverse transform, then transition to none; with GSAP Flip pass `absolute: true` for cross-parent moves. Measure with the element's running or scroll-driven animation neutralised in the same task; `getBoundingClientRect` includes current transforms.
dont: Do not run FLIP on very large DOM trees where synchronous measurement exceeds the input budget; do not use it when the box never changes.
values: measurement within about 100 ms of the input; playback on transform and opacity.
caveat: codex could not verify an authoritative FLIP source; the aerotwist article and the GSAP Flip page were cited by gemini-hydrogen and were not reopened here.
