rule: Do not apply a non-uniform FLIP `scale(x, y)` directly to containers holding text or icons without counter-scaling an inner wrapper, or the glyphs squash and blur mid-animation.
do: Counter-scale the inner wrapper by 1/scale per axis, or animate width and height only on text-free media cards.
dont: Do not scale text containers; do not skip the counter-scale because the effect is short.
values: inner scale = 1 / outer scale per axis.

rule: Set an eligible query container and size internal scene offsets with container units (`cqw`, `cqi`) so they follow the component width without JS resize listeners, with a grid/flex or media-query fallback.
do: Use `container-type: inline-size` on the scene wrapper and express offsets in `cqi`; add an `@supports not (width: 1cqi)` fallback.
dont: Do not rely on `cqh` unless the container is `container-type: size` with an explicit height; do not use it when the offset depends on auto-growing text height.
values: 1cqw = 1% of the query container width; support starts at Chrome 105, Safari 16, Firefox 110.
disagrees: gemini-hydrogen says `cqh` computes to 0 without `container-type: size`; the container-query units fall back to small viewport units when no eligible container exists, so the failure is a wrong size rather than 0; verify on the target browsers.

rule: Size the pinned stage in `100svh` (with a `vh` fallback) so scrub progress does not jump when the mobile URL bar moves; use `dvh` only on a stage that must fill the screen edge to edge.
do: Set the stage `height: 100vh; height: 100svh;` and keep the track in `svh` or `vh`.
dont: Do not put `dvh` on the track length; do not use `svh` on non-scrubbed full-screen modals where resizing with the URL bar is wanted.
values: viewport units: Chrome 108+, Safari 15.4+, Firefox 101+.
disagrees: dvh fills the space as the URL bar retracts but resizes during scroll; whether that destabilises scrubbed offsets is a practitioner judgement, not stated on the web.dev page.

rule: Use CSS anchor positioning for HTML elements tethered to a named anchor (callouts, labels, popovers), with `@position-try` fallbacks for overflow, and keep a feature-query or JS fallback until the target browser matrix is confirmed.
do: Declare `anchor-name` and `position-anchor`, position with `anchor()`, add `position-try-fallbacks`, and wrap in `@supports (anchor-name: --a)`.
dont: Do not state a browser-support percentage from these results; do not use it for SVG path routing.
values: support dates reported by gemini-hydrogen (Chrome/Edge 125, Safari 26, Firefox 147, newly available baseline Jan 2026) are unverified.
caveat: codex: MDN documents usage but no support percentage or full browser matrix was verified; check current compatibility data before relying on the dates.

rule: Native `view()`/`scroll()` timelines also carry one sticky stage with 3 states (v7 L629-697 runs 17 nodes on one named timeline, DIRECT). Choose GSAP ScrollTrigger for snapping, several pins or older-browser coverage.
do: Build simple reveals with `animation-timeline: view()` and keep GSAP for multi-state pinned stories.
dont: Do not assume cross-browser support without a tested fallback switch (AR21).
values: only transform and opacity animations stay off the main thread.
caveat: the baseline dates reported for Safari and Firefox (late 2026) were not verified in this research.

rule: Choose connector geometry by diagram type: orthogonal smooth-step paths for pipeline or architecture flows, cubic curves for organic hub-and-spoke relationships, and a straight line for two adjacent nodes.
do: Route technical flows with horizontal and vertical segments and a small corner radius, and use curves where continuity of flow matters.
dont: Do not claim a universal orthogonal-versus-curved rule, and do not add routing for two adjacent nodes where a divider communicates it.
values: React Flow defaults: smooth-step borderRadius 5, offset 20, stepPosition 0.5; bezier curvature 0.25.
caveat: the library defaults are documented; the diagram-type choice is a candidate, and no source supports claims about named marketing sites.

rule: Lay out diagram cards with normal CSS Grid or Flex so text wraps natively, then draw connectors in an absolutely positioned SVG overlay (`inset: 0`, `pointer-events: none`) using coordinates measured relative to the container.
do: Subtract `containerRect.left/top` from each node rect and compute the path from the measured edge midpoints.
dont: Do not hardcode pixel positions or percentages that drift when cards wrap; do not use this for a fixed-aspect inline SVG whose text never wraps.
values: overlay `pointer-events: none`; coordinates = nodeRect minus containerRect.

rule: Recompute connector paths whenever the layout changes: observe the container and every connected node with ResizeObserver, listen passively to scroll on scrollable ancestors, and re-run after fonts load.
do: Attach one ResizeObserver to the container and the nodes, redraw in a rAF callback, and also redraw on `document.fonts.ready`.
dont: Do not use raw window rects inside a transformed pan/zoom canvas; apply the inverse viewport matrix there.
values: `{ passive: true }` on scroll listeners.

rule: Option: Keep connectors readable by ordering related nodes next to each other and giving parallel orthogonal lines their own lanes instead of letting segments overlap.
do: Order nodes in DOM and grid order to avoid crossings, and offset parallel connectors by distinct step positions or handle offsets.
dont: Do not hand-tune lanes for user-editable graphs with dynamic topology (use an automatic layered layout there); no source gives a numeric crossing limit.
values: Option values: candidate: handle offset 20-30px, step positions such as 0.35 / 0.5 / 0.65.

rule: Option: On narrow viewports where a multi-column diagram stacks, change the connector ports (left/right to top/bottom) or hide lateral beams, and keep short local connectors between stacked nodes.
do: Switch the grid to one column at the diagram breakpoint and remap ports so lines no longer zigzag over card text.
dont: Do not keep desktop routing on stacked cards; skip this when the diagram scrolls horizontally on purpose.
values: Option values: candidate breakpoint 640-768px; exact breakpoints are unverified.

rule: Use `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke` on connector paths so line width stays constant as the SVG scales, and leave room around the paths so wide strokes are not clipped at the SVG edge.
do: Set the property in CSS on the path, add padding to the viewBox or set `overflow: visible` on the SVG.
dont: Do not use the CSS property in exporters that only read inline XML attributes (use the attribute form there).
values: candidate stroke 1.5-2px for connectors, 3px for glowing beams.

rule: Read `path.getTotalLength()` whenever nodes resize to set `stroke-dasharray` and `stroke-dashoffset` for traveling beams, and under reduced motion stop the pulse but keep the static line.
do: Recompute the dash lengths in the same observer that redraws the path, and gate the beam animation on `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.
dont: Do not hardcode dash pixel lengths in responsive diagrams; avoid infinite beams on dense diagrams of more than about 15 connectors; dash animation repaints and is not compositor-only.
values: candidate: beam loop about 3 s linear.

rule: Use anchor positioning for rectangular HTML callouts and labels attached to diagram nodes, and use measured JS geometry for the connector paths themselves.
do: Position badges with `anchor()`; compute curved or multi-segment SVG paths with JS plus ResizeObserver.
dont: Do not treat anchor positioning as a connector routing engine; it positions boxes and behaves unpredictably against SVG sub-elements.
values: anchor() resolves rectangular edges and centre.

rule: Draw a dim static track path beneath animated gradient beams so the topology stays readable at rest, during beam gaps, and under reduced motion.
do: Render the track as a 2px low-contrast stroke and the beam as a 3px stroke with transparent end stops.
dont: Do not rely on gradient beams in print or PDF diagrams.
values: candidate: track about 2px, beam 3px.

rule: Anchor a connector label to the computed path midpoint, never to a hardcoded percentage.
do: Use the `labelX`/`labelY` values returned with the path and position the badge there.
dont: Do not add labels to connectors that carry no status or protocol information.
values: smooth-step and bezier helpers return [path, labelX, labelY, offsetX, offsetY].

rule: On a concept or pre-launch page publish only evidence that exists and can be checked: working integrations, dated changelog entries, security documentation, attributed statements, and exact real counts.
do: Replace every claim with something a visitor can open or verify, and use exact numbers you measured instead of rounded aspirational ones.
dont: Do not invent customer names, logos, user counts, certifications or review scores; do not present internal benchmarks as customer outcomes.
values: illustrative only: a precise real count (for example the number of pilot teams) beats a rounded larger one.
caveat: codex verified no CXL, NN/g or Baymard page for which proof format converts best; the CXL pages are cited by gemini-hydrogen and were not reopened.

rule: Frame pre-launch access as a founding cohort with a real capacity or timeline, and state what the waitlist will and will not send.
do: Write the cohort size you actually accept and the review cadence next to the form.
dont: Do not invent scarcity on an open self-serve product.
values: a stated cohort cap and email cadence.

rule: Label design-partner feedback by source and context: full name, role, company and a real photo when consent exists, the objection that was overcome, and whether it is an observation or a measured outcome.
do: Format each quote with named attribution and one specific before/after fact, and mark the pilot scope in a caption.
dont: Do not use anonymous initials, stock photos or unattributed quotes; do not give an extrapolated or unmeasured figure to a named partner.
values: quote + name/role/org + photo + concrete outcome.

rule: Show the people and the activity behind a pre-launch product: named founders with working profile links, where the team comes from if true, and a dated changelog.
do: Add a short founder note with a real photo and profile links, and link a changelog with dated entries.
dont: Do not use this to replace compliance evidence on regulated enterprise products.
values: dated milestone entries; named authors with clickable profiles.

rule: Answer "information hunger" early with a working demo or unedited UI capture and publish pricing or usage limits instead of gating them behind a sales call.
do: Show a live preview and a pricing summary or tier limits near the first scroll; where pricing is custom, publish the starting tier or the pricing model.
dont: Do not publish a fixed list price for truly custom enterprise deployments that would mislead buyers.
values: visible tier limits plus an interactive preview near the first scroll.

rule: Put security and trust indicators next to the sensitive form or CTA and link them to the document or audit that backs them; never present a security posture as independently validated without that link.
do: Place the policy, certificate or status link directly under the form field group and state exactly what it covers.
dont: Do not claim certifications you do not hold; do not leave trust cues only in the footer; skip heavy padlock chrome on a newsletter field.
values: Baymard reports that 19 percent of checkout abandoners cited not trusting the site with card information (consumer checkout, not SaaS signup).

rule: Keep early-access forms minimal (one email field and a submit) and state exactly what happens after signup next to the button.
do: Ask for email only, and add one line on cadence and privacy adjacent to the CTA.
dont: Do not ask enterprise routing questions in the first form; mark any optional field clearly when sandbox requests need metadata.
values: 1 primary field plus a privacy/cadence note.

rule: Option: Build the desktop bento on a strict 4- or 12-column CSS Grid with bounded span types (1x1, 2x1, 1x2 and at most one 2x2 anchor per section), consistent gutters, and cell proportions set by the grid, not by uncropped screenshots.
do: Use `grid-auto-rows` or `minmax()` for row heights, lock image cells with `aspect-ratio`, and keep outer padding equal to or larger than the gutter.
dont: Do not use it for equal-weight comparison catalogs, or for user-resizable widgets with unpredictable content height.
values: Option values: candidate: gap 12-24px, card padding 16-32px, radius 16-20px, max one anchor cell per section.
caveat: codex: no cited source validates a cell ratio, cell count or dark palette as more memorable.

rule: Give every tall (1x2) bento cell a distinct vertical content job: a sequence, feed, timeline, mobile frame, or stacked metric and chart, so the height carries content.
do: Fill the tall cell with a vertical artifact that covers most of its height, cropped tight without browser chrome.
dont: Do not put only a short heading and one or two lines in a tall cell; send text-only points to 1x1 or 2x1 cells.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate: artifact fills about 60-70 percent of the cell height; no source gives a minimum content count.

rule: Limit each bento tile to one idea: one crisp visual or mini-preview, a short headline, and one or two sentences of micro-copy.
do: Move long explanation to a standard section below and link to it from the tile.
dont: Do not use it for documentation or compliance tables that need multi-paragraph prose.
values: one concept per cell, one or two sentences, 16-32px padding.

rule: Option: Create sharp contrast inside dark bento cells: a small muted uppercase tag, a tight medium-semibold title, subdued secondary body, and tabular numerals on metrics.
do: Use a tag at 13px uppercase with 0.08em tracking, a 20px title at weight 600 with -0.02em tracking, and 15px body at 1.5 line height in a muted neutral.
dont: Do not set any text below 13px (body 13px or more) and do not let muted grey fall below 4.5:1 on its card surface.
values: Option values: candidate: tag 13px / 0.08em, title 20px / 600 / -0.02em, body 15px / 1.5, `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.

rule: Format numeric bento tiles (latency, throughput, limits) as one large display figure with a short uppercase unit label rather than numbers buried in prose.
do: Use one large `tabular-nums` figure above a 13px uppercase unit label, and only for numbers you actually measured.
dont: Do not use it on qualitative stories where a numeric headline would look arbitrary or fabricated.
values: figure larger than the 20px card title; label 13px with 0.08em tracking.

rule: Option: Ground the dark bento on a near-black canvas with a slightly lighter card surface and 1px alpha-blended borders instead of heavy drop shadows, and give interactive cells a boundary or focus ring that meets 3:1.
do: Use a near-black canvas, a card fill a few percent lighter, a 1px border at 7-10 percent white, and a visible `:focus-visible` outline on interactive cells.
dont: Do not rely on 7 percent borders for high-glare or high-contrast themes, or to identify interactive components.
values: Option values: candidate: canvas #050505-#09090b, card rgba(255,255,255,0.02), border rgba(255,255,255,0.07-0.10).

rule: Option: Implement a cursor-tracking spotlight border with a pseudo-element masked to the 1px ring (`mask-composite: exclude`, with the `-webkit-` xor fallback) and keep any inner wash faint so text contrast stays above 4.5:1.
do: Set `--mouse-x/--mouse-y` from `pointermove` (throttled in rAF), draw the gradient on `::before` with `padding: 1px`, and put card content above it with `pointer-events: none` on the overlay.
dont: Do not run it on touch-primary viewports or on static grids where many pointermove listeners add style recalculation; do not let a halo reduce text contrast.
values: Option values: candidate: ring radius 220-300px, optional inner wash radius 600-800px at <= 0.15 alpha, fade 300-400 ms.
caveat: mask and gradient repaint on pointermove; this is not a compositor-only effect, so measure on a full grid.

rule: Use light or border illumination, not a `translateY` lift, for non-clickable bento tiles, and reserve the lift for cards that are links so users do not mistake static tiles for clickable ones.
do: Apply the spotlight or inner-widget interaction to static tiles and a 2-4px lift only to link cards, with a 200 ms transition.
dont: Do not remove the lift on a gallery of clickable cards where it reinforces affordance.
values: candidate: 200 ms hover transition; lift 4px on link cards only.
disagrees: static light-hover versus lift is a practitioner preference; no source tests whether users mistake lifted static tiles for links.
caveat: adopted in v8 as AR35; it reverses the v7 lift on static cards (L612-614).

rule: Option: Order bento cells in the DOM by priority so the anchor tile comes first when the grid collapses from 4 columns to 2 and then 1.
do: Place the anchor cell first in source order and collapse at about 1024px and 640px.
dont: Do not rely on visual `order` that disagrees with DOM and focus order.
values: Option values: candidate: 2 columns at <= 1024px, 1 column at <= 640px.

rule: Option: Reserve real interactive micro-demos for one or two anchor bento cells and make every interactive cell keyboard operable with a discoverable action and visible focus; hover-only content may only decorate or duplicate information.
do: Keep at most one or two interactive tiles in a block of 5-8, make them focusable with a visible outline, and show every hover detail in the DOM by default.
dont: Do not make every 1x1 tile interactive, and do not hide required content behind hover; navigation-hub grids where every tile links are an exception.
values: Option values: candidate cap: 1-2 interactive tiles per 5-8 tile block; no APG pattern was verified for bento grids.

rule: The hero performs the product: the first-viewport visual is the product's transformation at page scale on one shared axis (input, intermediate, output), not a card beside the copy; it uses only existing motif parts.
do: Draw the first-viewport visual as input, intermediate and output on one shared axis, built only from motif parts already on the page.
dont: Do not place a product card beside the copy as the hero visual, and do not introduce motif parts that appear nowhere else.
values: Stages: input, intermediate, output on one axis.

rule: Scrubbable demo contract: one state variable and one render function; the HTML is the final frame; a head-script class sets the pre-state so the final frame never flashes; autoplay once in under 4 s; input cancels it; leaving returns to the final frame; keyboard through a native range; nothing focusable is ever invisible.
do: Drive the demo from one state variable and one render function, ship the final frame as HTML, set the pre-state with a head-script class, autoplay once under 4 s, cancel on input, return to the final frame on leave, and expose a native range for the keyboard.
dont: Do not let the final frame flash before the pre-state applies, loop the autoplay, or leave a focusable element invisible.
values: Autoplay once, < 4 s; native range input; one state variable.

rule: Crossfade budget, floors in px only: each fade at least 100px; the incoming fade starts at 55-65% of the outgoing one; the handoff at least 170px. A handoff is out, gap, in. Replaces the AR12 4% / 40% numbers.
do: Size each fade to >= 100px, start the incoming fade at 55-65% of the outgoing one and keep handoffs >= 170px (out, gap, in).
dont: Do not use fades of about 31px or fully still plateaus: v7 scored them as cuts and dead stretches.
values: px by viewport height: 800 -> fade 108 / overlap 42 / handoff 174; 900 -> 122 / 47 / 196; 1080 -> 146 / 57 / 235 (UNPROVEN until scored; superseded in part by the AR47 v10 table); floors fade >= 100, handoff >= 170.
caveat: amended 2026-11-23 (iter4): the '8% of the pin' and scroll-tied drift clauses were removed; amended (iter5): the 'max opacity >= .35' floor was removed because a handoff is out, gap, in.

rule: No token holds a distance measured at one viewport (DIRECT failure v7 L50 vs L675). Derive travel from CSS percentages of a shared container, or from JS measured on load, `fonts.ready` and ResizeObserver with animations neutralised.
do: Compute travel from percentages of a shared container, or measure it in JS on load, `fonts.ready` and ResizeObserver with running animations neutralised.
dont: Do not store a pixel distance measured at one viewport in a token.
values: Re-measure on load, fonts.ready and ResizeObserver.

rule: Connectors live in a reserved empty lane between source and targets (DIRECT failure v7 L273-276); targets sit in columns ordered like their sources; each source x lies inside its target's column; drops are straight; jogs share one lane with disjoint x ranges.
do: Reserve an empty lane for connectors, order target columns like their sources, keep each source x inside its target's column, draw straight drops and give jogs disjoint x ranges in one lane.
dont: Do not route a connector across any card but its target. Test: connector rects intersect no card except the target.
values: Lane 28px in the hero, 16px in panels.

rule: Tier and utility class names never double as content indices (DIRECT, v7 L107 vs L782); grep every short class for a second meaning.
do: Keep tier and utility class names separate from content indices and grep every short class for a second meaning.
dont: Do not reuse a short class name for two jobs.
values: Grep each short class name before adding it.

rule: A transform or hidden state that belongs to a responsive variant is declared inside that variant's media query (DIRECT, v7 L588).
do: Declare variant-specific transforms and hidden states inside that variant's media query.
dont: Do not set a variant's transform or hidden state in the base styles.
values: Computed transform is `none` outside the variant.

rule: A number in UI copy is written from the DOM count, or the counted items are never hidden by a breakpoint (DIRECT, v7 L552 vs L778).
do: Write counts in copy from the DOM, or keep the counted items visible at every breakpoint.
dont: Do not hardcode a count in copy while a breakpoint hides some of the counted items.
values: Check the counted copy at each breakpoint.

rule: The free offer is one sentence, reused verbatim in hero, plan terms and form; scripts read it from the DOM (DIRECT, v7 L759/L962/L1052).
do: Write the free offer once and reuse it verbatim in hero, plan terms and form, reading it from the DOM in scripts.
dont: Do not rephrase the offer per section or duplicate it in script strings.
values: Offer-string count: one distinct sentence across the page.

rule: On a concept page invent no people, companies or sample sizes; proof is a sample output artifact plus numbers counted from the on-page sample.
do: Show a sample output artifact and numbers counted from that on-page sample as proof.
dont: Do not invent testimonials, companies or sample sizes.
values: Every number traceable to the on-page sample.

rule: A stat has a numeral, what it counts, and a SAMPLE / TARGET / ILLUSTRATIVE tag.
do: Write each stat as numeral, what it counts and a SAMPLE / TARGET / ILLUSTRATIVE tag.
dont: Do not show a bare abbreviation such as "5 h".
values: Tags: SAMPLE, TARGET, ILLUSTRATIVE.

rule: Only an element whose meaning is extent (a timeline, a to-scale bar) leaves the grid (DIRECT failure v7 L142); nothing inside the wrap overhangs it by a few px.
do: Let only extent-bearing elements (a timeline, a to-scale bar) leave the grid and keep everything else inside the wrap.
dont: Do not let an element overhang the wrap by a few px.
values: Overhang is 0px except for extent elements.

rule: Before review, run a pixel-snap pass: measure a fixed list of alignments (1px tolerance) and the fractional position of every hairline at DPR 1.
do: Measure a fixed list of alignments to 1px and the fractional position of every hairline at DPR 1 before review.
dont: Do not send a build to review without the pixel-snap pass.
values: Tolerance 1px; DPR 1.

rule: Static cards do not lift on hover: ring change only; the 2px lift is for cards that are links. Reverses the v7 lift on static cards (L612-614).
do: Change only the ring on hover for static cards and reserve the 2px lift for link cards.
dont: Do not lift cards that are not links.
values: Lift 2px on link cards only.

rule: A tall cell holds a vertical artifact of at least 60% of its height (DIRECT failure v7 L318/L326); `margin-top:auto` never fills a cell.
do: Fill a tall bento cell with a vertical artifact of at least 60% of the cell height.
dont: Do not use `margin-top: auto` to fill a tall cell.
values: Artifact >= 60% of cell height.

rule: Give a pinned scene a tall outer track with a sticky inner stage so every state has physical scroll distance to rest in; size the runway from the number of states and test it.
do: Wrap the stage in an outer track (`position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh` inside it) and start from about 70-80vh of runway per state, then tune against real content and real wheel and trackpad input.
dont: Do not pin short pages (under about 2 viewports) or conversion forms; do not present an authored runway length as an industry standard.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): starting points 300svh-500vh total or 70vh-80vh per step; no cited source (GSAP, MDN) gives a universal hold length. project evidence (DIRECT, one reviewer): 150svh for 3 states, 50svh each, left state 2 with no hold (L785-786). v9 tests 220svh, 73svh per state.
disagrees: gemini offered concrete runway numbers from tutorials; codex found no documented hold length in GSAP or MDN, so treat the numbers as starting values.

rule: Separate the crossfade from the readable hold: let the transition occupy a short window of each state and leave the rest as a plateau, and lengthen dwell by extending the scroll distance rather than the tween duration.
do: On one named timeline give each state build, hold, handoff; lengthen the track to lengthen holds.
dont: Do not rely on a longer tween duration to slow a scrubbed scene, it only changes its share of the timeline; do not call an overlap-to-hold ratio a benchmark.
values: v9 candidate: handoff 10% of the pin (two 6.5% fades, 3% overlap), holds 12-15%.
caveat: gemini sources are search-grounding redirects, so no canonical page was verified for the numbers; codex found no cited standard for overlap versus hold.

rule: Tie scene progress to the native scroll position, keep the DOM text linear and readable, and animate only opacity and transform, so scrolling back reverses the scene and no content depends on finishing an animation.
do: Drive the scene with scroll or view timelines, keep headings and paragraphs as normal semantic DOM, and make every state readable even if the animation never runs.
dont: Do not call `preventDefault()` on wheel events, change scroll speed, or hide essential content until an animation completes; do not use this pattern for data tables or docs meant for fast skimming.
values: 0 custom wheel overrides; compositor-only properties are `transform` and `opacity`.
disagrees: the Nielsen Norman Group warns that scrolljacking removes user control, while scrollytelling practice pins scenes; reconcile by keeping native scroll physics and varying only opacity and transform.

rule: Do not put root-level scroll-snap on a page that also has a sticky pinned stage unless it was tested with real wheel and trackpad input, and never combine CSS snap with a smooth-scroll library or ScrollTrigger snap.
do: Prefer a pinned scene with no snap; if snap is needed, use `proximity` on a dedicated container, keep every snap child no taller than the viewport, and use one snap controller.
dont: Do not use `mandatory` where a child can overflow the container, do not use `scroll-snap-stop: always` on long vertical wheel flows, and do not rely on a fixed snap duration, it is left to the browser.
values: `proximity` for optional snapping; `mandatory` only when every target is reachable; project evidence: a root snap with a sticky stage trapped the wheel. v9 decision: no snap; rests are reached by step buttons that scroll to the hold centre.
caveat: the wheel-trap finding is project evidence, not from the MDN page; MDN documents the mandatory/proximity semantics and that snap physics is user-agent defined.

rule: Option: If a scrubbed scene must snap, snap to named timeline labels or an explicit array of progress values that match the rest states, and keep the snap delay and duration short.
do: Use `snapTo: "labels"` or an array such as [0, 0.33, 0.66, 1] with a short delay and bounded duration, then test upward and downward wheel scrolling separately.
dont: Do not use uniform numeric snap increments that miss the states, and do not pair it with a smooth-scroll library with a very low lerp value, it makes snapping asymmetric.
values: Option values: candidate: delay 0.1-0.2 s, duration min 0.2 s and max 0.6 s, ease `power1.inOut`.
caveat: not applicable to native CSS scroll timelines.

rule: If a pinned stage flashes unpinned content during fast scrolling, tune `anticipatePin` against real scroll velocity instead of copying a value.
do: Test fast wheel flicks and touch flings, enable `anticipatePin` only if the flash appears, and tune it on the target devices.
dont: Do not treat one `anticipatePin` value as a universal design constant.
values: GSAP documents the flash as about one frame (about 1/60 s); it gives no universal hold in vh or px.
caveat: not applicable to native CSS scroll timelines.

rule: Show a step rail, dots or chapter counter in a multi-state pinned scene so each state is a visible rest point that can be jumped to; mark the active one with `aria-current="step"`.
do: Derive the active state from timeline progress, (scrollY - track top) / pinned distance; an IntersectionObserver cannot separate states inside one sticky stage. Buttons scroll to the state's hold centre.
dont: Do not add a rail to a single-state section; do not claim the rail lets users stop unless it works as navigation or pause.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): no verified universal count, opacity or placement; keep inactive labels at opacity .6 or more.

rule: Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, replace the pinned scroll-linked scene with a plain stacked flow that shows every state at full opacity with no transform.
do: Wrap the pin and `animation-timeline` rules in a no-preference query, and in the reduce branch reset `opacity: 1; transform: none` and drop the pin spacer.
dont: Do not keep large panning or scaling just because it is scroll-driven.
values: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`; no universal replacement duration is stated.

rule: Size pinned stages with `svh` or `dvh` units, or a JS-measured inner height, so the mobile address bar does not make the stage jump.
do: Use `height: 100svh` (fallback `100vh`) on the sticky stage and re-test on a real phone browser.
dont: Do not size a pinned stage in plain `vh` only and assume desktop behaviour on mobile.
values: 100svh stage height.

rule: Replace missing customer logos with disclosed, verifiable credibility: who is behind the product, current dated content, and outbound links that can be checked.
do: Name the founders with relevant background, give a real contact, keep dates current, and link to code, docs or social profiles that exist.
dont: Do not hide an anonymous team behind generic corporate wording.
values: four credibility pillars attributed to the Nielsen Norman Group: design quality, up-front disclosure, current content, verifiable links.
scope: real products only; a concept page has nobody to name, use cgh-9 and AR42.

rule: Show only real design-partner participation and label the relationship as design partner, not customer; never invent logos, testimonials, waitlist totals or sample sizes.
do: Say "built with design partners" only when partners agreed, name them only with consent, and show a waitlist position or total only when it is real.
dont: Do not display unnamed logos, invented quotes, ambiguous "trusted by" claims or fake counters.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): about 5-10 design partners is a starting heuristic; no source-verified minimum exists; conversion benchmarks were dropped as unsourced.
caveat: gemini sources are search-grounding redirects, so no canonical page was verified for the numbers; codex found no verified count or ratio.

rule: Option: Publish a dated changelog and an open roadmap from before launch as proof of execution, using only entries that are real.
do: Use roadmap columns such as Under consideration / In progress / Shipped and versioned, dated changelog entries that link to real work.
dont: Do not publish a roadmap in stealth work where it exposes competitive plans, and do not backfill invented releases.
values: Option values: 3 roadmap columns; regular versioned updates; the named companies are practitioner examples, not a standard.

rule: Label every projection, mockup and number for what it is, and state the measurement basis: a target, an estimate, a simulation or a measured result.
do: Write "Targeted to...", "Simulated view" or "Prototype interface", add a short legible disclaimer of the conditions, and swap in audited data once real usage exists.
dont: Do not publish fabricated customers, waitlist totals or performance outcomes as achieved facts. Do not print the disclaimer as a tag on a headline stat; 'TARGET · design goal' read as self-undermining (L900, DIRECT). Take unmeasured numbers out of stat position.
values: no verified numeric credibility threshold; keep disclaimer text at 12px or more.

rule: Prove value with things a visitor can verify on the page: an un-gated interactive sample, a clear integration list, a founder note or a concrete architecture statement.
do: Offer a real sandbox or sample, list integrations that exist, and describe the architecture posture precisely.
dont: Do not imply that example content alone proves customer adoption, and do not use vague feature bullets in place of evidence.
values: no verified count of proof elements.
caveat: gemini sources are search-grounding redirects, so no canonical page was verified for the numbers.

rule: Treat "private", "secure" and "never used for training" as specific commitments: link the policy that defines them and state only the posture that is true today.
do: Describe the real architecture and retention, link the policy next to the claim, and say what is in progress.
dont: Do not claim SOC 2 or any certification before the audit is complete, and do not infer a guarantee from a polished interface or a generic privacy link.
values: no universal number; claims must match the policy text.

rule: Use only real pilot or beta quotes, prefer ones that name an initial reservation, and pair them with the real person details or no avatar at all.
do: Quote what a pilot user actually said, with consent, and omit the avatar rather than faking one.
dont: Do not script a reservation-style quote, use stock or AI portraits beside beta quotes, or stack many awards.
values: practitioner and Nielsen Norman Group guidance; no numeric threshold.

rule: Do not show a tiny raw social count; use a qualitative pilot description until the number is meaningful, and show full breakdowns when you do show a rating.
do: Replace "37 signups" with a factual statement of what is happening, and show the sample size next to any rating.
dont: Do not display an isolated aggregate rating or a small count that signals low quality, and never inflate a count.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): about 50-100 signups as a cut-over is a heuristic.

rule: Place real proof next to the claim or call to action where doubt arises, not in a logo strip at the bottom of the page.
do: Put a design-partner quote or security statement directly under the headline claim or beside the sign-up form.
dont: Do not collect all trust content in one distant block.
values: no numeric threshold.

rule: Keep the try-it hero LCP at or under 2.5 s by making an eligible element (text, image or video poster) discoverable in the initial HTML, and never rely on an empty canvas for LCP.
do: Render a server-side shell with the H1 and a static image or poster, preload it with `fetchpriority="high"` only when late-discovered, and keep the demo widget hydrating after first paint.
dont: Do not lazy-load the hero media, do not give `fetchpriority="high"` to more than one or two images, and do not block first paint on file parsers or model weights.
values: LCP good <= 2.5 s, poor > 4.0 s (p75); canvas is not an eligible LCP element type.

rule: Load heavy interactive engines (WASM, Web Audio, Rive) only on pointer enter, focus or click on the demo.
do: Dynamic-import the engine in the first interaction handler and show a ready static state until then.
dont: Do not bundle the engine into the initial script path.
values: zero engine bytes before the first interaction.

rule: Use a real file input with an `accept` hint for the supported types and validate every file independently of that hint.
do: Set `accept="image/*,.pdf"` style hints and validate type, size and content on the client and the server.
dont: Do not trust `accept`, the file name or the picker as a security boundary.
values: `accept` is a chooser hint only.

rule: Say next to the upload whether processing is local or remote, what is retained, and how to remove submitted content.
do: When processing is local use `URL.createObjectURL` and call `URL.revokeObjectURL` after load; when remote show the retention and deletion policy before upload.
dont: Do not claim files stay on the device unless the implementation guarantees it.
values: no source-verified retention period.
caveat: the cited page covers validation; the disclosure rule and the object URL cleanup are practitioner guidance.

rule: Pair every hero dropzone with a keyboard-focusable trigger and a native file input so the drag action has a single-pointer alternative.
do: Make the dropzone a focusable button with Enter and Space handlers that open the file picker, and keep a visible label.
dont: Do not build a drag-only dropzone or hide or disable the file input.
values: WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.5.7 (Dragging Movements, AA).

rule: Announce try-it outcomes (file accepted, format error, playback state) with a polite live region and never attach one to a continuously updating timestamp.
do: Use `aria-live="polite"` with `aria-atomic="true"` for discrete messages; reserve `assertive` for critical upload failures.
dont: Do not announce a scrubber every second.
values: polite for milestones; assertive only for critical failures.

rule: Defer demo media bytes until the visitor asks: use a poster for video, `preload="none"` or `"metadata"`, and create audio contexts only in the click handler.
do: Show a poster, set `preload="none"` on hero audio, keep controls on a lazy audio element, and preload the poster with `fetchpriority="high"` only when it is the LCP element.
dont: Do not preload a non-LCP poster that competes with critical resources.
values: `preload="none"` or `"metadata"`.

rule: Let visitors start sound and video themselves and give them native or keyboard-operable controls; the demo meaning must not depend on audio alone.
do: Expose play and mute with `aria-pressed`, a keyboard-operable range seek, and a visible pause for anything that plays.
dont: Do not autoplay sound, and do not autoplay any audio longer than 3 seconds without an immediate pause control.
values: WCAG 1.4.2: 3 second limit for automatic audio.

rule: Size try-it controls (pills, sliders, toggles) at 24px or more on desktop and 44px or more on touch, with `touch-action: manipulation`.
do: Give every pill and thumb a hit area at that size, with label text at 13px or more.
dont: Do not rely on tiny pill hit areas.
values: 24px minimum (WCAG 2.5.8); 44px is a touch guideline.

rule: Make the try-it optional: ship two or three ready samples and a non-upload route so the value shows in one click and the page explanation never depends on personal data.
do: Offer sample presets or a prepared sample file next to bring-your-own input, and keep the product explanation outside the demo.
dont: Do not gate the central explanation on a visitor supplying data, and do not stack many primary calls to action above the fold.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate: 2-3 presets; no verified count or layout.

rule: Replace large animated GIFs with muted looping video with a poster, or a state-machine vector canvas, plus a static reduced-motion fallback.
do: Use `<video autoplay muted loop playsinline poster>` or a vector runtime, pause it off screen, and show the poster when motion is reduced.
dont: Do not ship a multi-megabyte GIF, and do not run WebGL or vector loops off screen or on low-spec devices unpaused.
values: no byte budget verified.

rule: Measure the rendered contrast of quote text against its final surface, including any overlay, image or texture: 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.
do: Check the actual pixels, treat italic serif as large text only when it meets the size criterion, and recheck after any fill or grain change.
dont: Do not assume large-looking italics qualify as large text, and do not use an alpha value as a substitute for the contrast check.
values: WCAG large text = 18pt regular or 14pt bold; no serif-specific ratio exists.

rule: Never dim a dark-mode quote with `opacity` on its container; use alpha colors for the fill and border so the text stays at full strength.
do: Keep the container at `opacity: 1`, use `rgba` or `hsla` for background and border, and keep any dimmed secondary text at alpha .6 or more after measuring.
dont: Do not use container opacity except briefly in enter and exit animations.
values: container `opacity: 1`; inactive text at .6 or more.
caveat: a scrub pre-state may dim to a measured floor (v8 off-quote .45, large text); the resting state never dims.

rule: Lift a highlighted quote on a dark page with a very faint white fill, and add `background-clip: padding-box` whenever the fill sits under a translucent border.
do: Start with a white wash of a few percent alpha, tune by eye on the real surface, then recheck text contrast.
dont: Do not use a light boxy fill on very minimal monochrome pages, where a left rule alone works better.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate: rgba(255,255,255, 0.03-0.07), about 0.04 typical, on #0a0a0a-#18181b surfaces; codex found no verified alpha.
scope: callout blocks only; a fill behind a whole 24px display-italic quote read as muddy (L169-170, L213, DIRECT). See AR39.

rule: Use a thin left rule for standalone editorial quotes, and measure its contrast against both surfaces when the rule identifies a UI state.
do: Draw a 2-4px `border-left` in a faint white alpha for decoration or a solid accent token, and verify at least 3:1 when it conveys state.
dont: Do not use a left rule on a phrase inside a paragraph, use an underline or fill there.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate: 2-4px; rgba(255,255,255, 0.2-0.25) decorative; 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11) for functional boundaries.

rule: Highlight an inline phrase on dark with a thick offset underline or a dark tinted `<mark>` instead of default light-mode marks.
do: Use `text-decoration-thickness: 2px` and `text-underline-offset: 4px` in a color of at least 3:1, and override `<mark>` with a dark tint and light text of at least 4.5:1.
dont: Do not underline non-linked editorial quotes where it reads as a hyperlink, and do not use a 1px line that disappears.
values: the example colours are light-theme reds; on dark use a low accent band (AR39).

rule: Avoid pure white text on pure black for quotes; use dark gray surfaces and off-white text to limit halation.
do: Set the surface to a near-black such as #121212-#18181b and quote text to #e0e0e0-#f4f4f5 or white at about .85.
dont: Do not drop to a pure #000 surface with #fff body copy.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate surface #121212-#18181b; text #e0e0e0-#f4f4f5.

rule: Tune italic serif quotes for dark mode: use optical sizing and slightly more tracking, and keep them at a size where the thin strokes survive.
do: Enable `font-optical-sizing: auto`, add `letter-spacing` of 0.01-0.03em, keep weight around 400 (350 only at larger sizes), and use 14px or larger.
dont: Do not set ultra-condensed display serifs below 14px, switch to an upright sans there.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate: tracking 0.01-0.03em (0.02em baseline); no verified serif-specific ratio.

rule: Reset the attribution in a dark quote to upright sans, a muted light gray, and verify it independently at 4.5:1.
do: Set `cite` to `font-style: normal`, a UI sans at 13px or more, and a gray around #a1a1aa that passes 4.5:1 on the quote surface.
dont: Do not drop attribution to a low alpha such as .38, it is below the .6 floor and fails contrast.
values: 4.5:1 minimum; inactive text alpha .6 or more.

rule: Option: Verify dark quotes against WCAG 2.x as the baseline and also check an APCA lightness value, because WCAG 2.x alone can pass pure white on black while ignoring halation and thin italic strokes.
do: Pass 4.5:1 first, then review APCA Lc targets as a second opinion, and review the quote at its real size.
dont: Do not treat APCA as a WCAG 2 conformance criterion, and do not accept a 60% white secondary alpha without measuring.
values: Option values: APCA candidates: Lc 75-90 body, about Lc 60 large or short text.
disagrees: WCAG 2.x gives #fff on #000 21:1 as a pass, while APCA-based sources say Material-style 60% white secondary text can fail perceptual lightness; WCAG remains the conformance baseline.

rule: Choose the highlight device by role: a left rule for a standalone editorial quote, a faint fill plus rule for a callout testimonial, and an offset underline or `<mark>` only for inline phrases.
do: Pick one device per quote type and test hierarchy in the composed page.
dont: Do not mix all three on one quote, and do not apply a fill, underline or rule value as a sourced standard.
values: no verified alpha, underline thickness or rule width in the sources.

rule: Draw dark-surface hairlines with a 1px alpha `box-shadow` ring instead of a flat solid border, and keep nested radii no larger than the parent.
do: Use `box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgba(255,255,255,.08-.12)`, raise it on hover, and add a transparent border or focus outline for forced-colors mode.
dont: Do not rely on the shadow ring in forced-colors mode, where it disappears.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate: 1px ring, .08-.12 resting alpha, about .2 hover.

rule: Simulate overhead light on a dark card with two or more tinted shadow layers and a faint inner top rim line, and fade an opacity layer rather than animating large shadows.
do: Combine a tight and a wide shadow in the surface hue plus `inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.1)`.
dont: Do not animate box-shadow spread on hover or scroll, and do not use pure black shadows on tinted surfaces.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate: 2+ layers, rim alpha about .1.

rule: Keep grain very faint and non-interactive, and validate it in the composed page; use it to break up 8-bit gradient banding on dark gradients.
do: Use a monochrome noise layer with `pointer-events: none` at low opacity and a soft blend, and force grayscale so no color specks appear.
dont: No live SVG filter on DOM content. An SVG data-URI tile used as background or mask is rasterised once and is acceptable (L141-142).
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate: opacity .03-.08, overlay or soft-light blend; no source-verified grain standard (codex).

rule: Prefer a pre-baked repeating noise tile over a live SVG turbulence filter on scrolling pages.
do: Export a small tile (about 128-200px) as PNG or WebP; if a live filter is unavoidable keep few octaves and `stitchTiles="stitch"`.
dont: No live SVG filter on DOM content. An SVG data-URI tile used as background or mask is rasterised once and is acceptable (L141-142).
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate: numOctaves 2-3, baseFrequency 0.6-0.9, tile 128-200px.

rule: Render ambient glow as a large soft radial gradient on a pseudo-element and animate only its opacity, with cursor tracking limited to fine hover pointers.
do: Put the gradient in `::after`, fade opacity, and gate tracking behind `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`.
dont: Do not animate the gradient position or size on many cards at once, or run it on touch.
values: peak alpha .05-.06 on warm near-black; .15 flares; at most 2 pools per page (AR41).

rule: Reserve `backdrop-filter` glass for the sticky nav and modals, keep the blur small, never stack one glass layer on another, and provide a solid fallback.
do: Cap mobile blur at about 8-12px, add `@supports not (backdrop-filter: blur(10px))` with a near-opaque dark background, and keep glass off repeating cards.
dont: Do not layer glass over glass or use 16-20px blur over scrolling content on mobile Safari.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate: 8-12px mobile ceiling, 0 nested layers.

rule: Apply perspective and 3D tilt only to hero or showcase mockups, not to containers that hold body text. a blank rotated under-sheet is allowed; the text-bearing sheet stays unrotated.
do: Scope the 3D context to the device frame so surrounding text stays on the 2D pixel grid.
dont: Do not tilt scrollable card grids with crisp body copy.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate perspective about 1000px on visual frames only.

rule: Use `will-change` only on the one or two elements that are animating right now, and never on whole card lists.
do: Add it just before the animation and remove it after, on the specific layer.
dont: Do not set `will-change: transform` or `backdrop-filter` globally, it holds layers in GPU memory.
values: no numeric limit verified.

rule: Option: Limit concurrent depth devices on a dark editorial page so hierarchy stays clear: for example one grain layer, one hairline or rim system and one hero glow.
do: Choose the devices per page, validate in a trace and in the composed layout, and let lower sections fall back to flat hairline depth.
dont: Do not claim a device count is an industry standard, and do not stack grain, glass, glow and 3D in one viewport.
values: Option values: candidate: at most 2-3 devices per viewport; no verified count or GPU threshold (codex).
caveat: gemini sources are search-grounding redirects, so no canonical page was verified for the numbers; gemini marked this a synthesis with no numerical study.

rule: Option: Keep a blur used in a transition tiny and short, because `filter` is not a compositor-only property like `transform` and `opacity`.
do: Pair a small scale and opacity change with at most a 2px transient blur over 150-250 ms and test on mobile Safari.
dont: Do not blur full-viewport layers or hold a large persistent blur.
values: Option values: candidate: 2px, 150-250 ms, scale .93-.97; a practitioner source warns against blur above about 20px.
disagrees: one practitioner recommends a transient filter blur, mobile Safari GPU reports warn against large persistent blur; keep it tiny and brief.

rule: Drive scroll-linked depth effects with transform and opacity through CSS scroll timelines, keep them modest, and do not animate every decorative property.
do: Use `animation-timeline` on opacity and translate for a few layers and measure it.
dont: Do not assume CSS alone guarantees smooth performance, and do not scroll-animate every layer.
values: no verified frame-budget threshold in the cited page.

rule: Reuse one product-specific hero motif at section transitions and in later proof or demo sections, changing its role as the story advances.
do: Pick one motif tied to the product and let it frame a proof block or demo later with a new job.
dont: Do not repeat decorative shapes without reinforcing product meaning.
values: no verified count or spacing rule.

rule: Keep section transitions legible and motion optional; scrolling backward must not leave content hidden or half-finished.
do: Make each section readable without its transition and respect the reduced-motion query.
dont: Do not make animation completion a prerequisite for reading.
values: scroll-driven progress follows scroll position.

rule: Option: carry a blueprint grid with small corner crosshairs from the hero into feature matrices and section dividers.
do: Reuse the same 1px faint grid and crosshair marks so lower bands share one structure.
dont: Do not copy another brand grid, and skip it for organic or consumer lifestyle brands.
values: Option values: 1px lines at about .05 alpha; one company observation, unverified.
caveat: gemini sources are search-grounding redirects, so no canonical page was verified for the numbers; attributed to one company aesthetic.

rule: Option: dissolve section boundaries with shared 1px hairlines and bento modules instead of alternating opaque bands.
do: Align cells on one grid and light each module with a faint top gradient.
dont: Do not use it on pages without strict grid alignment, a few pixels of mismatch breaks the effect.
values: Option values: 1px hairline at about .08 alpha; unverified company observation.

rule: Option: carry a hero light beam into later pipeline or integration diagrams as an opacity or transform animation.
do: Animate a transparent-to-accent gradient with transform or opacity and disable it under reduced motion.
dont: Do not run many beams at once or on touch.
values: Option values: beam gradient from transparent via an accent to transparent; unverified.

rule: Option: echo hero keyboard cues and live product specimens in lower sections so scrolling feels like exploring the real app.
do: Reuse the keycap style (label text 12px or more) and one small interactive specimen per section.
dont: Do not load heavy multi-megabyte widgets in every section.
values: Option values: examples are Cmd+K keycaps and tabbed code switchers; company observations, unverified.

rule: Option: use uppercase monospaced telemetry tags consistently on eyebrows, bento headers and changelogs.
do: Keep tags at 12px or more with sufficient contrast and the same format everywhere.
dont: Do not mix several tag styles or use tiny low-contrast tags.
values: Option values: tag style such as [ v2.4 RELEASE ]; unverified company observation.

rule: Carry the hero typographic pairing (editorial serif lead plus UI sans) into pull-quotes and section leads, with no third display font mid-page.
do: Reuse the hero heading face on pull-quotes and the UI sans on supporting text.
dont: Do not introduce a third display font in feature grids.
values: no numeric values.

rule: Tint borders, shadows and text toward the same brand hue in every section and keep nested radii concentric.
do: Derive neutrals from the brand hue and inner radius = outer radius minus padding.
dont: Do not mix pure-neutral shadows with tinted surfaces.
values: no numeric values verified.

rule: Recompose the hero from available width and copy length, test at exact widths including 1024px and 1280px, and keep two columns only when the demo stays legible beside readable copy.
do: Stack to one column below 1024px, use two columns from 1024px with a smaller gap and padding, and widen the gap and padding inside a max-width container from 1280px.
dont: Do not treat 1024 and 1280 as universal breakpoints or attribute a breakpoint to a named site without inspecting its CSS.
values: project: 1024-1199 h1 full width, lead columns 1-8, CTA row left under it; from 1200 h1 columns 1-8, side 9-12, side height <= h1 height.

rule: Give a dense dashboard preview more width than the copy at 1024px with an asymmetric split, and keep an even split for balanced visuals.
do: Use a 12-column grid with about 5 columns of copy and 7 of visual for dense UI.
dont: Do not use the asymmetric split for very long headlines that would wrap past four lines in the narrow column.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate 5:7 versus 1:1.

rule: Option: when the product column is too narrow at 1024px, let the mockup overflow and clip at the hero edge rather than shrinking UI text, keeping key content inside.
do: Use `overflow: hidden` on the hero and keep the important part of the UI inside the visible area.
dont: Do not crop symmetrical diagrams where labels sit on the cut edge.
values: Option values: applies at about 1024px; inferred composition rule, not a source standard.

rule: Bound the hero height to the usable laptop viewport instead of `100vh` or a fixed minimum so the primary call to action stays above the fold.
do: Use `min-height: clamp(500px, 80svh, 700px)` and check on 1280x720, 1280x800 and 1366x768.
dont: Do not use a rigid minimum of 720-800px, except on an intended full-bleed 100svh editorial cover with a scroll cue.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate: usable height about 600-700px on common laptops.
disagrees: generic starter templates specify roughly 720-800px minimums with even splits, while laptop viewport data suggests only 600-700px usable height.

rule: Scale the hero H1 fluidly and keep it to two lines plus one or two short subhead sentences at 1024px.
do: Use `clamp()` for font-size, a line-height near 1.15 and trim the copy if it wraps past two lines.
dont: Do not squeeze a very long headline into a narrow column.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate: font-size clamp(2rem, 4vw, 3.25rem), line-height about 1.15.
caveat: candidate only; authored line breaks (3 lines at 61-80px here) beat a line-count rule.

rule: Keep the primary call to action next to its explanatory copy when the hero stacks, and lay primary and secondary actions out horizontally or inline so a stack does not push them below the fold.
do: Use a wrapping flex row or an inline email-plus-button field and keep the demo visible without a long intro.
dont: Do not squeeze three or more buttons into one narrow column at 1024px.
values: no verified breakpoint or placement benchmark.

rule: Defer the two-column split to 1280px, or stack below 1024px, if the copy wraps awkwardly, and cap the right-column visual height.
do: Switch the split at the breakpoint where the CTA stops wrapping, and cap the preview height so it clears the laptop fold.
dont: Do not let a tall preview graphic pass the 768px laptop fold; skip this when copy is very short.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate: visual height at most about 500px at 1024px.

rule: Preload only the display face used by the LCP text; no `fetchpriority` on non-LCP previews.
do: Preload only the display weight used above the fold and subset it with `unicode-range`.
dont: Do not preload below-the-fold font weights.
values: no verified figure; preload one display face only.
caveat: gemini sources are search-grounding redirects, so no canonical page was verified for the numbers.

rule: Spine: one product-true axis leaves the hero and runs through every lower section; sections are dated entries hooked to it; all times come from one clock table. The spine starts after the end of the tape, not at 00:00.
do: Run one product-true axis from the hero through every lower section, hook each section to it as a dated entry and take every time from one clock table.
dont: Do not give sections their own unrelated timelines or hand-typed times.
values: One axis; one clock table; the spine starts at the turn (after the end of the tape), not at 00:00.

rule: Rest states (DIRECT failures v8 L774-779, L785-786): each state = build, hold, handoff; hold >= 200px and >= its handoff; nothing inside the frame changes in a hold; chrome never translates inside a static shell; no drift.
do: Give each state a build, a hold of at least 200px (and at least its handoff) and a handoff, and keep everything in the frame still during the hold.
dont: Do not translate chrome inside a static shell and do not add scroll-tied drift to a hold.
values: Hold >= 200px and >= handoff; see manual-motion-tokens for the v9 px table.

rule: Quote marker (DIRECT failure v8 L169-170): one device for every quote, a band over the lower .38em in the accent (.32 alpha dark, .6 paper); no fill box, no left bar.
do: Mark every quote with one accent band over the lower .38em of the text, alpha .32 on dark and .6 on paper.
dont: Do not use a fill box or a left bar behind quotes.
values: Band: lower .38em; alpha .32 dark, .6 paper.

rule: Bars to scale (DIRECT failure v8 L343-349): shared start x, one line each, both end-capped, both >= 3:1, none leaves the viewport.
do: Start all comparison bars at one x, keep each on one line, end-cap both and keep both at >= 3:1 inside the viewport.
dont: Do not let a bar leave the viewport or fall below 3:1.
values: Contrast >= 3:1; shared start x.

rule: Depth budget: grain as a background tile, rim and shadow on objects, at most one light pool per viewport and two per page; no glass beyond the nav; at most one 2D flip per page; no perspective, no preserve-3d, no animated shadow.
do: Use grain as a background tile, put rim and shadow on objects, and limit light pools to one per viewport and two per page.
dont: Do not use glass beyond the nav, perspective or preserve-3d transforms, or animated shadows; at most one 2D flip per page.
values: Pools: 1 per viewport, 2 per page.

rule: Proof by anatomy: on a concept page, proof is an annotated sample artifact whose every claim can be opened on the page; no stat carries a target tag; the concept disclosure appears once, in the footer.
do: Show an annotated sample artifact whose every claim opens on the page, and state the concept disclosure once in the footer.
dont: Do not attach a target tag to a stat or repeat the disclosure.
values: Disclosure count: one, in the footer.

rule: One audience (DIRECT, v8 L846 vs L1061, L1071): the hero range is the union of the plan ranges; plans partition it.
do: Make the hero audience range the union of the plan ranges and let the plans partition it.
dont: Do not name an audience in the hero that no plan covers.
values: Grep the audience range in hero and plans.

rule: Passive input never cancels autoplay (DIRECT, v8 L1254-1258): hover arms after autoplay ends; click, drag and keys cancel.
do: Arm hover only after autoplay ends and cancel autoplay on click, drag or keys.
dont: Do not cancel autoplay on a passive pointer move or hover.
values: Cancel on click, drag, keys only.

rule: No masked or rolling text in a scrubbed panel (DIRECT, v8 L724, L786): whole rows only.
do: Animate whole rows in a scrubbed panel.
dont: Do not mask or roll text inside a scrubbed panel.
values: Whole rows only.

rule: Extends AR36 (DIRECT, v8 L490): no flex auto-margin fills a column.
do: Size column content explicitly instead of letting a flex auto-margin fill the column.
dont: Do not use a flex auto-margin to fill a column.
values: No `margin: auto` fill in columns.

rule: In a pinned scene, never let the outgoing and incoming text of two states be readable at the same time in the same box; fade the outgoing state to zero before the incoming one starts.
do: Give each state its own window on the timeline: hold, exit to opacity 0, a short empty gap, then enter, so only one text state is legible at any scroll position.
dont: Do not crossfade multi-line headlines or paragraphs that occupy the same area, and do not rely on a 50% midpoint overlap for dense or light-on-dark type.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): example split (State 1 exit 22-28%, gap 28-34%, State 2 enter 34-62% of the track); a 4-10% gap; no source documents these numbers. project evidence (DIRECT, L854-855): a 3% overlap of two fading vignettes printed two title bars over each other. v10 candidate: out 5.5%, empty gap 1%, in 5.5% of a 250svh pin.
disagrees: codex found no source for any handoff delay or opacity threshold and calls the no-overlap rule a design inference; gemini presents sequential fades as established and cites GSAP docs for the syntax only, so the gap size is a starting value to test.

rule: Choose the handoff device by content: sequential fade or rectangular clip-path wipe for text, a simultaneous crossfade only for photos, media layers and one-line captions.
do: A wipe needs an opaque layer under it; states that are transparent over one shared shell (L797-798) take the sequential fade.
dont: Do not wipe transparent text layers directly over unclipped text, and do not use complex multi-vertex clip paths for a scrubbed text handoff.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate wipe `inset(0 100% 0 0)` to `inset(0)`; slices such as `entry 40% 70%` then `70% 100%`; codex lists crossfade, wipe and morph as options to prototype, with no verified superior one.
disagrees: GSAP-style crossfade guides favour overlap to avoid dead air, readability guidance favours zero overlap; clip-path wipes sit between them, but complex shapes may lose compositor acceleration. Codex treats all three as prototype candidates.

rule: Stack the competing states in one CSS grid cell so they share one frame, instead of stacking absolutely positioned boxes.
do: Use `display: grid; grid-template-areas: "stack"` with every state set to `grid-area: stack` so the frame follows the tallest state across font-size and viewport changes.
dont: Do not use this when states intentionally sit at independent offsets outside one shared container.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate container width `min(600px, 90vw)` to 800px.

rule: Drive child states from a view timeline on the tall outer track, with a sticky inner stage, instead of a scroll timeline on the sticky child, and always ship a readable static state.
do: Put `view-timeline` on the outer track and `position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh` on the stage, drive children with `animation-timeline: --name` and `animation-range: contain 0% contain 100%`, and keep the `animation-timeline` declaration after the `animation` shorthand.
dont: Do not put `animation-timeline` before the `animation` shorthand, it gets reset; do not make the animated version the only presentation of the content.
values: outer track about 300vh-400vh is a gemini example (test per content); range `contain 0%` to `contain 100%`; codex: no recommended duration, declaration order matters.
caveat: gemini sources were not opened here, so the numbers are unverified; the MDN property page documents the shorthand order and timeline syntax; the sticky-parent view timeline pattern and the 300-400vh track are from gemini.

rule: Use `linear` easing on keyframes bound to a scroll timeline so scroll distance maps one to one to progress; reserve eased curves for time-based, step-triggered transitions.
do: Write `animation: name linear both` with `animation-timeline`; give discrete UI transitions an ease-out curve of about 125-250 ms.
dont: Applies to the timeline mapping. A per-segment curve inside a scrubbed keyframe is fine when the segment is >= 100px (L845-870).
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate: ease-out `cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)` 125-250 ms; `cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)` 200-500 ms for drawers; scale entry `0.93-0.97`, never `scale(0)`.
disagrees: an animation-craft author wants every UI transition under 300 ms with ease-out, while scroll timelines need linear easing and large-area drawers or masked headline rolls may run 300-500 ms; split by trigger type (scrubbed, interactive control, large drawer).

rule: When a shared frame or badge changes size or position between pinned states, animate it with FLIP or a view transition on transform, not by animating width, height, top or left.
do: Measure first and last rects, apply the inverse `translate()` and `scale()`, then animate `transform` to `none` in 300 ms or less, or use `document.startViewTransition()`.
dont: Do not scale text-heavy boxes unless the inner text is counter-scaled or crossfaded.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate: transform transition at most about 300 ms; 16 ms frame budget at 60 fps.
scope: time-based transitions only; not for scrubbed scenes.

rule: Option: morph a persistent pinned header chapter label with a one-line masked viewport and a translated vertical stack, with only the active label exposed to assistive technology.
do: Use `overflow: hidden; height: 1.2em; line-height: 1.2em` and `transform: translateY(...)` on the stack; set the inactive labels `aria-hidden="true"`; keep label text at 12px or more.
dont: Do not use it where the label wraps to several lines, the 1.2em mask clips it.
values: Option values: mask 1.2em, step shift -1.2em, roll about 300 ms with `cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)`.
caveat: Collides with AR45 inside a scrubbed panel. One-line label only, and the roll sits inside the empty gap.

rule: Option: detect a stuck header or pinned element with a scroll-state container query instead of a scroll listener, and keep an IntersectionObserver sentinel as the fallback.
do: Set `container-type: scroll-state` on the sticky element and style compact chrome in `@container scroll-state(stuck: top)`.
dont: Do not depend on it without a fallback where the target browsers lack scroll-state queries.
values: Option values: `position: sticky; top: 0; container-type: scroll-state`; browser support not verified here.

rule: Toggle `inert` on the non-active overlapping layers of a pinned frame so Tab, screen readers and find-in-page skip hidden states, and offset scrolled focus targets below the sticky header.
do: Set `inert` on inactive panels from the step logic and add `scroll-padding-top` or `scroll-margin-top` of header height plus a buffer so a focused control is not obscured (WCAG 2.4.11).
dont: Do not leave interactive links inside opacity-0 layers; in a CSS-only scene with no JS keep controls outside the stack.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate `scroll-padding-top` about 90px, or header height plus 16px.

rule: Keep the scene content reachable in ordinary document order and via keyboard, and never make a drag or trackpad gesture the only path to later states.
do: Use real DOM text for every state, real buttons for step navigation, and normal tab order through the scene.
dont: Do not treat a skip link as a substitute for accessible content and controls inside the sequence.
values: no source-backed scene-specific placement or paging values (codex).

rule: A fold is one flap mirrored across a 45 degree crease in 2D, `rotate(45deg) scaleX(-1 to 1) rotate(-45deg)`, in a reserved zone with no text inside its sweep. Hinged 3D planes on a full-width strip: rejected here (card 1 sits 20px from the trunk, L215; 24px gutters, L70; the sweep crosses text).
do: Use `perspective`, `transform-style: preserve-3d`, `rotateX` or `rotateY` and an opacity sheen tied to the fold angle, on a handful of hinged planes, and keep the core message in plain text beside it.
dont: Do not use it as arbitrary geometric sculpture, do not exceed about 6-8 hinged planes on mobile, and do not name it as the pattern of a specific site without inspecting that site.
values: Option values: candidate: perspective 800px-1200px, 6-8 planes at most; codex found no verifiable CSS or SVG example of this exact transformation.
disagrees: gemini offers the CSS 3D fold as a synthesized candidate with concrete values; codex found no verifiable example of a paper-tape fold and marks its values unknown. Prototype and measure before adopting it.

rule: Animate hero and stand-out elements with transform and opacity, wrap a complex inline SVG in a div and animate the wrapper, and do not assume even these are free.
do: Animate `transform` and `opacity` on the wrapper, apply `will-change` only to the one element that animates now, and measure layer memory.
dont: Do not animate internal SVG geometry attributes every frame, do not leave `will-change` on dozens of idle cards, and do not claim a transform alone protects the LCP.
values: frame budget about 16.6 ms at 60 fps; no element-count or duration limit in the sources.

rule: use a CSS `linear()` spring for follow-through on the hero focal object and switch it off under reduced motion.
do: Store the curve in a custom property, gate continuous sweeps, 3D folds and springs in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, and show the static end state under `reduce`.
dont: Do not rely on cascade order alone to fall back a custom property, an unsupported `linear()` still parses as a valid custom property.
values: reduced-motion override of about 0.01 ms is a gemini pattern; MDN notes scaling and panning large objects can trigger vestibular symptoms but gives no safe threshold.
scope: time-based transitions only; not for scrubbed scenes.

rule: keep the LCP headline and main product visual painted at full opacity from first render and defer below-fold sections with `content-visibility`.
do: Do not gate the LCP element behind an entrance animation, mark the hero image `fetchpriority="high"`, and add `content-visibility: auto` with `contain-intrinsic-size` to heavy sections below the fold.
dont: Do not apply `content-visibility: auto` to the hero, and do not omit `contain-intrinsic-size`, the scrollbar will jump. No `content-visibility:auto` on a section whose children overflow it (trunk offsets L561-563, under-sheets L253): paint containment clips them.
values: LCP good at or under 2.5 s at p75, poor above 4.0 s; `contain-intrinsic-size: auto 300px` example.

rule: Publish specific and supportable security and data-handling statements, link the fuller policy, and describe a planned control as planned, never as an operating guarantee.
do: State what is true today (encryption, retention and deletion windows, no-training pledge only if real), name an in-progress audit with its honest status, and link a trust or security page that exists.
dont: Do not show a SOC 2 or ISO seal for an audit still in progress, and do not claim certifications, controls or retention behaviour the product does not have.
values: no universal placement or required certification; AES-256 and TLS 1.3 are gemini examples to state only if true.
scope: A concept has no 'true today'. State the design policy in plain present tense; no audit, cipher, customer or changelog claims; one disclosure (AR42); only links that resolve on the page.

rule: Do not fabricate customer logos, testimonials or adoption; substitute things the product can substantiate, such as an inspectable demo, a documented data policy and real build progress.
do: Show a working sample, a dated changelog of real entries and links to verifiable code, docs or founder profiles.
dont: Do not state an open roadmap, changelog or privacy diagram is a proven trust or conversion tactic; no reviewed source shows that.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): no placement or count benchmark; gemini cites public changelog and roadmap pages of other companies as examples, not as evidence of effect.
disagrees: gemini marks the open changelog and roadmap as directly supported momentum proof; codex states no reviewed source proves they raise trust. Use them as disclosure, not as a claimed conversion lift.
scope: A concept has no 'true today'. State the design policy in plain present tense; no audit, cipher, customer or changelog claims; one disclosure (AR42); only links that resolve on the page.

rule: Make the four credibility factors explicit on a concept launch: visual craft equal to the claim, up-front disclosure of beta status and pricing, dated current content, and verifiable external links.
do: Link a repo, founder profile, trust page or docs, keep dates current, and remove any link or claim that cannot be verified.
dont: Do not leave broken external links or undated proof on a page that asks for trust.
values: four pillars (design quality, up-front disclosure, current content, verifiable links) from a usability research group; no count threshold.
scope: A concept has no 'true today'. State the design policy in plain present tense; no audit, cipher, customer or changelog claims; one disclosure (AR42); only links that resolve on the page.

rule: Show real product UI states and the beta or plan scope before asking for an email, instead of putting the interface behind a demo-booking wall.
do: Show full-resolution workflow states and what the beta includes ahead of the waitlist field.
dont: Do not skip this for a product with no standardised UI yet; use an interactive walkthrough then.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): no count; gemini attributes the claim to a UX research firm, unverified here.

rule: Option: place an ungated try-it with a sample and a bring-your-own local mode in or just below the hero visual, so a skeptical visitor can test the result with no account.
do: Offer a short guided sample first and a paste-or-drop mode that stays local or ephemeral, with no form fields before the first run.
dont: Do not use it for inputs that need destructive changes or multi-minute provisioning; use prepared fixtures instead.
values: Option values: Option values: about 60 s guided flow, 0 required fields before first run.
scope: needs a real local engine; with no backend the inspectable sample is the try-it.

rule: Put concrete risk-reversal and data-handling lines directly under the primary call to action, not only in the footer, and keep them specific.
do: Use a 12-13px helper line (13px preferred) a short distance under the button, for example "No credit card required", "Sample data stays in your browser" if true.
dont: Do not use vague lines such as "Trusted by leaders", do not shrink the helper line below 12px, and do not state a data claim that is not true.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): helper 12-13px, margin-top about 12-40px (gemini example).

rule: Distribute trust signals by the visitor doubt stage across four zones instead of one block: friction lines under the hero call to action, an ungated sample below the hero, a data-flow section mid-page, and trust, changelog and roadmap links in nav and footer.
do: Place a concise data-flow diagram (client boundary, encrypted transit, processing scope, deletion path) of 3-4 labelled nodes after the product capabilities and link a security page.
dont: Do not put the dense diagram above the fold, where it competes with the value proposition, and do not cram compliance wording into the headline.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): four zones; 3-4 diagram nodes; placement is a gemini synthesis, not a documented standard.

rule: Option: Show a "last shipped" pill or the latest two or three dated milestones near the hero or proof band only if the changelog is kept current.
do: Link the pill to the dated changelog entry and remove it if the entry is old.
dont: Do not leave a changelog stale for months, it signals abandonment; do not backfill invented entries.
values: Option values: latest 2-3 entries; refresh cadence is an authoring choice.
scope: A concept has no 'true today'. State the design policy in plain present tense; no audit, cipher, customer or changelog claims; one disclosure (AR42); only links that resolve on the page.
