rule: Put a keyboard-focusable skip link before any long pinned track so keyboard and screen-reader users can bypass the whole sequence in one action.
do: Make the skip link visible in the scene head, not focus-only: pointer users and screenshot reviews need it too.
dont: Do not add it to short, non-pinned sections with only a couple of controls, and do not use it instead of accessible content inside the scene.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate threshold: tracks of about 200vh or more; WCAG 2.4.1 (Bypass Blocks) is the criterion cited by gemini.

rule: Pair scroll scrubbing in a long pinned scene with step controls (previous, next and direct step buttons) that scroll to each step offset, and make them keyboard-operable.
do: Build real buttons or a tablist with Left and Right arrows, Home and End, scroll the page to the step offset, and mark the active step with `aria-current="step"`.
dont: Do not adopt carousel semantics for a continuous scroll narrative that does not behave like a carousel, and do not add paging to decorative micro-parallax.
values: keys ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Home, End; the WAI tab example gives no scroll distance or paging interval.

rule: If a stepped showcase auto-advances, give it a pause control, stop it on keyboard focus and hover, and do not auto-advance copy-heavy walkthroughs at all.
do: Add a play and pause button whose label toggles, pause on focus and hover, and set `aria-live="polite"` only while the visitor pages manually.
dont: Do not apply this to a scene that moves only with the visitor scroll; WCAG 2.2.2 covers automatic movement that lasts longer than five seconds next to other content.
values: 5 s threshold (WCAG 2.2.2); no recommended pause duration.

rule: Keep the native wheel and trackpad scroll speed and inertia untouched, and place a pinned narrative below the fold rather than locking the first viewport.
do: Let the page scroll one to one, with pinned stages starting after the first viewport and step or skip controls available.
dont: Do not override wheel deltas, and do not cite an attention-above-the-fold percentage as fact without a source.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): gemini cites 80% of attention above the fold; unverified here, not used as a threshold.
disagrees: scrollytelling showcases rely on 300-400vh pinned narratives while usability research on scrolljacking warns that overriding scroll mechanics hurts task success; keep native scroll physics, place the scene below the fold and add skip and step controls.

rule: Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, drop the pinned runway and render the steps as a calm stacked list, with no empty scroll track left behind.
do: Gate sticky scrubbing in a no-preference query, and in the reduce branch set `animation: none; animation-timeline: auto`, remove the tall track and show all steps at full opacity.
dont: Do not leave a 300vh-400vh empty track active when animations are off, and do not apply WCAG 2.3.3 as a blanket AA requirement, it is AAA with an essential-animation exception.
values: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` gate; no duration cap in the sources.

rule: Guard scroll-driven rules with `@supports (animation-timeline: view())`, check current Firefox support at release rather than relying on an old claim, and make the unsupported branch a readable static layout.
do: Put every `opacity: 0` or pinned base style inside the `@supports` block, and let the fallback show `opacity: 1; transform: none`.
dont: Do not ship `opacity: 0` base styles outside the `@supports` block, and do not assert that Firefox categorically lacks support.
values: MDN compat data retrieved on 2026-11-23 lists Firefox support from version 159; gemini says October 2026, not verified; support changes over time. Version comes from compat data; release status not verified. Test the installed build with `CSS.supports`; gate by feature only.

rule: Avoid shipping a scroll-timeline polyfill on a production landing page; fall back to an IntersectionObserver entrance or a static stack, and use a passive scroll listener only for a stage that truly needs scrubbing.
do: When `!CSS.supports("animation-timeline", "view()")` use a discrete observer with a low threshold or an unpinned layout; compute progress as `-rect.top / (scrollHeight - innerHeight)` in a passive `rAF` listener for essential scrub stages.
dont: Do not attach an IntersectionObserver inside a tall sticky track whose items stay off screen, and do not assume a script path is faster or more reliable without measuring.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): observer threshold about .1; polyfill concerns (main-thread rAF, cross-origin stylesheets, range syntax drift) are from gemini and were not verified.
disagrees: tutorials document a scroll-timeline polyfill for older browsers; gemini reports it is a production risk (main-thread loop, stylesheet CORS, syntax drift); codex only says do not assume script is better without measuring.

rule: If a stepped pinned track needs snapping, prefer `proximity` over `mandatory`, and do not add snap to a root scroller with a sticky stage unless it was tested with a real wheel.
do: Use `scroll-snap-type: y proximity` on a dedicated container, test mouse wheel and trackpad separately, and keep each step no taller than the viewport.
dont: Do not use `mandatory` on tracks with steps taller than 100vh or for freeform drag and scrollbar users.
values: `y proximity`; project evidence that a root snap with a sticky stage trapped the wheel.

rule: Treat 1024-1199px as its own layout tier; set breakpoints where the content stops fitting, not at a device label, and recompose the hero from measured wrapping, column width and CTA fit.
do: Tighten outer padding and column gap in this band before widening at 1200px or 1280px, and test at 1024, 1100, 1199 and 1280.
dont: Do not take a framework default breakpoint as proof the hero works, and do not credit a named site with these values without inspecting its CSS.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate: container padding 24-32px, column gap about 32px at 1024-1199px, about 64px from 1280px; the two frameworks switch at different widths (992/1200 and 1024/1280). project evidence (DIRECT, L591, L593): an eyebrow right-aligned under the h1 read as floating, a note on the CTA row as stranded.
disagrees: one framework moves from large to extra-large at 1200px and another at 1280px, so 1200-1279px gets desktop styles in one and not in the other; tune the band explicitly instead of inheriting.

rule: Prefer flexible grid or flex layouts first, add a breakpoint only when content starts to look cramped, and stack rather than force two columns when the copy or the visual no longer fits.
do: Use fluid columns and `minmax()` with a minimum visual width, and stack below the width where the CTA row wraps.
dont: Do not change composition only because the viewport crossed a familiar device label.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate: stack below about 1100px for dashboards that need at least 560px of visual width; no verified threshold.

rule: In the 1024-1199px band prefer a 7/5 split (copy about 58%, visual about 42%) when the headline needs 44-56px size, and move to a 6/6 split only from 1200px or 1280px.
do: Use a 12-column grid with `grid-column: span 7` for copy and `span 5` for the visual, keep the visual at least about 400-460px wide.
dont: Do not use it when the visual needs 560px or more, then stack below about 1100px or cap the copy column.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate 7/5 (58.3% / 41.7%); visual min width 400-460px.

rule: Cap hero subheads in a two-column layout to a readable line length so lines do not collide with the visual gutter.
do: Set `max-width: 60ch` to `70ch` (about 66ch ideal) on the subheadline and body copy.
dont: Do not apply it to short display kickers or to narrow sidebars where it gives three-word lines.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate 45-75 characters per line, 66ch target; typographers differ (45-75 versus up to 90).
disagrees: one typographer and a UX research firm give 45-75 characters per line while another allows up to 90; cap hero subcopy at 60-70ch to satisfy both.

rule: Scale the two-column hero H1 with `clamp()` so it grows smoothly through 1024-1199px instead of jumping from a mobile size to a very large size.
do: Use `clamp(2.25rem, 4vw, 3.75rem)` with line-height about 1.1 and trim copy that wraps beyond four lines.
dont: Do not use it in a centered single-column hero that can carry larger type at 1024px.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate: 36-60px range, about 41-48px inside 1024-1199px.

rule: Place the eyebrow label flush left directly above the H1 inside the copy column, short, and set so it cannot collide with the visual column.
do: Use an inline-flex pill at 12px or more, padding about 4px 12px, margin below about 24px, at most five words.
dont: Do not span the eyebrow across both columns, and do not duplicate an announcement bar directly above it.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate 12px, 4px 12px, 24px margin-bottom, up to 5 words. project evidence (DIRECT, L591, L593): an eyebrow right-aligned under the h1 read as floating, a note on the CTA row as stranded.

rule: Group the primary and secondary calls to action in one wrapping horizontal row and bind the friction note directly under it in the same column, so the buttons do not orphan or wrap awkwardly at 1024px.
do: Use `display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px` for the buttons and a 12-13px note below with about 12-40px of space; 13px preferred.
dont: Do not put the trust note in the visual column, away from the call to action.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate gap 16px, button padding about 14px 24px, note 12px; codex: no source-verified CTA-note spacing. project evidence (DIRECT, L591, L593): an eyebrow right-aligned under the h1 read as floating, a note on the CTA row as stranded.

rule: Vertically center the two hero columns and cap the visual height in 1024-1199px so the H1, primary call to action, note and product frame fit above a 768-800px laptop fold.
do: Use `align-items: center`, section padding about 96-128px and a visual about 320-380px tall.
dont: Do not place tall vertical phone mockups in this band, they push the hero past 900px.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): candidate visual height 320-380px, section padding 96-128px.

rule: Define repeated waveform, grid or ruler artwork once in an SVG `symbol` and instantiate it with `<use>` when the instances share the same geometry, passing colors through inherited custom properties.
do: Put the geometry in `<defs><symbol id viewBox>`, stamp it with `<use href="#id">`, and set `--tick-color` style custom properties on the `<svg>` or `<use>`, because they inherit into the use shadow tree. The shared source is the data (seconds), not the artwork: each instance snaps to its own tick grid (L940 vs L1000-1002, DIRECT).
dont: Do not use it where each instance needs independent geometry or animated inner bars, descendant selectors do not reach into the use shadow tree.
values: `width` and `height` on `<use>` apply only when the referenced symbol has a `viewBox`; no instance limit is documented.

rule: Pair a stretched symbol with `vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"` so tick and waveform strokes stay 1-1.5px at every width.
do: Use `preserveAspectRatio="none"` on the stretched symbol and `vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"` on each `<line>` and `<path>`.
dont: Do not use it for icons where the stroke is meant to scale with size.
values: stroke-width 1 or 1.5; widths from 320px to 1440px.

rule: Generate a uniform tick ruler from custom properties and layered `repeating-linear-gradient()` backgrounds, with no extra DOM nodes.
do: Define `--tick-width`, `--tick-spacing` and `--major-tick-interval` and stack a minor and a major gradient. The shared source is the data (seconds), not the artwork: each instance snaps to its own tick grid (L940 vs L1000-1002, DIRECT).
dont: Do not use it for non-periodic waveforms or curved gauges.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): example minor 1px every 10px, major 3px every 50px.
disagrees: SVG `use` reuse and CSS repeating gradients solve different cases; neither source gives a benchmark (codex: no comparative benchmark found), so choose by shape: gradients for uniform ticks, symbol for static waveforms, one path or inline bars only when individual bars animate.

rule: Generate variable waveforms from one deterministic sample array so mini-map, card and scrubber instances stay identical, and never from `Math.random()` in render.
do: Map a normalised [0..1] array to path coordinates in one `viewBox` or to `--amp` custom properties, built by one helper shared by every instance. The shared source is the data (seconds), not the artwork: each instance snaps to its own tick grid (L940 vs L1000-1002, DIRECT).
dont: Do not use random values in render (hydration mismatch), and do not draw more than a few hundred animated bars when one path will do.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): canonical `viewBox="0 0 1000 100"` is an example; no verified bar ceiling.

rule: One state at a time (DIRECT, L854-859): the outgoing state reaches 0 before the incoming leaves 0; gap >= 16px; each fade >= 100px; hold >= handoff.
do: Bring the outgoing state to opacity 0 before the incoming one leaves 0, with a gap of at least 16px, fades of at least 100px and a hold at least as long as the handoff.
dont: Do not let two states have positive opacity at the same scroll position.
values: Gap >= 16px; fade >= 100px; hold >= handoff. See manual-motion-tokens for the v10 table.

rule: One clock for every picture of the same data (DIRECT, L940 vs L1002): position = seconds / total, snapped to the instance's own grid; instances differ by at most half a pitch.
do: Derive every picture of the same data from one seconds value, position = seconds / total, snapped to the instance's own tick grid.
dont: Do not hand-place the same event separately in each picture.
values: Instances differ by at most half a pitch.

rule: Panels are sized by content (DIRECT, L803, L806, L837, L842): no viewport-fitted height on a fixed panel; free space <= 16px; every DOM row shows at the top tier; slack goes to content, never to padding.
do: Size fixed panels by their content, keep free space at 16px or less, show every DOM row at the top tier and spend slack on content.
dont: Do not fit a fixed panel's height to the viewport or absorb slack in padding.
values: Free space <= 16px per panel state.

rule: Eyebrow and note attach (DIRECT, L591, L593): eyebrow above the headline, flush left; friction note directly under the CTA; nothing sits alone right-aligned on a row.
do: Put the eyebrow flush left above the headline and the friction note directly under the CTA.
dont: Do not right-align an eyebrow under the h1 or park a note beside the CTA row.
values: Eyebrow above h1, flush left; note under CTA.

rule: One stand-out moment: one physical change of the product's own data unit; reserved zone, no text in its sweep; transform and opacity only; frame 0 at scrollY 0 and the last frame are clean rests; the last frame is the static, no-SDA and reduced-motion frame.
do: Give the page one physical change of its own data unit in a reserved zone, animate transform and opacity only, and make frame 0 and the last frame clean rests.
dont: Do not put text inside the sweep or add a second stand-out moment.
values: Last frame = static, no-SDA and reduced-motion frame.

rule: Concept trust: four facts in plain words (what is recorded, where it is processed, who sees it, when it is deleted), consistent with the plan table, plus one honest limit; nothing that implies an audit or a customer.
do: State what is recorded, where it is processed, who sees it and when it is deleted in plain words, match the plan table, and add one honest limit.
dont: Do not imply an audit, a certification or a customer.
values: Four facts plus one limit.

rule: Pins of 200svh or more: visible skip link, step buttons with arrow keys, feature detection only, tested in the real browser; no polyfill, no snap, no wheel code.
do: On a pin of 200svh or more add a visible skip link and step buttons with arrow keys, gate by feature detection and test in the real browser.
dont: Do not add a polyfill, scroll snap or wheel handlers.
values: Pin >= 200svh triggers the rule.

rule: De-familiarise by subtraction: per iteration change one hue of the 60% and one face; emphasis uses the page's own device, never an italic word with a drawn underline.
do: Per iteration change one hue of the 60% and one typeface, and emphasise with the page's own device.
dont: Do not emphasise with an italic word plus a drawn underline.
values: One hue and one face per iteration.

rule: Establish a proportional border-radius token scale anchored to a single root variable or 4px geometric progression so small controls, medium cards, and large modals scale cohesively.
do: Establish a proportional border-radius token scale anchored to a single root variable or 4px geometric progression so small controls, medium cards, and large modals
dont: Do not apply rounded radii (>0px) to full-bleed viewport containers, edge-to-edge sticky top bars, or flush table cells where corner gaps create visual leaks. | Geist (codex): 6px for base/small materials and 12px for medium/large/menu/modal; codex notes the source gives no full radius scale and platform shapes may override.
values: Fluent 2 enterprise scale: None=0px (nav/tab bars), Small=2px (badges <32px), Medium=4px (buttons/inputs), Large=8px (cards), X-Large=12px (flyouts/sheets), Circle=50% (avatars); Shopify Polaris scale: --p-border-radius-100=4px, -200=8px, -300=12px, -400=16px; shadcn/ui radius math: --radius=0.625rem (10px), --radius-sm=calc(var(--radius) - 4px) (6px), --radius-md=calc(var(--radius) - 2px) (8px), --radius-lg=var(--radius) (10px), --radius-xl=calc(var(--radius) + 4px) (14px).

rule: Scale expressive, touch-first surfaces above the standard radius scale using additional 'increased' tokens (Material 3 Expressive adds 20dp, 32dp, 48dp); shape morphing is native-only.
do: Scale expressive, touch-first surfaces above the standard radius scale using additional 'increased' tokens (Material 3 Expressive adds 20dp, 32dp, 48dp); shape morph
dont: Do not use 20-48dp radii on dense desktop data grids, financial terminals or compact inputs (<36px high). context: choose radius by density profile, not vendor: dense productivity profile (Fluent 2, 2-12px) vs expressive consumer profile (larger radii).
values: Material 3 Expressive: standard tokens XS 4dp, S 8dp, M 12dp, L 16dp, XL 28dp, plus additional 'increased' tokens 20dp, 32dp, 48dp; Full = capsule. Shape morph on state change is a native (Compose/Android) feature, not a web default.

rule: Derive a nested child radius from its parent as inner = outer - padding with a floor of 4px; if padding >= outer, use the next scale step down.
do: Derive a nested child radius from its parent as inner = outer - padding with a floor of 4px; if padding >= outer, use the next scale step down.
dont: Do not apply the subtraction when sibling elements separate the child from the parent corner. context: derived geometry, not a vendor-documented formula; the sources consulted only document 'child radius <= parent radius'. Merged from research2-codex-1.
values: inner = max(4px, outer - padding); if padding >= outer pick the next token one step down the radius scale. Example: outer 20px, padding 8px -> inner 12px; outer 8px, padding 12px -> next step down (4px).

rule: In native SwiftUI apps, align top-level container corners to the device/window curvature with container-concentric geometry; on the web use the nested-radius rule instead.
do: In native SwiftUI apps, align top-level container corners to the device/window curvature with container-concentric geometry; on the web use the nested-radius rule in
dont: Do not use hardware-concentric radii on interior elements far from screen bezels or parent corners. Not available in CSS.
values: Native SwiftUI only: .rect(cornerRadius: .containerConcentric) / ConcentricRectangle derive inner radii from the container or device corner radius minus inset.

rule: Shape floating navigation bars, primary touch pills, and status badges as full capsules by setting the corner radius to at least half of the element's height.
do: Shape floating navigation bars, primary touch pills, and status badges as full capsules by setting the corner radius to at least half of the element's height.
dont: Do not use capsule (9999px) radii on multi-line text containers, tall cards, or expandable accordions, where a 9999px radius distorts vertical edges into an oval stadium shape.
values: Capsule radius: border-radius: 9999px (CSS) or CornerRadius = Height / 2 (e.g., a 44pt high floating tab bar or button uses a 22pt corner radius; a 24px badge uses a 12px radius).

rule: Apply continuous squircle (superellipse) corner smoothing rather than standard circular arcs on large app icons, hardware-adjacent modals, and hero cards to eliminate the abrupt tangent jump between straight edges and curves.
do: Apply continuous squircle (superellipse) corner smoothing rather than standard circular arcs on large app icons, hardware-adjacent modals, and hero cards to eliminate
dont: Do not use SVG clip-path squircle hacks on dynamic-height containers or scrollable tables where clip-path breaks sub-pixel border anti-aliasing and overflow scrolling.
values: Continuous (squircle) corners via Figma corner smoothing or an SVG shape for icons; CSS corner-shape: squircle is Chromium-only, so use it as progressive enhancement over a border-radius: 16px-24px fallback.

rule: Build soft light-mode elevation by stacking several (heuristic: 3-5) comma-separated box-shadow layers whose offsets and blur grow per layer with low alpha.
do: Build soft light-mode elevation by stacking several (heuristic: 3-5) comma-separated box-shadow layers whose offsets and blur grow per layer with low alpha.
dont: Do not use single-layer high-opacity black shadows (e.g., 0 10px 15px rgba(0,0,0,0.3)) or apply multi-layer drop shadows to dark-mode surfaces where shadows muddy the background.
values: heuristic: Tobias Ahlin 'smooth shadows' technique: layer offsets and blur roughly double per layer, per-layer alpha low (about 0.03-0.10); low elevation 2-3 layers, high elevation (modals) more layers. The basic recipe remains the 2-layer shadow.

rule: Tint shadow layers using the underlying surface's HSL/OKLCH hue at reduced saturation and low lightness rather than neutral black so shadows blend naturally with colored backgrounds.
do: Tint shadow layers using the underlying surface's HSL/OKLCH hue at reduced saturation and low lightness rather than neutral black so shadows blend naturally with colored
dont: Do not use heavily saturated shadow tints (>50% saturation) or mix inconsistent X/Y offset angles across components on the same screen.
values: Shadow color formula: hsl(var(--surface-hue) 40% 13% / 0.04 to 0.10) or oklch(0.20 0.04 var(--surface-hue) / 0.06) instead of rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25), keeping light source direction fixed across the entire UI (typically top-lit: X-offset = 0px, Y-offset > 0px).

rule: Combine a sharp directional key shadow with a broader diffused ambient shadow across a constrained 4-to-6 step elevation ramp to separate resting cards from floating overlays.
do: Combine a sharp directional key shadow with a broader diffused ambient shadow across a constrained 4-to-6 step elevation ramp to separate resting cards from floating
dont: Do not assign Shadow 16–64 to static inline cards, as high-elevation shadows make non-interactive page sections look like unclosed modal popups. | codex: use at least two shadow layers (ambient + directional); do not use shadow as the only state or focus signal.
values: Fluent 2 & Refactoring UI dual-shadow scale: Shadow 2 (resting card/button): 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.14), 0 0px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.12); Shadow 4 (grid/list item): 0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.14), 0 0px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.12); Shadow 8 (command bar/card hover): 0 4px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.14), 0 0px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.12); Shadow 16 (dropdown/flyout): 0 8px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.14), 0 0px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.12); Shadow 64 (modal dialog): 0 32px 64px rgba(0,0,0,0.24), 0 0px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.20).

rule: Structure application Z-space into four semantic elevation tiers—Sunken, Default, Raised, and Overlay—so every component maps to a predictable depth role.
do: Structure application Z-space into four semantic elevation tiers—Sunken, Default, Raised, and Overlay—so every component maps to a predictable depth role.
dont: Do not nest more than 3 distinct elevation tiers within a single component tree (e.g., an overlay inside a raised card inside another raised card).
values: Atlassian Design System elevation tokens: 1. elevation.surface.sunken (recessed wells, Kanban columns, code blocks); 2. elevation.surface (default page canvas, 0dp); 3. elevation.surface.raised + elevation.shadow.raised (draggable cards, elevated tiles); 4. elevation.surface.overlay + elevation.shadow.overlay (modals, dropdown menus, popovers, floating toolbars).

rule: Pair card shadows with a 1px structural border ring to keep crisp edges on low-contrast surfaces; an inset top-edge highlight is an optional extra.
do: Pair card shadows with a 1px structural border ring to keep crisp edges on low-contrast surfaces; an inset top-edge highlight is an optional extra.
dont: Do not apply a top-edge white bevel highlight to sunken/recessed input wells, where the top inner edge should be slightly darker (inset shadow) rather than highlighted.
values: heuristic: Shopify Polaris & modern SaaS card recipe: box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.15), 0 0 0 1px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.06), 0 2px 4px -1px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.06) (in dark mode: inset 0 1px 0 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08), 0 0 0 1px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.07)).

rule: Separate surfaces with a 1px low-opacity hairline: in dark themes add a surface lightness step and use shadows only on overlays; in light themes pair the hairline with a low 2-layer shadow.
do: Separate surfaces with a 1px low-opacity hairline: in dark themes add a surface lightness step and use shadows only on overlays; in light themes pair the hairline wi
dont: Do not rely on a hairline alone for floating overlays (menus, popovers, modals) over varied content. context: layered shadows + bevels (Fluent 2, Polaris) vs hairline-first (Linear, Geist) is a theme/density choice, not a vendor choice.
values: heuristic: light hairline 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.08); dark hairline 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.06-0.08); dark surface step = next surface-container lightness; light low shadow = 2 layers, e.g. 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.06), 0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.06).

rule: Simulate physical directional illumination on hero cards and feature borders by applying a 1px fading linear-gradient along the top edge rather than wrapping the entire border in a loud gradient.
do: Simulate physical directional illumination on hero cards and feature borders by applying a 1px fading linear-gradient along the top edge rather than wrapping the entire
dont: Do not apply specular gradient borders to every list row, table cell, or secondary form input, which turns a subtle lighting cue into visual clutter.
values: heuristic: Top specular border highlight: height: 1px; background: linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(255,255,255,0) 0%, rgba(255,255,255,0.22) 50%, rgba(255,255,255,0) 100%); paired with a subtle top-down surface wash background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.04) 0%, rgba(255,255,255,0) 100%).

rule: Interpolate multi-stop CSS gradients in the perceptual OKLCH or Oklab color space so transitions between hues maintain uniform lightness without a muddy gray midpoint.
do: Interpolate multi-stop CSS gradients in the perceptual OKLCH or Oklab color space so transitions between hues maintain uniform lightness without a muddy gray midpoint.
dont: Do not interpolate complementary hues (180deg apart) across full chroma in oklch without a muted intermediate stop, as it creates hyper-saturated neon bands unsuitable for functional product UI.
values: CSS Color Level 4 syntax: background: linear-gradient(in oklch 135deg, oklch(0.65 0.18 250), oklch(0.72 0.16 190)); keep analogous hues and avoid saturated complementary stops.

rule: Cap ambient background radial glow opacity at 0.06 to 0.12 with a large diffusion radius (>= 400px) so atmospheric lighting supports hierarchy without reducing foreground text contrast.
do: Cap ambient background radial glow opacity at 0.06 to 0.12 with a large diffusion radius (>= 400px) so atmospheric lighting supports hierarchy without reducing
dont: Do not place colored glows behind dense long-form reading paragraphs, data tables, or code editors where luminance shifts fatigue the eye. | codex (CANDIDATE): gradient/glow supports hierarchy, not decoration on every element; no source-verified numeric value.
values: Ambient glow recipe: background: radial-gradient(600px circle at 50% 0%, oklch(0.65 0.15 var(--brand-hue) / 0.08), transparent 70%); or pointer-tracked card spotlight: radial-gradient(400px circle at var(--mouse-x) var(--mouse-y), rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06), transparent 40%).

rule: Restrict gradient text fills to short display headlines (heuristic: <= 6 words at >= 36px) using a subtle luminance fade within one hue family.
do: Restrict gradient text fills to short display headlines (heuristic: <= 6 words at >= 36px) using a subtle luminance fade within one hue family.
dont: Never apply background-clip: text gradients to body copy, interactive links, sub-24px headings, or multi-line paragraphs where gradient stops reduce contrast below WCAG thresholds.
values: heuristic: background: linear-gradient(180deg, #FFFFFF 0%, rgba(255,255,255,0.68) 100%) (dark) or linear-gradient(180deg, #111111 0%, #555555 100%) (light) with -webkit-background-clip: text; color: transparent; the lowest-opacity stop must still meet WCAG 4.5:1.

rule: Restrict translucent glass materials strictly to the floating control and navigation layer (tab bars, toolbars, command palettes, transient popovers) and never apply them to content-layer cards, tables, or background containers.
do: Restrict translucent glass materials strictly to the floating control and navigation layer (tab bars, toolbars, command palettes, transient popovers) and never apply
dont: Never stack glass-on-glass (e.g., a translucent card inside a translucent container) or apply glass blur to primary reading containers and data tables. | codex: Apple gives no universal numeric blur/transparency threshold.
values: Apple HIG Liquid Glass (2025) architectural rule: Layer 1 (Content layer: lists, articles, data grids, standard cards) = opaque surface materials; Layer 2 (Floating control layer: TabView, Toolbar, floating action pills, active sliders/toggles) = Liquid Glass / translucent blur material floating above content.

rule: Pair CSS backdrop-filter blur (12px-24px) with a surface tint verified by testing composited text contrast against the worst-case backdrop that can scroll behind it (WCAG 4.5:1).
do: Pair CSS backdrop-filter blur (12px-24px) with a surface tint verified by testing composited text contrast against the worst-case backdrop that can scroll behind it
dont: Do not ship a glass surface with text without compositing the text colour over the brightest and darkest content that can sit behind it. context: tint opacity 0.05-0.15 is acceptable only on text-free decoration, never behind text.
values: heuristic starting recipe, always verify: Light: background rgba(255,255,255,0.75); backdrop-filter: blur(16px) saturate(180%); border 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.08). Dark: background rgba(18,19,22,0.65); backdrop-filter: blur(16px) saturate(160%); border 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12). No universal tint threshold exists.

rule: Provide an opaque surface fallback using @media (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce) and @supports (backdrop-filter: blur(12px)) so users with visual impairments or unsupported GPUs receive a high-contrast solid surface.
do: Provide an opaque surface fallback using @media (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce) and @supports (backdrop-filter: blur(12px)) so users with visual impairments or
dont: Never ship a translucent background rgba() without an @supports or prefers-reduced-transparency override, as unblurred semi-transparent text over text is unreadable. | codex: use clear variants only over visually rich backgrounds and test with reduce-transparency/increase-contrast settings.
values: CSS fallback pattern: Default background-color: rgb(245, 245, 247) (light) / rgb(24, 25, 28) (dark); inside @supports (backdrop-filter: blur(12px)) or (-webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(12px)) apply translucent rgba() and blur; inside @media (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce) enforce backdrop-filter: none; background-color: var(--solid-surface); border-color: var(--solid-border);.

rule: Limit active backdrop-filter regions (heuristic: at most 2 concurrent per viewport) and keep blur radii modest (heuristic: <= 24px) to protect scroll frame rate.
do: Limit active backdrop-filter regions (heuristic: at most 2 concurrent per viewport) and keep blur radii modest (heuristic: <= 24px) to protect scroll frame rate.
dont: Do not animate backdrop-filter: blur() radius values continuously on scroll or apply backdrop-filter to dozens of repeating list items/cards in a scrollable feed.
values: heuristic GPU budget: <= 2 active backdrop-filter layers; blur 8px-24px, saturate(140%-180%); cost grows quickly with radius on mobile GPUs (heuristic: degrades above 24px). Apple's native Liquid Glass shader internals are UNVERIFIED for web replication.

rule: Map every neutral and accent hue onto a 12-step semantic scale where each index has a fixed functional UI role across both light and dark modes.
do: Map every neutral and accent hue onto a 12-step semantic scale where each index has a fixed functional UI role across both light and dark modes.
dont: Do not use Steps 9–10 for large container backgrounds or use Steps 6–8 for text, as they violate the contrast architecture of the scale. | codex: define colour by semantic role and use the same colour consistently for the same meaning.
values: Radix Colors 12-step architecture: Step 1 = App background; Step 2 = Subtle background (sidebars/cards/striped rows); Step 3 = UI component resting background; Step 4 = Hovered component background; Step 5 = Active/selected component background; Step 6 = Subtle borders/dividers; Step 7 = UI element border & focus rings; Step 8 = Hovered UI element border; Step 9 = Solid accent background (primary buttons/badges); Step 10 = Hovered solid accent background; Step 11 = Low-contrast secondary text (advisory APCA Lc >= 60); Step 12 = High-contrast primary text (advisory APCA Lc >= 90).

rule: Alternatively, when using a 10-step functional token scale, assign Steps 1–3 to component surfaces, Steps 4–6 to borders, Steps 7–8 to high-contrast solid fills, and Steps 9–10 to secondary and primary text.
do: Alternatively, when using a 10-step functional token scale, assign Steps 1–3 to component surfaces, Steps 4–6 to borders, Steps 7–8 to high-contrast solid fills, and
dont: Do not mix 10-step (Geist/Tailwind) and 12-step (Radix) numbering indices within the same token namespace without semantic aliases (e.g., --bg-subtle, --border-default, --text-primary).
values: Vercel Geist 10-step color system: Background 1 & 2 (page canvas: #FFFFFF / #FAFAFA in light, #000000 / #0A0A0A in dark); Steps 1–3 = default/hover/active component backgrounds; Steps 4–6 = default/hover/active borders; Steps 7–8 = solid high-contrast fills; Step 9 = secondary text/icons; Step 10 = primary high-contrast text.

rule: Define design system color tokens in OKLCH so equal numeric lightness steps are perceptually more uniform than in HSL.
do: Define design system color tokens in OKLCH so equal numeric lightness steps are perceptually more uniform than in HSL.
dont: Do not use HSL lightness (L%) to algorithmically generate multi-hue status palettes (yellow vs blue at 50% HSL lightness have a >3x perceived luminance difference, breaking text contrast).
values: OKLCH syntax: oklch(L C H), L 0-1, C 0-~0.37, H 0-360. shadcn/ui OKLCH tokens: --background: oklch(1 0 0), --foreground: oklch(0.145 0 0), --border: oklch(0.922 0 0).

rule: Infuse neutral gray scales with a subtle trace of chroma (0.004 to 0.015 in OKLCH) matched to the primary brand hue or a warm slate angle to prevent sterile, lifeless interfaces.
do: Infuse neutral gray scales with a subtle trace of chroma (0.004 to 0.015 in OKLCH) matched to the primary brand hue or a warm slate angle to prevent sterile, lifeless
dont: Do not push neutral gray chroma above C = 0.020 in OKLCH, or the entire application background will appear overtly colored rather than neutral.
values: heuristic: Warm/cool tinted neutral recipe: Cool slate gray: oklch(L 0.010 255); Warm charcoal/stone gray (Linear 2024–2025 shift): oklch(L 0.006 80) or hex ramp #08090a -> #0f1011 -> #141516 -> #18191a; pure achromatic gray (C = 0) reserved only for stark Swiss-minimalist themes like Vercel Geist.

rule: Style semantic badges, callouts, and alert banners using a very low-saturation tinted background (Step 2–3) paired with deep high-contrast text of the same hue (Step 11–12) rather than solid saturated fills.
do: Style semantic badges, callouts, and alert banners using a very low-saturation tinted background (Step 2–3) paired with deep high-contrast text of the same hue (Step
dont: Do not use soft pastel fills for the single primary call-to-action button on a page or critical destructive confirmation buttons that require maximum visual weight (Step 9 solid fill).
values: Refactoring UI & Radix soft badge formula: Light mode: background = Step 3 (oklch(0.94 0.04 H)), border = Step 6 (oklch(0.85 0.07 H)), text = Step 11 (oklch(0.38 0.14 H)); Dark mode: background = Step 3 (oklch(0.22 0.04 H)), border = Step 6 (oklch(0.32 0.07 H)), text = Step 11 (oklch(0.82 0.10 H)), achieving >= 4.5:1 text contrast.

rule: Enforce a 60-30-10 spatial color distribution where neutral surfaces occupy ~60% of the viewport, secondary containers/borders/muted text occupy ~30%, and high-chroma brand/status accents occupy at most 10%.
do: Enforce a 60-30-10 spatial color distribution where neutral surfaces occupy ~60% of the viewport, secondary containers/borders/muted text occupy ~30%, and high-chroma
dont: Do not apply high-chroma brand colors to large navigation sidebars, top headers, and card backgrounds simultaneously, which exhausts visual attention and hides primary actions.
values: Viewport area budget: >= 60% primary/secondary neutral canvas (C <= 0.015), ~30% structural containers, sidebars, and secondary typography, <= 10% high-chroma accent tokens (C >= 0.12) reserved for primary CTAs, active indicators, focus rings, and status alerts.

rule: Default to off-black dark surfaces and off-white body text; use #000000 only as an explicit art-direction choice or for sunken wells.
do: Default to off-black dark surfaces and off-white body text; use #000000 only as an explicit art-direction choice or for sunken wells.
dont: Do not mechanically invert the light palette; use semantic tokens per theme. context: Geist uses true black on marketing/OLED layouts; claims that pure black causes OLED smear or eye strain are weakly evidenced, so treat off-black as a default, not a requirement.
values: Off-black dark canvas range #08090A to #121316 (OKLCH L 0.14-0.19, e.g. shadcn/ui oklch(0.145 0 0); Material 3 dark surface #141218). Off-white text e.g. #EDEDEF to #F4F4F6; #000000 only for sunken wells or explicit art direction.

rule: Communicate elevation in dark mode by progressively lightening surface container colors as Z-depth increases rather than relying on dark drop shadows.
do: Communicate elevation in dark mode by progressively lightening surface container colors as Z-depth increases rather than relying on dark drop shadows.
dont: Do not invert this logic by making elevated modals or cards darker than the page canvas in dark mode, which makes floating overlays look like holes cut into the screen. | codex: do not assume added shadows give readable depth on very dark backgrounds.
values: heuristic: Atlassian-style dark surface ramp (Sunken #101214, Canvas #161A1D, Raised #1D2125, Overlay #22272B); Material 3 dark surface container ramp as example hexes (lowest #0F0D13, low #1D1B20, container #211F26, high #2B2930, highest #36343B). Principle: higher elevation = lighter surface.

rule: Desaturate and lighten primary brand and semantic accent colors in dark mode so they pass WCAG 4.5:1 against dark surfaces without optically vibrating.
do: Desaturate and lighten primary brand and semantic accent colors in dark mode so they pass WCAG 4.5:1 against dark surfaces without optically vibrating.
dont: Do not use full-saturation dark-toned light-mode brand colors (e.g., deep royal blue #1D4ED8 or dark red #B91C1C) as text or icons directly on a #121212 dark background, where contrast drops below 2.5:1. | codex: Apple recommends 7:1 for custom colors; 7:1 is not the general WCAG AA criterion.
values: Dark-mode accent adjustment: Increase OKLCH Lightness L by +0.10 to +0.18 and reduce Chroma C by 15%–25% (or in HSL, shift from 500/600 shade in light mode to 400/300 shade in dark mode, e.g., Blue-600 #2563EB on light -> Blue-400 #60A5FA on dark for text/links).

rule: Render sunken wells, form text inputs, and code blocks in dark mode using an opaque surface tone darker than the parent card or canvas so they appear physically recessed.
do: Render sunken wells, form text inputs, and code blocks in dark mode using an opaque surface tone darker than the parent card or canvas so they appear physically recessed.
dont: Do not make text inputs lighter than a raised modal card in dark mode if clickable buttons inside the same modal also rely on lighter surface fills, as inputs and buttons will become indistinguishable.
values: Sunken surface lightness delta: L_sunken = L_parent - 0.03 to 0.05 in OKLCH (e.g., parent card #18191A / oklch(0.21 0 0) -> recessed input or Kanban well #0F1011 / oklch(0.17 0 0) with border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08)). Atlassian token: elevation.surface.sunken darkens in both light and dark modes.

rule: Declare color-scheme on :root to match the themes the page really supports ('light dark' only when both themes exist; a single-theme page declares its one scheme); dimming bright raster images in dark mode is optional.
do: Declare color-scheme on :root to match the themes the page really supports ('light dark' only when both themes exist; a single-theme page declares its one scheme); d
dont: Do not apply brightness dimming to logos, SVGs, color-accurate product swatches, or transparent-background charts.
values: Both themes: :root { color-scheme: light dark; }. Single theme: :root { color-scheme: light; } (or dark). Optional dark-mode image dimming: @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { img:not([src$='.svg']) { filter: brightness(0.85) contrast(1.05); } }, with filter: none on :hover or in a lightbox.

rule: Define dark-mode borders and dividers using semi-transparent white alpha channels (rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06) to 0.14) so borders automatically adapt to any underlying surface container elevation.
do: Define dark-mode borders and dividers using semi-transparent white alpha channels (rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06) to 0.14) so borders automatically adapt to any underlying
dont: Do not use transparent borders on overlapping sticky table headers or sticky columns without an opaque background fill behind the cell, or scrolling content will bleed through the border.
values: Dark border alpha ramp: Subtle divider = rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06); Default card/input border = rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.10); Hovered component border = rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.18); Active/selected border = rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.28).

rule: Scale display and section headings fluidly across viewports using CSS clamp() with a preferred value that combines rem and vw units so browser zoom remains WCAG 1.4.4 compliant.
do: Scale display and section headings fluidly across viewports using CSS clamp() with a preferred value that combines rem and vw units so browser zoom remains WCAG 1.4.4
dont: Never use pure viewport units (e.g., font-size: 4vw without a rem term) because pure vw locks out user zoom scaling and fails WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text; do not fluidly scale dense dashboard table/form text below 14px (0.875rem). | codex: do not use a clamp formula that blocks user text zoom.
values: Fluid type scale recipes (320px to 1440px viewport): Hero Display: font-size: clamp(2.25rem, 1.5rem + 3vw, 4.5rem); H1: clamp(1.875rem, 1.35rem + 2vw, 3.25rem); H2: clamp(1.5rem, 1.2rem + 1.2vw, 2.25rem); H3: clamp(1.25rem, 1.1rem + 0.6vw, 1.625rem); Body copy remains stable at 1rem (16px) or 0.875rem (14px) for dense apps.

rule: Use a tracking ramp as the default for neutral grotesque headings: progressively negative em values as size grows above 24px, capped at -0.04em; halve the values for optical display cuts.
do: Use a tracking ramp as the default for neutral grotesque headings: progressively negative em values as size grows above 24px, capped at -0.04em; halve the values for
dont: Never apply negative tracking (< -0.01em) to small body text (<= 14px), monospace code, or all-caps labels. context: no source validates a universal tracking value; optical display cuts (opsz) already tighten spacing, so use roughly half the ramp.
values: Neutral grotesque ramp: Body 14-16px: 0em, line-height 1.5-1.6; Subheadings 18-22px: -0.01em to -0.015em, 1.3; H1/H2 24-40px: -0.02em to -0.03em, 1.15-1.2; Display 48px+: -0.03em to -0.04em (cap), 1.05-1.12. Optical display cuts: halve.

rule: Add positive letter-spacing (+0.04em to +0.08em) and medium/semibold weight (500–600) whenever rendering uppercase micro-labels, section kickers, or table column headers at 11px–12px.
do: Add positive letter-spacing (+0.04em to +0.08em) and medium/semibold weight (500–600) whenever rendering uppercase micro-labels, section kickers, or table column headers
dont: Do not set full sentences or multi-line descriptions in all-caps with positive tracking; all-caps weakens word-shape recognition.
values: Micro-label recipe: font-size: 0.75rem (12px) or 0.6875rem (11px); text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em to 0.08em; font-weight: 500 or 600; line-height: 1.33.

rule: Enable font-optical-sizing: auto on variable fonts; where a font exposes a Grade (GRAD) axis, lowering grade in dark mode can offset light-on-dark bloom.
do: Enable font-optical-sizing: auto on variable fonts; where a font exposes a Grade (GRAD) axis, lowering grade in dark mode can offset light-on-dark bloom.
dont: Do not reduce font weight below 400 (e.g., to 300 Light) on small dark-mode body text (<= 14px), as thin strokes fragment on standard 1x DPI non-Retina monitors. | codex (CANDIDATE): verify font support and legibility before relying on variable-font axes.
values: font-optical-sizing: auto adjusts the opsz axis to the font size. Use font-variation-settings: 'GRAD' only on fonts that expose it (e.g. Roboto Flex); Inter has no GRAD axis, so for fonts without it step weight down slightly instead.

rule: Anchor application UI typography to a constrained, documented type scale and cap reading line length between 60ch and 75ch.
do: Anchor application UI typography to a constrained, documented type scale and cap reading line length between 60ch and 75ch.
dont: Do not allow body paragraphs in documentation, modals, or marketing sections to stretch across a full 1200px–1440px container (>90ch), which causes users to lose their line position during return eye sweeps.
values: Atlassian Design System composite scale: Body Small = 12px/16px, Body Default = 14px/20px (app UI) or Body Large = 16px/24px (prose), Heading S = 16px/20px, Heading M = 20px/24px, Heading L = 24px/28px, Heading XL = 29px–32px/36px, Heading XXL = 35px–40px/44px; Prose measure: max-width: 65ch (range 60ch–75ch).

rule: As a progressive enhancement, apply text-wrap: balance to short headings and text-wrap: pretty to body paragraphs to reduce orphans.
do: As a progressive enhancement, apply text-wrap: balance to short headings and text-wrap: pretty to body paragraphs to reduce orphans.
dont: Do not apply text-wrap: balance to long-form paragraphs (>6 lines) or live-streaming chat/log containers, because browser line-balancing computation is capped at ~6 lines and adds layout recalculation overhead on large text blocks.
values: CSS Text Level 4 wrapping: h1, h2, h3, .card-title, blockquote { text-wrap: balance; } (equalizes line widths across up to 6 wrapped lines in Chromium/Safari/Firefox); p, .prose { text-wrap: pretty; } (prevents single-word orphan lines at paragraph endings).

rule: Construct bento layouts on a strict 3-column or 4-column CSS Grid with uniform 16px–24px gutters and a single dominant 2x2 (or 2x1) anchor cell positioned in the top-left F-pattern focal zone.
do: Construct bento layouts on a strict 3-column or 4-column CSS Grid with uniform 16px–24px gutters and a single dominant 2x2 (or 2x1) anchor cell positioned in the
dont: Do not give every bento cell the same 1x1 span (which reverts to a monotonous template grid) or create multiple competing 2x2 anchor cells in the same viewport fold. | codex (CANDIDATE): use asymmetric cards only when size reflects importance; bento is not required by the cited systems.
values: Bento grid CSS specification: display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr)); grid-auto-rows: minmax(180px, auto); gap: 16px (compact app) or 24px (marketing); Top-left hero anchor cell: grid-column: span 2; grid-row: span 2; (occupying 4 of 12 grid units in a 4x3 bento matrix).

rule: Scale internal card padding proportionally to cell span inside a bento grid so large 2x2 anchor tiles have generous breathing room while 1x1 tiles remain compact.
do: Scale internal card padding proportionally to cell span inside a bento grid so large 2x2 anchor tiles have generous breathing room while 1x1 tiles remain compact.
dont: Do not make external grid gaps wider than internal card padding (e.g., 32px gap with 12px padding), which visually fragments the card interior.
values: Bento padding hierarchy: 2x2 or 3x2 anchor cell padding = 28px–32px (1.75rem–2rem); 2x1 or 1x2 medium cell padding = 24px (1.5rem); 1x1 compact cell padding = 16px–20px (1rem–1.25rem); outer gutter gap = 16px–24px (always strictly less than or equal to internal cell padding so internal content groups coherently by Gestalt proximity).

rule: Ensure all multi-column and multi-row cell spans in an asymmetric bento grid sum mathematically to complete rows at every desktop and tablet breakpoint so no empty dead zones appear.
do: Ensure all multi-column and multi-row cell spans in an asymmetric bento grid sum mathematically to complete rows at every desktop and tablet breakpoint so no empty dead
dont: Do not use Pinterest-style waterfall masonry (columns: 3) for functional product bento grids or dashboard KPIs, as ragged bottom edges destroy horizontal scannability.
values: Complete row math examples: 4-column x 3-row matrix (12 units) = one 2x2 (4) + two 2x1 (4) + four 1x1 (4) = 12 units; 3-column x 2-row matrix (6 units) = one 2x1 (2) + one 1x1 (1) on Row 1, one 1x1 (1) + one 2x1 (2) on Row 2 (alternating 66%/33% and 33%/66% asymmetric zigzag). At tablet (768px–1023px), step down to a 2-column grid where 2x2/2x1 cells span 2 columns and 1x1 cells pair side-by-side.

rule: Collapse multi-span bento grids into a single-column vertical stack below 768px while preserving the exact HTML DOM source order for keyboard focus and screen readers.
do: Collapse multi-span bento grids into a single-column vertical stack below 768px while preserving the exact HTML DOM source order for keyboard focus and screen readers.
dont: Never use CSS order or explicit grid-row/grid-column placement to visually move a bottom-of-DOM element to the top-left visual slot if it contains interactive focusable controls.
values: Mobile breakpoint rule (< 768px): grid-template-columns: 1fr; with all child cells reset to grid-column: span 1 !important; grid-row: span 1 !important; without using CSS order or grid-auto-flow: dense rearrangements that violate WCAG 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence and 2.4.3 Focus Order.

rule: Frame embedded product screenshots and UI illustrations with a concentric border-radius and a 1px inset alpha border ring so dark or light edges inside the image never bleed into the page background.
do: Frame embedded product screenshots and UI illustrations with a concentric border-radius and a 1px inset alpha border ring so dark or light edges inside the image never
dont: Do not add an inset border ring to free-floating cutout illustrations or transparent 3D renders that are intentionally designed to float without a rectangular bounding box.
values: Screenshot framing recipe: border-radius: calc(var(--card-radius) - var(--card-padding)); outline: 1px solid rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08) (light mode) or outline: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.10) (dark mode); outline-offset: -1px; (or box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.1)).

rule: Declare explicit width, height, or CSS aspect-ratio with object-fit on media containers to reserve space and reduce Cumulative Layout Shift.
do: Declare explicit width, height, or CSS aspect-ratio with object-fit on media containers to reserve space and reduce Cumulative Layout Shift.
dont: Do not use object-fit: cover on technical architecture diagrams, charts, or full-screen product screenshots where cropping the outer edges deletes essential labels (use object-fit: contain instead).
values: aspect-ratio: 16 / 9 (video/hero), 4 / 3 (feature cards), 1 / 1 (avatars); object-fit: cover; object-position: center top for UI screenshots so top bars are not cropped; Core Web Vitals CLS target < 0.1.

rule: Serve raster imagery in modern AVIF and WebP formats with responsive srcset descriptors (1x, 2x, or width w descriptors), applying fetchpriority="high" to the single Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) hero asset and loading="lazy" to all below-the-fold media.
do: Serve raster imagery in modern AVIF and WebP formats with responsive srcset descriptors (1x, 2x, or width w descriptors), applying fetchpriority="high" to the single
dont: Never apply loading='lazy' to the above-the-fold LCP hero image; lazy-loading it delays the initial render.
values: Responsive <picture>: AVIF primary, WebP fallback, 2x density for UI screenshots; hero LCP image: loading='eager' fetchpriority='high' decoding='async'; below-the-fold images: loading='lazy' decoding='async'.

rule: Replace generic flat vector stock illustrations ("Corporate Memphis" figures) with live interactive HTML/CSS component vignettes or schematic wireframe previews of the actual product interface.
do: Replace generic flat vector stock illustrations ("Corporate Memphis" figures) with live interactive HTML/CSS component vignettes or schematic wireframe previews of the
dont: Do not make illustrative UI vignettes look like functional page forms with active tab stops unless they are genuinely interactive demos; set tabIndex={-1} and aria-hidden="true" on non-functional UI previews.
values: context: Modern SaaS (Linear/Vercel/Stripe) visual artifact specification: Build miniature interactive or schematic HTML/CSS replicas of the real UI (using the app's actual design tokens, 1px hairline borders, mono badges, and subtle peripheral fade mask-image: linear-gradient(to bottom, black 70%, transparent 100%)) with aria-hidden="true" if purely illustrative.

rule: Standardize system icons on a 24x24px grid with Material-style 2px padding (20x20px live area) and a dedicated 16x16px grid for compact inline controls.
do: Standardize system icons on a 24x24px grid with Material-style 2px padding (20x20px live area) and a dedicated 16x16px grid for compact inline controls.
dont: Do not scale a intricately detailed 24x24px icon down below 14px without switching to a simplified 16px optical variant, or internal paths will blur together.
values: Material Symbols grid: 24x24 canvas, 2px padding, 20x20 live area. Lucide has its own icon guide and should be checked against it; do not assume the Material 2px/20px live area applies to Lucide. Compact tier 16x16 or 20x20.

rule: Maintain a uniform stroke width (1.5px or 2px), rounded caps/joins, and at least 2px of negative space between parallel paths across every icon in the interface.
do: Maintain a uniform stroke width (1.5px or 2px), rounded caps/joins, and at least 2px of negative space between parallel paths across every icon in the interface.
dont: Never mix filled icons, 1px hairline icons, and 2px bold stroke icons within the same navigation bar or toolbar unless fill vs. outline explicitly encodes active vs. inactive selection state.
values: Lucide & Atlassian icon vector metrics: stroke-width: 2px (Lucide/Material regular) or 1.5px (Atlassian/Linear high-density UI); stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; minimum internal gap between distinct strokes = 2px; 90-degree corner radius = 2px for shapes >= 8px and 1px for shapes < 8px.

rule: Balance icons optically using keyline templates (making circles 20px in diameter and squares 18x18px) and shift asymmetric glyphs like play triangles 1px–2px toward their visual center of mass.
do: Balance icons optically using keyline templates (making circles 20px in diameter and squares 18x18px) and shift asymmetric glyphs like play triangles 1px–2px toward
dont: Do not rely on automated SVG bounding-box centering (justify-content: center on a tight path bounding box) for asymmetric directional icons (play, send, chevron, external-link).
values: Material Symbols keyline dimensions inside 24x24px canvas: Circle = 20px diameter; Square = 18x18px; Vertical rectangle = 16x20px; Horizontal rectangle = 20x16px; Asymmetric triangular play icon inside a circular button: shift +1px to +2px horizontally along the pointing axis so the centroid aligns with the circle center.

rule: Hide decorative icons from assistive technology using aria-hidden="true" while giving standalone icon-only buttons an explicit aria-label, a >= 24x24px (44x44px mobile) hit area, and a tooltip on hover/focus.
do: Hide decorative icons from assistive technology using aria-hidden="true" while giving standalone icon-only buttons an explicit aria-label, a >= 24x24px (44x44px mobile)
dont: Do not use unlabeled icon-only buttons for complex or irreversible domain actions where the icon metaphor is ambiguous (use an icon + text label instead).
values: Accessible icon-button anatomy: <button type="button" aria-label="Copy API key"><svg aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" width="16" height="16">...</svg></button> paired with a fast-appearing tooltip (delay 300ms–500ms, instant 0ms on subsequent adjacent buttons, dismissible via Escape per WCAG 1.4.13).

rule: Generate surface grain procedurally using an inline SVG <feTurbulence type="fractalNoise"> filter rather than downloading raster PNG noise textures.
do: Generate surface grain procedurally using an inline SVG <feTurbulence type="fractalNoise"> filter rather than downloading raster PNG noise textures.
dont: Do not use low baseFrequency (< 0.40) which creates cloudy Perlin blotches rather than fine analog film/paper grain.
values: Resolution-independent SVG noise recipe: <feTurbulence type="fractalNoise" baseFrequency="0.65" to "0.80" numOctaves="3" stitchTiles="stitch" /> encoded as an inline SVG data URI or referenced via filter: url(#noise); zero external HTTP requests and < 300 bytes payload.

rule: Treat grain overlay opacity as a heuristic (start around 0.02-0.05, or 0.15-0.30 with mix-blend-mode: overlay/soft-light) and let the text contrast check on the grain rule govern.
do: Treat grain overlay opacity as a heuristic (start around 0.02-0.05, or 0.15-0.30 with mix-blend-mode: overlay/soft-light) and let the text contrast check on the grai
dont: Never put visible grain over dense data tables or small body text. context: no source establishes a universal grain opacity; text contrast over the grain decides, not the number.
values: heuristic: Subtle anti-banding grain overlay: opacity: 0.03 to 0.04 (normal blend) or opacity: 0.20; mix-blend-mode: overlay; applied strictly to hero backdrops, dark gradient banners, or promotional cards.

rule: Isolate noise overlays on a non-interactive ::after pseudo-element with pointer-events: none and z-index below foreground text so click/selection events and glyph sub-pixel anti-aliasing remain unaffected.

rule: Advisory: replace generic 3-column symmetric icon-title-paragraph feature cards (grid-cols-3 with boxed Lucide icons) with asymmetric bento grids, split editorial narratives, or interactive product showcases.

rule: Advisory: eliminate decorative floating blurred neon orbs, excessive glassmorphism on content cards, and gratuitous sparkle/robot-head icons that signal low-effort AI template generation.

values: context: Zero decorative blur blobs: remove random position: absolute; filter: blur(100px); width: 300px; background: #a855f7 / #06b6d4 background circles; cap backdrop-filter usage to <= 2 functional navigation/overlay surfaces per viewport; replace generic sparkle/wand icons on non-AI features with domain-specific semantic iconography or clean typography.

rule: Advisory: break the repetitive centered-pill-badge + gradient-H1 + subtext + two-buttons hero formula by introducing left-aligned editorial typography, immediate interactive product state, or high-contrast spatial framing.

Asymmetric 7:5 or 6:6 desktop grid with left-aligned high-contrast display type (letter-spacing: -0.04em, solid #111111 or #F5F5F7 without rainbow text-clip) and a live interactive sandbox on the right; 2. Architectural grid lines (1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.07) or rgba(0,0,0,0.07)) dividing hero copy, live telemetry metrics, and action controls into structural cells.

rule: Ensure that no keyboard-focused element is ever completely hidden behind sticky headers, fixed footers, floating bottom bars, or cookie banners by setting CSS scroll-padding matching the sticky overlay height (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 Level AA).

CSS remediation: html { scroll-padding-top: calc(var(--sticky-header-height, 64px) + 16px); scroll-padding-bottom: calc(var(--sticky-footer-height, 56px) + 16px); }.

rule: Render keyboard focus indicators via :focus-visible using a 2px thick solid ring with at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors and a 2px offset (or two-tone inner/outer ring) so focus is unmistakable on any background (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.13 Level AAA).

values: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.13 Focus Appearance: Area >= 2 CSS px thick perimeter around the component; Contrast change between focused and unfocused states >= 3:1; Adjacent contrast >= 3:1 or >= 2px offset. Universal two-tone CSS recipe: :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring-outer, #2563EB); outline-offset: 2px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--bg-canvas, #FFFFFF); } (never use outline: none without a high-contrast replacement).

rule: Size every pointer target to at least 24x24 CSS pixels on all web (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Level AA legal floor), or space undersized targets with a 24px clearance circle.
do: Size every pointer target to at least 24x24 CSS pixels on all web (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Level AA legal floor), or space undersized targets with a 24px clearance circle.

rule: Provide a single-pointer click or tap alternative for every drag-and-drop interaction, slider, Kanban card move, or sortable list so users with motor tremors or eye-gaze pointers never have to press-and-drag (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7 Level AA).
do: Provide a single-pointer click or tap alternative for every drag-and-drop interaction, slider, Kanban card move, or sortable list so users with motor tremors or eye-gaze
dont: Only exempt when dragging path itself is essential to the activity (such as freehand drawing or signature capture canvases). | codex: drag-only operation is forbidden except where dragging is essential or user-agent controlled.
values: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7 Dragging Movements (Level AA): Pair every draggable Kanban card/list row with a single-click context menu or action popover ("Move to column...", "Move up / Move down" buttons) and pair range sliders with clickable step buttons or direct numeric text inputs. Note: Keyboard-only arrow support does NOT satisfy SC 2.5.7; it must be operable by a single pointer without dragging.

rule: Ensure page layouts reflow cleanly down to a 320 CSS pixel viewport width (equivalent to 400% browser zoom on a 1280px screen) without horizontal overflow or two-dimensional scrolling (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Level AA).

values: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Reflow (Level AA): Vertical scrolling content must fit within 320 CSS pixels width without horizontal scrollbars; Horizontal scrolling content within 256 CSS pixels height. Use min(100%, 420px) instead of fixed width: 420px, flex-wrap: wrap on toolbars, and minmax(min(100%, 280px), 1fr) on CSS grids.

rule: Build all text containers with flexible heights and relative padding so user-injected text-spacing overrides never clip, overlap, or truncate copy (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.12 Level AA).

dont: Do not hardcode fixed pixel heights (e.g., height: 32px; overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap) on multi-word cards, alert banners, or navigation items that will clip when letter-spacing expands to 0.12em. | codex: WCAG 1.4.12 values are tolerance targets (1.5, 2, 0.12, 0.16), not required design values.
values: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.12 Text Spacing (Level AA) test thresholds: 1. Line height (line spacing) to at least 1.5 times the font size; 2. Spacing following paragraphs to at least 2 times the font size; 3. Letter spacing (tracking) to at least 0.12 times the font size (0.12em); 4. Word spacing to at least 0.16 times the font size (0.16em). Use min-height instead of fixed height on buttons/cards/badges and avoid overflow: hidden on text wrappers without expandable/tooltip recovery.

rule: Disable or replace spatial translation, parallax and spring bounce when prefers-reduced-motion: reduce is active; keep high-frequency keyboard actions instant (heuristic).

values: Preferred: inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) remove or swap specific spatial animations for opacity cross-fades. Fallback only (not the default): a global '*, *::before, *::after' reset with animation-duration/transition-duration 0.01ms and scroll-behavior: auto. Heuristic: instant response for keyboard actions used very often (e.g. command palette arrows).

rule: Gate text contrast on WCAG 2.x ratios only (4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text >=18pt or >=14pt bold); treat APCA Lc as advisory, never as a pass/fail gate.
do: Gate text contrast on WCAG 2.x ratios only (4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text >=18pt or >=14pt bold); treat APCA Lc as advisory, never as a pass/fail gate.

rule: Maintain at least a 3:1 non-text contrast ratio on active form input borders, custom checkboxes/toggles, and data chart series against adjacent surfaces, and make hover/focus popovers dismissible via Escape, hoverable, and persistent (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 & 1.4.13 Level AA).

WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (Level AA): Tooltips/popovers must be: 1. Dismissible (Escape key closes without moving focus), 2. Hoverable (cursor can move onto tooltip without it closing, using a 4px–8px invisible hover bridge), 3. Persistent (stays open until user moves focus/hover away or dismisses).

rule: Implement the APG Tabs pattern with roving tabindex; use automatic activation for static panels and manual activation when switching has latency or layout shift.

Left/Right arrows move between tabs, Home/End jump to first/last. Automatic: arrow focuses and selects. Manual: arrow focuses, Enter/Space selects.

rule: Auto-populate previously entered data across multi-step workflows (WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.7 Level A) and allow password-manager autofill, passkeys, and clipboard paste on all authentication and OTP fields without cognitive puzzle tests (WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.8 Level AA).

rule: Structure forms in a single vertical column with persistent top-aligned labels placed 4px–8px above each input field, never using placeholder text as a substitute for a visible label.

values: Baymard Institute form layout metrics: 1 column vertical flow; Label position: top-aligned, margin-bottom: 6px (4px–8px), font-size: 14px (0.875rem), font-weight: 500; vertical gap between distinct form fields: 16px–24px (ensuring label-to-own-input distance 6px is < 1/3 of label-to-previous-input distance 20px for unmistakable Gestalt grouping).

rule: Trigger inline field validation only after the user leaves the field (on blur) or submits, and immediately clear the error state on keystroke the moment the input becomes valid.
do: Trigger inline field validation only after the user leaves the field (on blur) or submits, and immediately clear the error state on keystroke the moment the input
dont: Exception for live feedback: password-strength checklists and handle-availability checks (debounced).
values: Validation state machine (unattributed UX pattern; not a Baymard finding): 1. while typing the first attempt, show no error; 2. on blur validate and show a specific error; 3. while in error state re-validate on every keystroke and clear the error the moment the value is valid.

rule: Set form input font-size to at least 16px (1rem) on mobile viewports to prevent iOS Safari from auto-zooming the page, and match field widths to the expected character length of the data.
do: Set form input font-size to at least 16px (1rem) on mobile viewports to prevent iOS Safari from auto-zooming the page, and match field widths to the expected character
dont: Do not stretch a 5-digit ZIP code or 3-digit CVV field across a full 600px container width, which makes the field look broken and obscures what format is expected.
values: Input sizing tokens: Mobile input font-size >= 16px (1rem), height = 44px–48px; Desktop input font-size = 14px–16px, height = 36px–40px, horizontal padding = 12px. Expected-length width constraints: ZIP/Postal code = 10ch–12ch (100px–120px); CVV = 6ch–8ch (72px–88px); Phone = 18ch–22ch (180px–220px); Standard text/email = 100% up to max-width: 420px.

rule: Connect inline error messages programmatically to their input via aria-describedby and aria-invalid="true", combining a high-contrast border, an error icon, and specific corrective instructions.

rule: Cap top-level summary KPI cards (heuristic: about 4-6) in the top row of a dashboard, pairing each metric with a temporal comparison delta and period context.

values: KPI card anatomy (Atlassian & Carbon dashboard standards): 1. Metric Label (12px–14px muted text, top-left); 2. Primary Metric Value (28px–36px font.metric.large, bold/semibold, font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums); 3. Contextual Delta Badge (+12.4% vs. last 30 days, using upward/downward arrow icon + semantic green/red text so direction is clear without color alone); 4. Optional micro-sparkline (height 24px–32px, stroke 1.5px, no axis clutter).

rule: Suppress loading indicators for very short operations (heuristic: under ~100-300ms) and use layout-matched skeleton screens (heuristic: after ~400ms) instead of spinners for initial panel loads.
do: Suppress loading indicators for very short operations (heuristic: under ~100-300ms) and use layout-matched skeleton screens (heuristic: after ~400ms) instead of spin
dont: Do not place a single centered full-page spinner over a blank screen for dashboard loads, and do not use skeleton screens for indeterminate background tasks whose final layout structure is unknown.
values: heuristic thresholds: ~0-100ms instant, no loader; ~100-300ms delay the skeleton by a short timer so cached responses never flash a loader; ~400ms+ render structural skeletons matching card/table heights with a subtle pulse, paused when prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. Compact inline spinners for localised button actions.

rule: Right-align all quantitative numeric, currency, and percentage columns (along with their column headers) and enforce font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so decimal points and place values align vertically.
do: Right-align all quantitative numeric, currency, and percentage columns (along with their column headers) and enforce font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so decimal points
dont: Do not right-align nominal numeric strings that are not compared by magnitude (such as phone numbers, ZIP codes, credit card digits, or alphanumeric UUIDs)—left-align them and still apply tabular-nums. | codex (CANDIDATE): align comparable numbers and use tabular figures; no tables for layout.
values: Data table alignment & typography matrix (Shopify Polaris, IBM Carbon, NN/g): 1. Text, names, IDs, status badges = Left-aligned; 2. Counts, currency ($1,240.00), percentages (14.2%), durations = Right-aligned with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; and consistent decimal precision (e.g., always 2 decimal places for currency); 3. Single-icon action triggers or boolean checkmarks = Center-aligned (or right-pinned).

rule: Keep data table headers sticky during vertical scroll, pin the primary identifier column during horizontal scroll, and provide a row-density toggle for long tables.
do: Keep data table headers sticky during vertical scroll, pin the primary identifier column during horizontal scroll, and provide a row-density toggle for long tables.
dont: Do not truncate critical identifier cells without a full-text tooltip or expandable row view, and never allow sticky table headers to have a transparent background.
values: Use the design system's density tokens (compact / default / relaxed) rather than hard-coded row heights. Sticky header: position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 2; opaque background; border-bottom. Sticky first column: position: sticky; left: 0; z-index: 1; with a subtle edge shadow when scrolled horizontally.

rule: Use subtle 1px horizontal row dividers and a distinct row hover fill instead of heavy four-sided grid lines; reserve zebra striping for wide tables (heuristic: more than ~6 columns).
do: Use subtle 1px horizontal row dividers and a distinct row hover fill instead of heavy four-sided grid lines; reserve zebra striping for wide tables (heuristic: more
dont: Do not combine heavy alternating zebra striping, row hover highlights, AND colored status row backgrounds in the same table, which creates visual strobing when scrolling.
values: Table border & hover tokens: Horizontal row rule: border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.06) (light) or rgba(255,255,255,0.06) (dark); Vertical cell borders: none (use 16px–24px horizontal cell padding for column separation); Row hover state: background-color: var(--gray-2) or --p-color-bg-surface-hover; Selected row state: background-color: var(--accent-3) with a 2px left accent bar.

rule: Replace persistent per-row multi-button action clutter with a contextual batch-action toolbar that appears when checkboxes are selected and a single right-pinned overflow menu (or hover-revealed quick actions with keyboard focus parity).
do: Replace persistent per-row multi-button action clutter with a contextual batch-action toolbar that appears when checkboxes are selected and a single right-pinned
dont: Never hide primary row actions behind mouse :hover without making them equally visible on :focus-within, as keyboard and touch-screen users cannot hover.
values: IBM Carbon batch action pattern: When >= 1 row checkbox is checked, morph or overlay the table toolbar with a high-contrast batch action bar showing "{N} items selected", primary batch CTAs (Export, Archive, Delete), and a "Cancel" button (also triggered via Escape). Per-row actions: maximum 1–2 inline icon buttons + 1 "..." overflow menu (all reachable via keyboard Tab focus, never mouse-hover-only).

rule: Start the quantitative axis of every bar chart, column chart, and filled area chart at a strict zero baseline (Y = 0) so bar lengths remain mathematically proportional to the underlying values.
do: Start the quantitative axis of every bar chart, column chart, and filled area chart at a strict zero baseline (Y = 0) so bar lengths remain mathematically proportional
dont: Never truncate a bar chart Y-axis to start above zero, as a bar starting at 90 makes a value of 100 look twice as large as 95 (a 100% visual distortion of a 5.2% difference).
values: NN/g & Carbon Charts zero-baseline mandate: Bar/Column/Area chart Y-axis minimum = 0 (100% of cases); Line chart Y-axis: may use a non-zero domain [min - padding, max + padding] ONLY when visualizing narrow rate-of-change fluctuations (e.g., latency or stock price between 98ms and 102ms) AND the axis break/range is clearly labeled.

rule: Label data series directly at the end of lines or bars whenever a chart contains 4 or fewer series instead of forcing users to cross-reference a detached color legend.
do: Label data series directly at the end of lines or bars whenever a chart contains 4 or fewer series instead of forcing users to cross-reference a detached color legend.
dont: Do not use direct line-end labels when > 4 time-series lines converge at the same final Y-value unless a collision-avoidance force layout separates the labels with leader lines. | codex: use a legend only when direct labelling is not feasible.
values: Direct labeling threshold: Series count <= 4: place category/series name and terminal value directly beside the final data point or bar end (minimum 8px gap, 12px font-size, tabular-nums) and omit the external legend; Series count = 5 to 6: place a horizontal top-aligned legend directly above the plot area with interactive hover-to-highlight series isolation.

rule: Prioritize 2D position and linear length encodings (horizontal/vertical bar charts, line charts, scatter plots) over area or angle encodings (pie, donut, radial gauge, or 3D charts) for quantitative comparison.
do: Prioritize 2D position and linear length encodings (horizontal/vertical bar charts, line charts, scatter plots) over area or angle encodings (pie, donut, radial gauge,
dont: Never use 3D extruded charts, multi-ring concentric pie charts, or donut charts with > 5 slices (replace with a sorted horizontal bar chart with direct percentage labels).
values: Cleveland & McGill / NN/g perceptual accuracy ranking: 1. Position along a common scale (bar/dot plot); 2. Position on identical non-aligned scales (small multiples); 3. Length; 4. Angle/Slope (pie chart); 5. Area (bubble/treemap); 6. Color saturation (heatmap). Cap pie/donut charts strictly to <= 3–5 part-to-whole categories that sum to 100%, sorting slices clockwise from 12 o'clock largest-to-smallest.

rule: Cap categorical chart palettes at 5 to 6 distinct series per chart, alternate lightness as well as hue across adjacent series to meet 3:1 non-text contrast (WCAG 1.4.11), and reserve red/amber/green strictly for threshold alerts.
do: Cap categorical chart palettes at 5 to 6 distinct series per chart, alternate lightness as well as hue across adjacent series to meet 3:1 non-text contrast (WCAG
dont: Never assign semantic alert red (#DC2626) or success green (#16A34A) to arbitrary non-status categories (e.g., "Region A" vs "Region B"), which tricks users into thinking Region A is failing. | codex: do not reuse a palette built for another number of groups unless the group count is variable.
