values: IBM Carbon categorical data-viz palette rules: Maximum recommended series per chart = 5–6 (group remaining tail categories into a neutral gray "Other" series); Adjacent bar/slice contrast >= 3:1 (or separate adjacent stacked bars/pie slices with a 1px–2px background-colored gap stroke); Secondary redundant encoding for color-blind accessibility: pair line colors with distinct stroke dash patterns (solid, 4-4 dashed, 2-2 dotted) or marker shapes (circle, square, triangle).

rule: Mute background chart grid lines to low-opacity hairlines (3 to 5 horizontal ticks maximum) so the data series strokes (2px) and bars remain the highest-contrast elements in the plot area.
do: Mute background chart grid lines to low-opacity hairlines (3 to 5 horizontal ticks maximum) so the data series strokes (2px) and bars remain the highest-contrast
dont: Do not draw a 4-sided enclosed box border around the inner chart plot area or display minor sub-grid lines every 10px, unless the chart is a scientific engineering nomogram requiring manual interpolation.
values: Chart visual hierarchy metrics (Edward Tufte data-ink ratio & Carbon Charts): Grid lines: 3–5 horizontal ticks only (omit vertical grid lines on time-series line/bar charts), stroke: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.06) (light) or rgba(255,255,255,0.07) (dark); Axis labels: 11px–12px, muted text token (Step 11), tabular-nums; Primary data line: stroke-width: 2px to 2.5px; Subtle area fill under single-series line chart: 12%->0% vertical linear gradient of the line hue.

rule: Provide an accessible keyboard-navigable crosshair tooltip AND a screen-reader-accessible summary or expandable HTML <table> view for every interactive canvas or SVG chart.
do: Provide an accessible keyboard-navigable crosshair tooltip AND a screen-reader-accessible summary or expandable HTML <table> view for every interactive canvas or SVG
dont: Never render an SVG or <canvas> chart with dozens of raw unlabelled <path> nodes exposed to the accessibility tree without an aria-label summary and tabular data fallback. | codex: provide a table or text alternative for chart data; do not make the chart the only access to values.
values: Accessible chart contract: 1. Root SVG/Canvas container has role="img" or role="graphics-document" with an informative aria-label summarizing the headline trend (e.g., "Monthly revenue grew 24% from $120k in Jan to $149k in Jun"); 2. Keyboard Left/Right Arrow keys step through data points with a visible focus indicator and synchronised tooltip; 3. A visually hidden (.sr-only) or toggleable "View as table" <table> provides exact row/column access to all underlying data values.

rule: Anchor primary navigation and high-frequency actions in the bottom third of the mobile viewport (the natural thumb zone) while placing destructive or infrequent settings in the top bar or secondary sheets.
do: Anchor primary navigation and high-frequency actions in the bottom third of the mobile viewport (the natural thumb zone) while placing destructive or infrequent settings
dont: Do not place a sticky bottom primary CTA bar AND a persistent bottom navigation tab bar stacked together on the same screen; hide the bottom tab bar on focused transactional task flows (e.g., checkout or compose screens) where a bottom sticky CTA is used.
values: context: Mobile thumb-zone ergonomics (6.1"–6.9" displays): Natural one-handed thumb arc reaches the bottom 35%–45% of the screen effortlessly; Place primary CTAs, floating action buttons, search triggers, and tab bars in the bottom 48px–120px zone (above the bottom safe-area inset); Keep top app bars (top 15% of viewport) limited to page title, back navigation, and at most 1–2 low-frequency action icons.

rule: Keep mobile bottom navigation to a small set of frequent top-level destinations (Material default: 3-5), pairing every icon with a persistent text label that does not truncate.
do: Keep mobile bottom navigation to a small set of frequent top-level destinations (Material default: 3-5), pairing every icon with a persistent text label that does no
dont: Do not hide text labels on inactive tabs; do not add overflow tabs. context: Apple HIG gives no number of tabs, only 'limit to frequently used destinations'; the 3-5 default is attributed to Material only.
values: Material 3 Navigation Bar guidance: 3-5 destinations; beyond that move secondary destinations to a menu/sheet or use a sidebar/rail on large screens. Platform bar dimensions follow the platform component; do not hard-code them.

rule: Make anything touch-reachable at least 44x44 px by default on web (24px is the WCAG legal floor), 48x48dp on Android native and 44x44pt on iOS native, with spacing between adjacent targets.
do: Make anything touch-reachable at least 44x44 px by default on web (24px is the WCAG legal floor), 48x48dp on Android native and 44x44pt on iOS native, with spacing b
dont: Never pack several small action icons close together on a mobile list row; move secondary actions to a sheet or overflow menu. context: 24 CSS px is the legal floor (WCAG 2.5.8) for desktop pointer UIs.
values: Defaults: web touch 44x44px, Android native 48x48dp, iOS native 44x44pt; legal floor 24x24 CSS px. Expand visual 20-24px icon buttons via padding or a pseudo-element: .icon-btn { position: relative; } .icon-btn::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: -10px; }

rule: Present contextual mobile tasks, filters and detail views in bottom sheets with standard snap detents (medium and large) and a visible drag grabber.
do: Present contextual mobile tasks, filters and detail views in bottom sheets with standard snap detents (medium and large) and a visible drag grabber.
dont: Always provide an explicit visible Close ("X" or "Done") button or scrim-tap dismissal alongside the drag grabber so users who cannot perform vertical drag gestures can still close the sheet (WCAG 2.5.7). | codex: keep default sheet size sufficient for context; do not show several sheets at once from the main UI.
values: iOS SwiftUI presentationDetents([.medium, .large]) with the system grabber; Material 3 bottom sheet with drag handle inside an accessible hit area. Sizes follow the platform component; do not hard-code them.

rule: Extend background surfaces edge-to-edge across the full display while padding all interactive controls and text using OS safe-area insets (env(safe-area-inset-*)) to clear notches, Dynamic Island, and bottom gesture indicators.
do: Extend background surfaces edge-to-edge across the full display while padding all interactive controls and text using OS safe-area insets (env(safe-area-inset-*)) to
dont: Do not apply safe-area padding as an outer white margin that cuts off background colors or scrolling lists before the screen edge—let backgrounds and scroll views bleed to the physical bezel while insetting inner content. | codex: do not anchor important actions in covered zones.
values: Edge-to-edge + safe-area: <meta name='viewport' content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover'>; bottom bar padding: padding-bottom: max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom)); inset values vary by device, so rely on env(safe-area-inset-*) rather than numbers. Use 100dvh (dynamic viewport height) instead of 100vh on mobile web so browser address bars do not clip bottom controls.

rule: Pair discrete physical state changes (toggle switches, sheet detent snaps, pull-to-refresh thresholds, and validation errors) with calibrated system haptics while keeping continuous scroll silent.
do: Pair discrete physical state changes (toggle switches, sheet detent snaps, pull-to-refresh thresholds, and validation errors) with calibrated system haptics while
dont: Never trigger haptic pulses on standard page loads, passive list scrolling, or every character keystroke outside the system keyboard, as constant vibration drains battery and causes sensory fatigue. | codex: Apple gives no universal numeric haptic intensity.
values: Native haptic mapping: 1. Toggle switch / picker tick = iOS UISelectionFeedbackGenerator / Android HapticFeedbackConstants.CLOCK_TICK or SEGMENT_FREQUENT_TICK; 2. Sheet detent snap / button confirm = UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(.light or .medium) / Android CONFIRM; 3. Form submission success or destructive error = UINotificationFeedbackGenerator(.success / .warning / .error) / Android REJECT.

rule: In native SwiftUI apps, let a floating (Liquid Glass) tab bar minimize on downward scroll and expand on upward scroll so content claims more space.
do: In native SwiftUI apps, let a floating (Liquid Glass) tab bar minimize on downward scroll and expand on upward scroll so content claims more space.
dont: Do not collapse or auto-hide the bottom navigation bar on non-scrolling fixed-viewport utility screens (e.g., calculators, camera viewfinders, or dashboard home screens that fit within 100dvh).
values: UNVERIFIED: exact scroll thresholds, horizontal inset and spring parameters of Apple's Liquid Glass tab bar behaviour; use the native SwiftUI tab bar behaviour rather than re-implementing numbers. Native only, no CSS equivalent.

rule: Animate mobile touch interactions (bottom sheets, floating action menus, and morphing toggles) with interruptible spring physics rather than fixed-duration linear or cubic-bezier timers.
do: Animate mobile touch interactions (bottom sheets, floating action menus, and morphing toggles) with interruptible spring physics rather than fixed-duration linear or
dont: Never apply under-damped bouncy springs to opacity, color fades or enterprise financial tables, and disable spring motion when prefers-reduced-motion: reduce is active.
values: Prefer interruptible springs for position/shape (sheet drag, expand, morph); opacity/color use a fast ease-out. Preserve the velocity vector when interrupted mid-gesture. UNVERIFIED: specific damping ratio and stiffness values.

rule: Flatten nested container hierarchies on mobile viewports (< 640px) by using full-width grouped sections or single-level inset cards with a 16px screen margin instead of nesting boxed cards inside boxed cards.
do: Flatten nested container hierarchies on mobile viewports (< 640px) by using full-width grouped sections or single-level inset cards with a 16px screen margin instead of
dont: Never nest 3 levels of bordered/padded cards on a 375px mobile screen, which squeezes inner text columns down to < 220px (~22 characters per line).
values: Mobile horizontal screen budget (375px–393px viewport width): Outer screen margin = 16px left/right (leaving 343px–361px content width); If a desktop view has an outer panel (24px padding) containing inner cards (24px padding), collapse the outer box on mobile so only one level of 16px padding separates text from the viewport edge (recovering 64px of lost horizontal text width).

rule: Keep the leftmost and rightmost 20px–24px vertical screen edges free of horizontal drag sliders or custom swipe gestures so they never conflict with iOS and Android system edge-swipe Back navigation.
do: Keep the leftmost and rightmost 20px–24px vertical screen edges free of horizontal drag sliders or custom swipe gestures so they never conflict with iOS and Android
dont: Do not override or block native browser/OS edge-swipe back navigation with custom full-bleed horizontal touch handlers.
values: System gesture exclusion zone: the left and right screen edges are reserved by iOS back-swipe and Android predictive back; inset horizontal carousels, slider thumbs and swipe-to-archive triggers away from the edges and require a clear horizontal intent before locking horizontal pan.

rule: Provide a global keyboard-first Command Palette (Cmd+K / Ctrl+K) in multi-view applications that opens instantly, groups actions semantically and filters results as the user types.
do: Provide a global keyboard-first Command Palette (Cmd+K / Ctrl+K) in multi-view applications that opens instantly, groups actions semantically and filters results as
dont: Do not center a command palette vertically with align-items: center if its height shrinks as search results filter down, because the search input box will jump up and down on every keystroke.
values: Command palette pattern (cmdk / Linear style): Cmd+K / Ctrl+K plus a visible search pill; max-width about 640px; fixed top anchor (about 15-20% from top) so the input does not move as results filter; group headers (Recent, Navigation, Actions); Up/Down cycle, Enter executes, Escape closes.

rule: Keep primary navigation to a small set of top-level items (heuristic: about 5-7), indicate the active route with at least two visual cues plus aria-current='page', and middle-truncate long breadcrumbs.
do: Keep primary navigation to a small set of top-level items (heuristic: about 5-7), indicate the active route with at least two visual cues plus aria-current='page', a
dont: Never rely on a subtle hue shift alone (< 3:1 contrast difference from inactive links) to mark the active navigation item, which fails WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color.
values: heuristic: top-level nav about 5-7 items; active route = high-contrast text/weight + subtle surface pill or accent indicator bar + aria-current='page'; long breadcrumbs: Root / ... (menu revealing middle ancestors) / Parent / Current Page.

rule: Design every empty state (first-use onboarding, user-cleared inbox, or zero search/filter results) with a clear heading stating what is empty, a 1-to-2 sentence explanation of value or cause, and at most two actions (one primary CTA and one secondary link).
do: Design every empty state (first-use onboarding, user-cleared inbox, or zero search/filter results) with a clear heading stating what is empty, a 1-to-2 sentence
dont: Never display a blank white/dark box or a bare "No data" string without explaining whether the state is due to first-time setup, active search filters, or a permission/loading failure.
values: Shopify Polaris & IBM Carbon Empty State anatomy: Container max-width: 400px–480px centered within the empty panel/table body; 1. Optional restrained spot graphic/icon (48x48px to 64x64px, muted monochrome or subtle brand tint); 2. Heading (16px–20px semibold, e.g., "No deployment logs match your filters"); 3. Body copy (14px muted text, max 2 lines); 4. Action row: Maximum 2 actions—1 primary button ("Reset filters" or "Create first project") + 1 optional secondary link ("Read documentation" or "Import CSV").

rule: Format system and network error states with a human-readable explanation of what failed, preserve all user-entered state, and provide an immediate inline recovery action (Retry, Undo, or Edit Filters) while relegating technical request IDs to a copyable secondary detail.
do: Format system and network error states with a human-readable explanation of what failed, preserve all user-entered state, and provide an immediate inline recovery action
dont: Never use an auto-dismissing toast notification (disappearing after 3s–5s) as the sole indicator for a critical save failure or destructive error that requires user recovery action.
values: NN/g & Carbon Error State contract: 1. What happened + why in plain language (never raw HTTP 500 / JSON stack traces as primary heading); 2. Zero data loss (keep form inputs, drafts, or table selections intact in memory/localStorage); 3. Primary recovery CTA button ("Try again", "Reconnect", or "Restore draft"); 4. Optional subtle monospace footer (12px Geist/Atlassian Mono: Request ID: req_9f8a... with a one-click Copy button for support debugging).

rule: In a shadow scale use blur as a distance cue: larger elevation gets larger blur.
do: Scale blur with elevation (Fluent: shadow 2 blur 2px, shadow 64 blur 64px).
dont: Do not treat these values as a complete recipe independent of system tokens and opacities.
values: Fluent shadow 2 = blur 2px; shadow 64 = blur 64px

rule: Pick tokens by semantic role, not because the visual value looks right.
do: Reference dynamic/semantic colour tokens.
dont: Do not hardcode platform colour values in place of dynamic tokens.

rule: Apply grain discreetly and only when it improves separation or character; check contrast of text above it.
do: Use subtle noise and verify text contrast over it.
dont: Do not rely on a universal opacity/blur value for noise; none is established. disagrees: gemini-argon R52 gives 0.02-0.05 opacity as DIRECT.

rule: Vary hierarchy, composition and density by content and purpose; avoiding a generic 'AI-made' look has no common measurable criterion, so treat it as an art-direction hypothesis.
do: Vary hierarchy, composition and density per content.
dont: Do not present 'avoid AI look' as a verified fact or hard rule.
values: context: no measurable criterion in sources

rule: Use coherent semantic type roles: display, headline, title, label and body.
do: Define the five Material 3 roles.
dont: Material 3 does not require all products to adopt the same sizes.
values: roles: display, headline, title, label, body

rule: Use a documented or tokenised type ramp.
do: Take a ramp such as Fluent Web as reference.
dont: Do not copy these values if your font and platform have different metrics.
values: Fluent Web: body large 18px/24px, title 28px/36px, large title 40px/52px, display 68px/92px

rule: Use tabular numeric formats for data columns and pick tracking per type style.
do: Use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums or Geist Mono for data.
dont: Do not assume a universal tracking value for display text; none is validated. disagrees: gemini-argon R34 gives progressive negative tracking values.
values: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums

rule: Allow text enlargement up to 200% without loss of content or functionality.
do: Use flexible heights and layouts that survive 200% text.
dont: Do not fix heights or clips that hide enlarged text.
values: 200% text resize

rule: Provide alternatives to complex path-based or multipoint gestures and do not require a specific screen orientation unless essential.
do: Offer single-pointer alternatives and support both orientations.
dont: Check WCAG exceptions that apply in context.

rule: Content shown on hover or focus must be dismissible, hoverable and persistent long enough (WCAG 1.4.13).
do: Let users dismiss, hover over and read tooltips.
dont: Do not use tooltips that vanish before the user can read them.
values: WCAG 1.4.13

rule: Differentiate focus with a clear contour or stroke, not colour change alone.
do: Use a thicker-stroke focus container as in Fluent.
dont: Do not remove the focus indicator for a minimalist look.

rule: Avoid flashes and abrupt motion that can trigger seizures and communicate animated changes through an accessible channel such as ARIA live regions.
do: Convey state changes by text/live region as well as animation.
dont: Do not convey information only by animation.

rule: Do not use colour as the only means of conveying meaning; add labels, shapes, patterns or descriptive text for signals and charts.
do: Add label/shape/pattern next to colour.
dont: Do not signal status only by colour.

rule: Group information by purpose and importance using semantic tokens for colour, spacing and elevation.
do: Group related metrics under one purposeful container.
dont: Do not give every indicator its own card just because the dashboard format allows cards.

rule: If the legend is hidden on small screens, give a visible control to open it.
do: Add a visible legend toggle button on small screens.
dont: Do not remove the legend without an alternative access path (Carbon).

rule: Separate adjacent colour areas by space or border and do not put text over series colours that miss 4.5:1; place labels beside the data.
do: Place labels next to data; add gap or border between areas.
dont: Do not overlay text on series colours below 4.5:1.
values: text contrast 4.5:1

rule: Avoid a legend for a single-category chart and use plain-language titles and axis labels without needless acronyms.
do: Use titles and axis labels in plain language.
dont: Do not hide the legend if the user needs it to tell series apart.

rule: Use th elements for headers, scope for row/column headers when needed, and a descriptive caption to identify the table.
do: Use th + scope + caption.
dont: Do not use tables for visual effect or page layout.

rule: Allow two-dimensional scrolling inside the table region when the structure needs it, while keeping surrounding content and controls responsive at 320 CSS px.
do: Scope scroll to the table container.
dont: Do not extend the table exception to the whole page.
values: 320 CSS px

rule: Use a tab bar for navigating between top-level app sections, not for in-screen actions; keep it visible while navigating between sections (except temporary modal cover) and do not disable or hide tabs for temporarily unavailable destinations.
do: Keep the tab bar visible and show unavailable state consistently.
dont: Do not put contextual actions in the tab bar or hide tabs.

rule: Limit primary destinations to frequently used ones, avoid overflow tabs and consider a sidebar for complex hierarchies.
do: Keep the main destination list short.
dont: context: Apple gives no universal number of tabs; Material's default of 3-5 destinations is a Material-only guideline, not a cross-platform cap.

rule: For disclosure-style web navigation use links for navigation and predictable keyboard behaviour.
do: Use real links with predictable keys.
dont: Radix warns that complex navigation menus can be unnecessary or confusing for ordinary web patterns.

rule: For a modal dialog keep Tab/Shift+Tab within the dialog, provide a visible close button, and restore focus to the trigger on close.
do: Trap focus, show close button, return focus to the trigger.
dont: Do not allow interaction with the background while the modal is open.

rule: Never put glass/backdrop-blur behind body content; use it only on nav and overlays.
do: Never put glass/backdrop-blur behind body content; use it only on nav and overlays.
dont: Do not apply backdrop-filter to cards, tables or reading containers, and do not stack glass on glass.
values: Glass belongs to the floating control layer (nav bars, toolbars, popovers, command palettes); the content layer stays opaque.

rule: Give every glass surface a solid fallback via @supports not (backdrop-filter) and @media (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce).
do: Give every glass surface a solid fallback via @supports not (backdrop-filter) and @media (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce).
dont: Never ship a translucent rgba() background without an opaque fallback for unsupported browsers and reduced-transparency users.
values: Default: opaque background-color; @supports (backdrop-filter: blur(12px)) { translucent + blur }; @media (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce) { backdrop-filter: none; background: var(--solid-surface); }.

rule: Use 100dvh (not 100vh) for full-height mobile layouts.
do: Use 100dvh (not 100vh) for full-height mobile layouts.
dont: Do not size full-height mobile layouts with 100vh, which ignores the dynamic browser toolbars and can clip bottom controls.
values: min-height: 100vh; min-height: 100dvh; (dvh as the enhancement; vh as the fallback for older browsers).

rule: Use a six-step non-linear duration scale such as Carbon's as one concrete reference, without treating it as universal.
do: Map fast tokens to micro-interactions and slow tokens to expansions/dimming as Carbon names them.
dont: Do not apply slow-01/slow-02 (400ms-700ms) or expressive tokens inside dense data tables, form inputs or enterprise toolbars.
values: fast-01=70ms, fast-02=110ms, moderate-01=150ms, moderate-02=240ms, slow-01=400ms, slow-02=700ms

rule: Keep separate productive (task efficiency) and expressive (brand/emphasis) easing curves and do not treat them as interchangeable.
do: Use expressive curves for marketing/brand moments and productive curves for dense app UI.
dont: Do not mix productive and expressive curves arbitrarily within one component.
values: Productive: standard cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0.38, 0.9), entrance cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.38, 0.9), exit cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 1, 0.9); Expressive: standard cubic-bezier(0.4, 0.14, 0.3, 1), entrance cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.3, 1), exit cubic-bezier(0.4, 0.14, 1, 1)

rule: Scale transition duration with travel distance and surface area instead of using one fixed duration everywhere.
do: Small state shifts short, medium components mid, large layout expansions longest.
dont: Do not use the same fixed duration (e.g., 300ms everywhere) across both 16px checkboxes and 800px drawers.
values: Carbon: 70ms button/toggle micro-interactions, 110ms fades, 150ms small expansions or short movements, 240ms expansions/toasts, 400ms large expansions, 700ms background dimming; gemini ranges: small (<32px) 50ms-150ms, medium (cards, dropdowns) 150ms-250ms, large (dialogs, drawers) 250ms-400ms

rule: Build a separate spring-based token option when following Material 3 Expressive rather than forcing it into fixed durations.
do: Define standard and expressive schemes, each with fast, default and slow speeds for spatial and effects tokens.
dont: Do not translate spring tokens into fixed durations unless the implementation requires that mapping.
values: standard/expressive schemes x fast/default/slow speeds; spatial and effects tokens

rule: Define a tiered duration token ladder in 50ms steps from short micro-interactions up to extra-long ambient transitions.
do: Reserve long/extra-long tokens for large or ambient transitions.
dont: Do not use long or extra-long tokens (>=450ms) for high-frequency utility controls or keyboard-triggered menus.
values: M3: short1=50ms, short2=100ms, short3=150ms, short4=200ms; medium1=250ms, medium2=300ms, medium3=350ms, medium4=400ms; long1=450ms, long2=500ms, long3=550ms, long4=600ms; extra-long1..4=700ms-1000ms

rule: Fluent's scale tops out at 500ms; use an 8-step semantic scale mapped to element size and travel distance.
do: Use the slow end only for large surfaces.
dont: Do not use durationSlower (400ms) or durationUltraSlow (500ms) for hover states, checkboxes, or focus ring transitions.
values: Fluent 2: durationUltraFast=50ms, durationFaster=100ms, durationFast=150ms, durationNormal=200ms, durationGentle=250ms, durationSlow=300ms, durationSlower=400ms, durationUltraSlow=500ms

rule: Pair directional easing tokens with duration tiers in token aliases: decelerate for entering, accelerate for exiting, standard/emphasized for on-screen movement.
do: Bundle easing and duration into one semantic alias per motion role.
dont: Do not pair an exit acceleration token with a long duration (>300ms), which makes dismissed UI feel unresponsive.
values: M3: easing-emphasized (use M3 standard curve cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) as fallback for emphasized), easing-emphasized-decelerate=cubic-bezier(0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1), easing-emphasized-accelerate=cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0.8, 0.15)

rule: Expose semantic motion tokens as CSS custom properties on :root so a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce query can override spatial curves and durations globally.
do: Remap spatial duration tokens >200ms to 100ms-150ms cross-fade tokens under reduced motion.
dont: Do not collapse duration tokens to 0s globally when component unmount logic listens for transitionend or animationend events.
values: >200ms -> 100ms-150ms under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce; never 0ms globally

rule: Use an aggressive decelerating ease-out curve for elements entering the viewport so the animation starts instantly and settles gently.
do: Apply to entering overlays, toasts and revealed content.
dont: Never use for exiting elements or continuous looping spinners.
values: M3 Emphasized Decelerate cubic-bezier(0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1); Carbon Entrance Productive cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.38, 0.9); Fluent 2 curveDecelerateMax cubic-bezier(0.1, 0.9, 0.2, 1)

rule: Use an accelerating ease-in curve only for elements permanently exiting the screen so they clear the workspace rapidly.
do: Apply to dismissals and exits.
dont: Never use ease-in or accelerate curves for entering UI elements or user-triggered hover/press feedback, as slow starts feel laggy.
values: M3 Emphasized Accelerate cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0.8, 0.15); M3 Standard Accelerate cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 1, 1); Carbon Exit Productive cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 1, 0.9); Fluent 2 curveAccelerateMax cubic-bezier(0.9, 0.1, 1, 0.2)

rule: Use an asymmetric ease-in-out curve for elements moving or morphing while remaining visible on screen.
do: Fast initial acceleration followed by prolonged deceleration.
dont: Do not use for simple opacity-only cross-fades or elements entering from outside the viewport.
values: M3 standard curve cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) (fallback for emphasized); Carbon Standard Expressive cubic-bezier(0.4, 0.14, 0.3, 1); Fluent 2 curveEasyEase cubic-bezier(0.33, 0, 0.67, 1) or curveEasyEaseMax cubic-bezier(0.8, 0, 0.2, 1)

rule: Use springs for spatial, gesture-driven or interruptible motion and time-based easing curves for short non-spatial effects such as opacity.
do: Use springs (or CSS linear() approximations) where gesture velocity must be preserved or motion can be interrupted mid-flight.
dont: Do not force springs onto every property; avoid bouncy springs (bounce > 0.2 or under-damped) in enterprise productivity interfaces, financial dashboards, or when prefers-reduced-motion: reduce is active.
values: SwiftUI spring API Spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.0-0.2); Motion spring stiffness: 300-500, damping: 25-35, mass: 1 (or bounce: 0.15, duration: 0.35); CSS linear(0, 0.006, ..., 1.045 30.5%, ..., 1)

rule: Configure physics springs through physical parameters and let settling time follow the spring instead of specifying a fixed duration as its defining parameter.
do: Use a duration only for a CSS linear() approximation that necessarily requires one.
dont: disagrees: gemini-argon gives duration-based spring presets (Spring(duration: 0.4, ...), bounce: 0.15, duration: 0.35).

rule: Reserve linear easing strictly for constant-rate time indicators, marquee loops, and color/opacity transitions without spatial translation.
do: Use linear for progress and time indicators.
dont: Never apply linear easing to spatial transform: translate() or scale() movements, which look robotic.
values: linear or cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)

rule: Keep standard interactive UI transitions (dropdowns, popovers, tooltips, menus, modals) under 300ms so the interface never feels sluggish.
do: Pick the duration per component type from the values.
dont: Do not apply the <300ms cap to full-screen mobile bottom sheets mimicking native iOS spring physics or ambient background illustrations.
values: Button press: 100ms-160ms; Tooltips/micro-interactions: 100ms-200ms; Dropdowns/popovers: 150ms-250ms; Modals/drawers: 200ms-300ms (mobile bottom sheets up to 400ms-500ms)

rule: Make exits feel quicker than entrances when that supports the interaction, treating any specific enter/exit ratio as a candidate.
do: Use distinct entrance and exit curves.
dont: disagrees: gemini-argon prescribes exits 20%-35% shorter; codex found no verified universal timing ratio.

rule: Make exit animations 20% to 35% shorter than entrance animations so dismissed elements vacate the screen right after user intent is registered.
do: Example: medium entrance 250ms-300ms vs short exit 150ms-200ms.
dont: Do not use fast exits when an element minimizes into a spatial target the eye must track. disagrees: codex says no verified universal enter/exit ratio exists.
values: 20%-35% shorter; M3 example: entrance 250ms-300ms (medium1/medium2) vs exit 150ms-200ms (short3/short4); Josh Comeau hover: enter 125ms-200ms vs fast modal close 150ms

rule: Stagger sequential list or grid items by 30ms-60ms per item while capping total stagger wait time at 400ms-600ms.
do: Clamp total delay for long lists.
dont: Never stagger lists exceeding 10-15 visible items linearly without clamping total delay, and never use per-item stagger >150ms. disagrees: codex found no reliable universal numeric stagger range.
values: Per-item delay: 30ms-60ms for lists/chips, 60ms-100ms for cards (up to 80ms for large cards); item duration: 200ms-300ms; total cap: 400ms-600ms

rule: Keep frequent feedback brief and remove animation entirely (0ms) from high-frequency keyboard actions so motion never becomes a speed tax.
do: Use 0ms for command palettes, autocomplete highlighting, arrow-key navigation and warm tooltip groups; let users continue or cancel without waiting for an animation.
dont: Do not add motion to frequent standard controls that already have system feedback; do not strip animation from first-time contextual disclosures or low-frequency spatial transitions where orientation matters.
values: 0ms for keyboard selection changes and repeated command-palette toggles; subsequent tooltips in a warm group 0ms

rule: Use motion to communicate state, feedback, instruction, hierarchy or direct manipulation, not as decoration.
do: Give every animation a functional purpose.
dont: Do not add motion solely as decoration when it distracts or delays the task.

rule: Animate popovers, dropdowns, modals and toasts from an initial scale of 0.90-0.97 with opacity 0 rather than from scale(0).
do: Initial opacity: 0; scale(0.95) -> opacity: 1; scale(1).
dont: Never animate overlays from scale(0).
values: scale range 0.90-0.97 (default 0.95); duration 150ms-200ms; easing cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)

rule: Anchor every popover, tooltip and context menu's transform-origin to the trigger edge it emerges from.
do: Use top left, bottom center or a dynamic anchor-position origin.
dont: Do not leave the default transform-origin: center on menus attached to a top or bottom trigger.
values: scale 0.95 -> 1.0, translation 4px -> 0px, duration 150ms

rule: Delay the first tooltip in a group by 300ms-500ms, then open adjacent tooltips instantly while the group remains warm.
do: Use a warm handoff window between tooltips.
dont: Never make users wait 500ms and watch a fresh entrance on every icon when scanning a toolbar.
values: Initial delay: 300ms-500ms; warm handoff window: 300ms-400ms; subsequent tooltip delay 0ms, duration 0ms (or 100ms layout morph)

rule: Morph stateful action icons (Copy -> Checkmark, Play -> Pause) with simultaneous opacity and scale.
do: Hold the feedback state before reverting.
dont: Do not run the morph longer than 200ms or leave the feedback state stuck.
values: scale(0.5) -> scale(1), 150ms-200ms; hold 1500ms-2000ms

rule: Let swipe-to-dismiss drawers and toasts inherit release velocity and apply rubber-band resistance past their limit.
do: Dismiss on a velocity flick or a drag-distance threshold.
dont: Do not trigger destructive swipe actions on a minor flick without an undo toast or clear threshold confirmation.
values: flick velocity >500 px/s OR drag >40%-50% of element height; damping factor 0.2-0.35 (distance * 0.25)

rule: Gate hover-only effects behind a hover-capable input query and give touch and keyboard users equivalent active and focus feedback.
do: Use @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine); touch feedback relies on :active (100ms).
dont: Never make hover the only way to reveal critical controls, labels or information.
values: @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine); :active 100ms

rule: Shrink buttons slightly on :active press to confirm the press registered.
do: Use 0.98-0.99 for large cards/rows and 0.95-0.97 for buttons/pills.
dont: Do not apply :active shrink to giant cards (>400px) or to disabled buttons.
values: scale(0.97), transition: transform 100ms ease-out; 100ms-150ms

rule: Use asymmetric hover timing on cards and decorative elements: fast on pointer enter, gentler settle on pointer leave.
do: Enter 100ms-150ms; leave 250ms-450ms.
dont: Do not use slow hover exits (400ms) on dense list rows, menu items or table rows.
values: hover enter: transition: transform 125ms ease-out; translateY(-4px); base (exit): 400ms ease-out

rule: Prevent hover jitter on lifted cards by keeping the hit-test wrapper stationary and translating only the inner visual surface.
do: Outer hit area fixed; inner .card-surface translateY(-6px).
dont: Never translate the element bearing :hover directly without a stationary wrapper.
values: translateY(-4px) to -8px; example -6px

rule: Treat scroll-driven animation support as browser-version-dependent and do not claim support for older versions.
do: Check compatibility data at build time.
dont: Do not assume support in older Safari/Firefox.
values: animation-timeline, scroll(), view(): Chrome 115, Firefox 159, Safari 26

rule: Gate CSS scroll-driven animations behind @supports and keep content fully visible by default for unsupported browsers.
do: Use scroll() for scroller progress and view() for element visibility progress inside @supports (animation-timeline: view()) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference).
dont: Never set opacity: 0 in base CSS outside the @supports block.
values: fallback 0 KB JS, or IntersectionObserver (threshold: 0.15) if an entrance trigger is required

rule: Use CSS animation-timeline: scroll() for reading progress bars and scroll-linked headers instead of main-thread JavaScript scroll listeners.
do: animation-timeline: scroll(nearest block) or scroll(root).
dont: Do not ship without @supports progressive enhancement when legacy parity is mandatory.
values: Chrome/Edge 115+, Safari 26+, Firefox 159+

rule: Pair animation-timeline: view() with a constrained animation-range so reveals complete before the element reaches 30%-50% viewport height.
do: animation-range: entry 0% cover 30%.
dont: Never tie essential reading copy opacity to cover 0% cover 100%.
values: animation-range: entry 0% cover 30% (or entry 10% entry 90%); animation-fill-mode: both

rule: Trigger scroll-reveal entrance animations only once on downward scroll rather than replaying them in reverse when users scroll back up.
do: Use IntersectionObserver and unobserve after the first intersection, or ScrollTrigger once: true.
dont: Do not apply once: true to live indicators like reading-progress bars or sticky header shrink.
values: threshold: 0.1-0.2, rootMargin: "0px 0px -10% 0px"

rule: Keep scroll-linked effects subtle and nonessential and keep static content readable when the animation is unsupported or reduced.
do: Provide a readable static state.
dont: Do not gate comprehension on scroll-linked motion.

rule: Wrap same-document state changes in document.startViewTransition() behind a feature check so unsupported browsers update immediately.
do: if (!document.startViewTransition) { updateDOM(); return; }
dont: Do not wrap high-frequency keystrokes, drag coordinates or 60fps canvas updates in startViewTransition().
values: Chrome/Edge 111+, Safari 18.0+, Firefox 144+ (gemini)

rule: Use cross-document view transitions between opted-in same-origin pages as progressive enhancement, declared inside a reduced-motion no-preference query.
do: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { @view-transition { navigation: auto; } } in both pages.
dont: Do not enable on slow-TTFB pages without prerendering/prefetching; keep standard navigation when unsupported.
values: Chrome/Edge 126+ and Safari 18.2+ (no Firefox support as of late 2026 - feature-detect)

rule: Assign unique view-transition-name values only to the few shared hero elements that morph and share styling via view-transition-class.
do: Typically 1-5 elements per transition.
dont: Never assign unique view-transition-name values to 50+ list items simultaneously.
values: ::view-transition-group(*.card-morph) { animation-duration: 250ms; animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1); }

rule: Constrain ::view-transition-old/new with object-fit: cover and height: 100% when morphing between containers of different aspect ratios.
do: Apply overflow: clip on the snapshot.
dont: Do not rely on the default cross-fade scaling when morphing text blocks of different line-wrap widths.
values: height: 100%; object-fit: cover; overflow: clip

rule: Keep page transitions subordinate to navigation and content and never block user actions while they run.
do: Let users act immediately.
dont: Do not prevent interaction during a transition.

rule: Keep full-route page transitions between 150ms and 300ms using subtle cross-fades or short directional shifts rather than opaque curtain wipes.
do: translateY(8px) to translateY(16px) with opacity 0 -> 1.
dont: Never use 800ms-1200ms full-screen curtain wipes on content, documentation, e-commerce or SaaS apps.
values: 150ms-300ms (M3 medium1=250ms, medium2=300ms); offset 8px-24px

rule: Overlap route exit and entrance with a fast fade-through: outgoing fades in the first 30% while incoming fades and scales up in the remaining 70%.
do: Run exit and entrance overlapping, not sequentially.
dont: Do not wait for a 300ms exit before a 300ms entrance (600ms blocked time).
values: total 250ms-300ms; exit 0ms-90ms cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 1, 1); enter 90ms-300ms scale(0.96 -> 1) cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0, 1); initial scale 92%-96%

rule: Encode hierarchy in direction: going deeper pushes forward, returning pops back, peer tabs slide by index order.
do: Use shared-axis transitions for related routes.
dont: Do not apply directional slides between unrelated top-level routes; use fade-through.
values: shared axis 30px, 250ms-300ms, cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)

rule: Reset scroll and move focus to the new route heading after the outgoing view hides, and skip custom transitions on native back/forward swipe gestures.
do: Synchronize the focus move with transition completion.
dont: Never play a custom slide on top of iOS Safari's native edge-swipe back gesture.
values: focus move <=300ms

rule: Use a skeleton only when the final layout is known and the placeholder helps users understand what is loading.
do: Match the skeleton to the known layout.
dont: disagrees: gemini-argon gives skeleton timing thresholds (1s-10s, 300ms-500ms hold, 1.5s shimmer); codex found no verified duration or conversion benefit.

rule: Delay showing any spinner or skeleton briefly and keep it visible for a minimum hold once shown to avoid single-frame flashes.
do: Show nothing for responses under 100ms.
dont: Do not add an artificial delay when the server-rendered skeleton is already the static shell. disagrees: codex found no verified skeleton timing.
values: <100ms show nothing; delay 150ms-200ms (100ms-200ms); minimum hold 300ms-500ms (UNVERIFIED)

rule: Use full-section skeletons only for loads between 1 and 10 seconds, spinners for short local actions, and determinate progress bars beyond 10 seconds.
do: Show time/step feedback for long waits.
dont: Never use an indeterminate skeleton for uploads, exports or AI generation lasting >10 seconds. disagrees: codex found no verified skeleton duration.
values: <1s: no skeleton; 1s-10s: skeleton; >10s: determinate progress bar (0%-100%)

rule: Pace skeleton shimmer at about 1.5s per cycle using a composited transform overlay instead of animating background-position.
do: Under reduced motion use static blocks or a slow opacity pulse.
dont: Never animate background-position on dozens of blocks and never run shimmers faster than 0.8s.
values: cycle 1.5s (range 1.2s-1.8s), infinite; ::after translateX(-100%) -> translateX(100%); reduced motion: opacity pulse 2s ease-in-out

rule: Match skeleton geometry to the final content and cross-fade to real data so the swap causes no layout shift.
do: Match heights, radii, gaps and aspect ratios.
dont: Do not render generic 3-line skeletons that jump by 100px+ when content hydrates.
values: CLS 0.00 (Google good threshold 0.1); cross-fade 150ms-200ms

rule: Animate text only when it stays readable and does not delay access to the complete message.
do: Keep the full message available immediately.
dont: Do not use animated text as the sole way to convey meaning.

rule: Preserve screen-reader access when splitting text into spans: aria-label on the parent, aria-hidden on fragments, and revert the split when done.
do: GSAP SplitText.create(el, { type: "words,chars" }) auto-injects the aria attributes in GSAP 3.13+; clean up with split.revert().
dont: Never split body paragraphs or long-form articles into character spans.
values: <h1 aria-label="Full original text">; <span aria-hidden="true">; GSAP 3.13+

rule: Animate longer hero copy by line or word inside an overflow-clip mask rather than character by character.
do: Use per-character animation only for short headlines (<=30 chars).
dont: Do not use per-character stagger on multi-sentence value propositions (a 120-character string at 25ms/char = 3,000ms delay).
values: char stagger 15ms-25ms (<=30 chars); word/line stagger 40ms-70ms per line (25ms-50ms), duration 400ms-600ms, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); switch above 30-40 characters

rule: Apply font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums to animated counters, timers and pricing toggles so changing digits do not jitter.
do: Use short decelerating interpolation.
dont: Do not count up from 0 over 2000ms+ for static metrics such as prices; use a 200ms-350ms slot-roll or cross-fade.
values: tabular-nums; counter 300ms-600ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); static metrics 200ms-350ms

rule: Never hide the LCP element (hero heading/image) behind an entrance animation; animate secondary elements instead.
do: Render the hero heading/image visible in the first paint; animate secondary elements (eyebrow, subcopy, decorative layers).
dont: Do not hide the LCP element with opacity: 0, visibility or a delayed entrance waiting on JS.
values: LCP <= 2.5s (good threshold)

rule: Remove or replace parallax, depth zooming, animated blur and scroll-linked background panning when reduced motion is requested.
do: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .parallax-layer { transform: none !important; animation: none !important; } }
dont: Do not rely on parallax to communicate essential state.
values: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.3.3; Apple Reduce Motion evaluation criteria

rule: Keep parallax speed differentials subtle so foreground copy and background layers do not clash.
do: Move only background/decorative layers.
dont: Never apply parallax to body text containers or interactive buttons.
values: speed factor 0.1 to 0.3 (10%-30%); max offset ±40px to ±80px (UNVERIFIED universal cap)

rule: Enable pointer-tilt parallax only on fine-pointer hover devices with no reduced-motion preference, and clamp the rotation.
do: window.matchMedia("(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)").
dont: Do not bind continuous deviceorientation gyroscope parallax on mobile landing pages; disable below 768px.
values: rotateX(±4deg-8deg) rotateY(±4deg-8deg); off below 768px

rule: Animate transform and opacity for continuous or interactive motion so the compositor can handle it without layout or paint.
do: Use translate, scale, rotate and opacity. Exception: one-off disclosure (grid-template-rows 0fr->1fr) on a small subtree.
dont: Never animate top, left, width, height, margin, padding or border-width in keyframes or per-frame JS loops.
values: frame budget 16.67ms at 60Hz, 8.33ms at 120Hz

rule: Animate only the properties you need instead of broad transition: all, and still profile the real page.
do: List transitioned properties explicitly.
dont: Do not use transition: all where unintended properties may animate.

rule: Apply will-change only when a measured performance issue justifies it and remove it when the change is no longer imminent.
do: Measure first.
dont: Do not promote every animated element preemptively. disagrees: gemini-argon applies will-change on anticipated interaction without requiring a measured issue.

rule: Apply will-change dynamically on anticipated interaction and remove it after transitionend rather than declaring it permanently.
do: Add it on :hover or pointerenter.
dont: Never declare * { will-change: transform; } or permanent will-change on dozens of cards. disagrees: codex requires a measured performance issue before using will-change.
values: each 1080p RGBA layer ~8.3 MB VRAM (1920 * 1080 * 4 bytes)

rule: Measure user-facing responsiveness and layout shifts instead of assuming smooth motion is free.
do: Profile INP and CLS on the real page.
dont: Do not infer a quantified INP or CLS improvement from adopting one animation library.

rule: Use FLIP (First, Last, Invert, Play) when transitioning layout dimensions or grid positions so the change runs as a compositor transform.
do: Automate via the Motion layout prop or GSAP Flip.from().
dont: Do not run FLIP measurements across 100+ nodes on every resize without throttling.
values: animate to translate(0,0) scale(1,1) over 200ms-300ms

rule: Paint press/toggle feedback on the next frame before heavy synchronous work to keep INP within the good threshold.
do: Use :active, the Web Animations API, requestAnimationFrame or startTransition.
dont: Never block the click handler for >50ms before the press animation starts.
values: INP good <= 200ms (75th percentile); needs improvement 200ms-500ms; poor > 500ms

rule: Never insert unsolicited animated banners, toasts or accordions above existing content without reserved space or fixed positioning, to keep CLS low.
do: Use position: fixed or pre-allocated space; transform-based motion does not add CLS. User-initiated expansion within 500ms of input is excluded from CLS, so this applies to unsolicited insertions only.
dont: Never expand a top banner from height: 0 -> 48px after initial paint.
values: CLS good <= 0.1 (75th percentile); poor > 0.25; transform animations contribute 0.00

rule: Honor prefers-reduced-motion: reduce by removing, reducing or replacing nonessential spatial movement with short cross-fades, not by disabling every animation.
do: Replace translate/scale/bounce with 100ms-200ms opacity/color fades; in Motion wrap the app in <MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">. Avoid large-scale panning and scaling and test the adapted experience with the OS setting enabled; do not presume that shortening every duration addresses vestibular triggers. Allow interaction-triggered motion to be disabled via prefers-reduced-motion and/or a site setting unless essential (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.3.3, Level AAA), covering parallax, page morphs and scroll-jacked sequences.
dont: Never use the global * { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; transition-duration: 0.01ms !important; } reset without testing. Do not confuse the AAA criterion 2.3.3 with the A-level flash criteria.
values: 100ms-200ms opacity cross-fade (gemini synthesis: 150ms); SC 2.3.3 Level AAA

rule: Keep essential status and hierarchy signals under reduced motion by swapping to a dissolve, highlight fade, color shift or slower pulse.
do: Keep progress bars updating; replace a rapid 0.6s spinner with a 1.5s-2.0s opacity pulse or stepped indicator.
dont: Do not remove the only signal that an action succeeded and do not hide or freeze loading spinners.
values: spinner 0.6s -> 1.5s-2.0s opacity pulse

rule: Put large or decorative animations inside a no-motion-first @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) block.
do: Scroll-driven, parallax and decorative keyframes live inside no-preference.
dont: Do not gate basic 100ms hover color transitions or focus outlines behind no-preference.
values: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference); 100ms color transitions stay

rule: Provide an in-app motion toggle or pause control that supplements the OS reduced-motion setting via a root data attribute.
do: Check both the media query and :root[data-motion="reduced"]; auto-pause background video when either is active.
dont: Do not force users to change OS settings just to stop an autoplaying background video.
values: [data-motion="reduced"]

rule: Provide pause, stop or hide controls for moving, blinking or scrolling content that starts automatically, lasts more than 5 seconds and runs alongside other content (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.2, Level A).
do: Applies to carousels, marquees and background video.
dont: Do not apply the threshold to every animation indiscriminately; exempt only essential movement.
values: > 5 seconds; SC 2.2.2 Level A

rule: Ensure nothing flashes more than 3 times in any one-second period unless below the general and red flash thresholds (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.3.1, Level A).
do: Check strobe effects and video.
dont: Do not confuse SC 2.3.3 with this flash threshold; no exceptions.
values: <= 3 flashes per 1 second

rule: Keep the focused element from being entirely hidden by sticky headers, floating bars, bottom sheets or toasts (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11, Level AA).
do: html { scroll-padding-top: var(--sticky-header-height, 72px); scroll-padding-bottom: var(--sticky-cta-height, 64px); }; trap focus inside intentional modals.
dont: Do not treat a motion effect that obscures focus as harmless decoration.
values: SC 2.4.11 Level AA (part visible); SC 2.4.12 Level AAA (100% visible); 72px / 64px example paddings

rule: Size interactive targets to at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels or meet the spacing exception, including while scaled during animation (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8, Level AA).
do: Aim for 44 x 44 where possible (SC 2.5.5 AAA, Apple 44x44pt, Material 48x48dp).
dont: Do not shrink an interactive target to make room for motion decoration.
values: 24 × 24 CSS px (SC 2.5.8 AA); 44 × 44 CSS px (SC 2.5.5 AAA); Apple 44x44pt; Material 48x48dp

rule: Keep animation supplemental to other feedback and never the only way to communicate important information.
do: Pair motion with text, icon or color change.
dont: Do not rely on a visual transition alone to confirm an action.

rule: Default to native CSS transitions/animations and WAAPI for simple states and reserve JS libraries for sequencing, gestures, layout projection or orchestration.
do: Use CSS for hover, enter/exit fades, @starting-style disclosures and simple scroll reveals.
dont: Do not add a library for a few simple state transitions.
values: CSS: 0 KB JS (Motion useAnimate mini ~2.3 KB gzipped)

rule: Choose Motion in React for exit animations, layout projection or gesture-to-spring handoff, and use LazyMotion with m to cut the initial bundle.
do: <LazyMotion features={domAnimation}> + <m.div>.
dont: Do not import the full motion object on performance-critical landing pages; do not treat the size as guaranteed for every build.
values: vendor claim: codex: about 5kb initial; gemini: full ~34 KB -> ~4.6 KB shell (+ ~15 KB feature pack; domMax ~25 KB); useAnimate ~2.3 KB

rule: Choose GSAP when coordinated timelines or complex sequencing justify its runtime, using its x/y transform aliases.
do: Prefer the x and y aliases over parsing transform strings.
dont: Do not treat the GSAP size as verified; core ~25 KB gzipped is a budget hint only.
values: core ~25 KB gzipped (budget hint)

rule: Choose GSAP for multi-element timelines, pinned scrollytelling, SVG morphing or text splitting that must bypass React's render cycle.
do: Drive it imperatively via gsap.ticker.
dont: Do not load GSAP + ScrollTrigger just to fade in cards on scroll. disagrees: codex found no verified GSAP bundle size.
values: core ~25 KB gzipped (budget hint)

rule: Restrict Lottie to designer-authored vector illustrations that CSS/SVG cannot express, ship .lottie with a lazy-loaded player and tune rendering for the actual asset.
do: Limit concurrent instances and pause off-screen ones via IntersectionObserver.
dont: Never use Lottie for layout, simple spinners or gradients; do not assume Lottie is inherently faster or smaller than CSS or a static asset.
values: vendor claim: lottie-web ~50 KB-65 KB gzipped (lottie_light ~35 KB-40 KB); .lottie cuts JSON payload 70%-80%; <= 2-3 active instances

rule: Curate a small set of the strongest relevant projects rather than publishing everything.
do: Pick projects matching the target role.
dont: Do not treat project count as a universal numeric formula.

rule: Give each showcased project a case study explaining the design and the process behind it.
do: Show process with context.
dont: Do not present visuals without context when demonstrating UX work.

rule: Pair project images with captions and a concise introduction so reviewers can orient themselves.
do: Caption every image.
dont: Do not make reviewers infer context from screenshots alone.

rule: Open every case study with a summary block stating your role, timeline, team, problem and the supported outcomes before the process narrative.
do: Highlight 2-3 concrete metrics with high typographic contrast.
dont: Do not bury solution and impact at the end of a long chronological scroll, and do not claim impact the evidence cannot support.
values: 2-3 metrics

rule: Make the portfolio homepage show who you are, your role and links to featured case studies immediately, without an intro preloader.
do: Render role and case-study links right after first paint.
dont: Never lock a portfolio behind a mandatory 2s-4s counter preloader or unskippable intro animation.

rule: Use clear visual hierarchy within case studies so context, process and outcome can be scanned.
do: Use headings and section structure.
dont: Do not rely on a uniform wall of images and text.

rule: Use strong project thumbnails that make each project easy to identify.
do: Make each preview distinctive.
dont: Do not use ambiguous or weak previews as the only project cue.

rule: Provide a readable still image or text explanation for work shown as video or prototype.
do: Add stills and captions next to video.
dont: Do not make video or an interactive prototype the sole way to understand a project.

rule: Audit portfolio content before publishing and remove stale, repetitive or irrelevant material.
do: Review before each publication.
dont: Do not treat the portfolio as an unfiltered archive.

rule: Use animation only as a restrained way to reveal or demonstrate work and keep a static or reduced-motion viewing path.
do: Keep project evidence in focus.
dont: Do not let spectacle compete with project evidence.

rule: Keep native vertical scrolling in portfolio indexes and case studies instead of scroll-jacking.
do: If a smooth-scroll library is used on creative showcases, keep it light and disable it on touch devices and under reduced motion.
dont: Never trap trackpad scrolling in a horizontal scroll-jacking tunnel inside a text-heavy case study.
values: Lenis lerp >= 0.12-0.15 or duration <= 0.8s

rule: Show UI motion artifacts as compressed muted looping video with a poster frame instead of large GIFs.
do: <video autoplay loop muted playsinline preload="metadata"> with an accessible play/pause control.
dont: Never embed 15MB+ GIFs or live iframes that capture page scroll mid-article.
values: clip 3s-8s; < 1.5 MB; 60fps

rule: Morph the clicked project thumbnail into the case-study hero with a shared-element view transition.
do: Fall back to a 150ms opacity cross-fade under reduced motion.
dont: Do not morph when thumbnail and hero images have different compositions or subjects.
values: 250ms-350ms; cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1); reduced motion 150ms

rule: Require an explicit click-to-interact overlay on embedded Figma, CodeSandbox or canvas demos so page scrolling is never swallowed.
do: Default to pointer-events: none on the iframe until activated; provide an Esc exit button.
dont: Do not add the barrier when the whole page is itself the demo.
values: activation button >= 44x44px

rule: Keep the native cursor visible; if a hover preview follower is used, move it with transforms and disable it on touch.
do: gsap.quickTo(el, "x", { duration: 0.15, ease: "power3" }) behind (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).
dont: Never set cursor: none on a portfolio.
values: follower lag 80ms-150ms (100ms-150ms)

rule: Animate project category filters with FLIP layout projection, overlapping exits and entrances.
do: Exiting cards fade/scale with position: absolute so the remaining grid reflows immediately.
dont: Do not run filter exit and entrance sequentially (600ms perceived latency).
values: FLIP 200ms-300ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1); entering stagger 20ms-30ms; exit opacity 0, scale(0.95) over 150ms

rule: Limit WebGL/shader backgrounds to one active canvas, pause it off-screen and fall back to a static image on low frame rate or reduced motion.
do: Cap the device pixel ratio.
dont: Do not load a 150KB+ Three.js bundle on portfolios where 3D adds no signal about the candidate's craft.
values: Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio, 2); IntersectionObserver threshold: 0; fallback if rolling 30-frame average < 30fps (> 33.3ms/frame) (UNVERIFIED)

rule: Keep case-study headings and body text fully opaque during scroll and limit scroll-triggered entrances to media, diagrams and callouts.
do: Trigger figure entrances once.
dont: Never fade in body copy paragraph-by-paragraph on scroll.
values: text opacity 1.0; figures translateY(12px -> 0), 250ms (150ms-300ms), once: true, threshold: 0.15

rule: Give one-click contact actions (copy email with confirmation, direct resume/GitHub/LinkedIn links) instead of a multi-step animated contact wizard.
do: Show a checkmark morph and a "Copied to clipboard" toast.
dont: Never hide the email behind a chatbot animation or a 4-step form modal.
values: feedback < 100ms; scale(0.97) on press; 150ms icon morph; 2000ms reset; target >= 44x44px (>= 24x24px WCAG 2.5.8 minimum)

rule: Label billing cadence next to every price and frame the annual discount concretely, showing the per-month equivalent.
do: Show "$24/mo, billed annually" and a "2 months free" badge next to the Annual label before the user toggles.
dont: Do not rely on the toggle alone to explain the amount charged or hide the annual savings until after switching.
values: "2 months free" (= 16.7% off) or "Save 20%"; "$24/mo billed annually"

rule: State the included usage, seats or other billable unit beside each consumption-dependent price.
do: Define the unit.
dont: Do not use an undefined unit or vague credits as the whole explanation.

rule: Explain overage rates, usage limits and what happens when a plan limit is reached.
do: Show it next to the plan.
dont: Do not conceal material recurring costs below the main plan description.

rule: Make the next step explicit for each plan: start trial, buy or contact sales.
do: Label buttons with what they do.
dont: Do not make users guess whether a button starts billing or a conversation.

rule: Describe plan differences in comparable rows or concise bullets, keeping the cards short and the full matrix in a comparison table below.
do: Prefix with "Everything in [Lower Tier], plus:"; align rows with grid-template-rows: subgrid.
dont: Do not cram 25+ bullets into summary cards or force users to remember details across pages.
values: 5-8 bullets per card; full matrix in the collapsible table

rule: Highlight a recommended plan only when it genuinely fits the target audience and explain why.
do: State the basis of the recommendation.
dont: Do not use a popularity label as unsupported social proof. disagrees: gemini-argon recommends a "Most Popular" badge citing ~57% adoption.

rule: Visually anchor one target tier with a 2px contrasting border, a "Recommended for <audience>" label (use "Most popular" only if real sales data proves it) and the only filled CTA.
do: Keep sibling CTAs secondary/outlined.
dont: Never highlight more than one tier or pulse/bounce the highlighted card. disagrees: codex says a popularity label needs a genuine basis and is not proven social proof.
values: 2px solid border; CTA contrast ratio >= 4.5:1

rule: State trial terms and risk-reversal cues (payment method required or not, what happens at trial end, cancellation) right beside the plan CTAs.
do: Place "No credit card required", "14-day free trial", "Cancel anytime" within the CTA block.
dont: Do not leave trial-to-paid terms ambiguous; never use fake countdown timers or fake purchase toasts.
values: <= 16px-32px below the CTA row

rule: Explain what a free tier includes and what triggers an upgrade.
do: List the limits explicitly.
dont: Do not present free as equivalent to paid when limits differ.

rule: Offer a route to sales or custom pricing when price depends on customer needs and explain what that route requires.
do: Say what information the sales step needs.
dont: Do not show a misleading fixed amount for negotiated plans.

rule: Put plan prices and the primary comparison on the page itself, not behind a modal.
do: Keep material price details visible.
dont: Do not hide material price details behind an extra interaction.

rule: Validate plan wording and page hierarchy with target users or controlled experiments before adopting conversion claims.
do: Test with your own audience.
dont: Do not treat one company's A/B lift as a universal design law. disagrees: gemini-argon states tier-count/highlight/FAQ benchmarks (~65%, ~57%, ~60%) as rules.

rule: Limit the primary pricing grid to 3 or 4 tiers organized by buyer persona.
do: Render a 4th/5th option (enterprise, free-forever) as a full-width banner below the 3-card grid.
dont: Do not show 5 to 7 side-by-side columns above the fold. disagrees: codex says benchmark and A/B figures are not universal laws.
values: 3 to 4 tiers (heuristic)

rule: Update all plan prices in place when the Monthly/Annual toggle changes, with tabular numerals and a sliding pill indicator.
do: Cross-fade or slot-shift the numbers.
dont: Never reload the page or show a spinner on toggle, and never animate a slow 1,500ms odometer that obscures the final price.
values: pill 150ms-200ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1); price change 150ms-250ms; tabular-nums

rule: Default the billing toggle to Annual only with a per-month equivalent and savings badge, and default to Monthly for B2C/prosumer monthly buyers.
do: Show "$24/mo, billed annually" when Annual is the default.
dont: Do not default to an annual lump sum for SMB/prosumer buyers (sticker shock).
values: "$24/mo, billed annually"; "2 months free"

rule: Keep the comparison table's plan header row (name, price, CTA) sticky while scrolling, with scroll-padding so focus is not obscured.
do: position: sticky; top: var(--header-height); add a 150ms shadow fade once pinned.
dont: Do not make 300px-tall summary cards sticky.
values: sticky bar <= 64px-80px; shadow 150ms; WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11

rule: Explain unfamiliar metrics or acronyms in the feature table with accessible popovers opened by hover, focus and tap.
do: Make them dismissible with Escape (WCAG 1.4.13).
dont: Never put mission-critical caveats (onboarding fees, overage penalties) only inside a hover tooltip.
values: entrance 150ms opacity 0 -> 1, scale(0.96 -> 1); target >= 24x24 CSS px

rule: Snap usage/seat sliders to discrete steps with instant price recalculation and switch the CTA to Contact Sales past the enterprise threshold.
do: Offer logarithmic steps or a numeric input next to the slider.
dont: Do not require dragging 1 to 10,000 seats in 1-seat increments.
values: update latency 0ms; crossover fade 150ms-200ms

rule: Localize currency and tax labels by locale and give an explicit currency selector near the billing toggle.
do: Display the 3-letter ISO currency code.
dont: Never auto-convert with rough FX rates without clean rounding and the ISO code.
values: USD, EUR, GBP, AUD, CAD; exact % lift varies by region/cohort

rule: Place a billing/cancellation/refund FAQ accordion directly below the comparison table.
do: Animate grid-template-rows 0fr -> 1fr.
dont: Do not put generic company-history questions on the pricing page.
values: 200ms-250ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)

rule: Option: Set Linear-style marketing hero H1s in Inter Variable using optical size 32 and custom intermediate variable weights with tight negative tracking and near-unit leading.
do: Option: Set Linear-style marketing hero H1s in Inter Variable using optical size 32 and custom intermediate variable weights with tight negative tracking and near-unit leading.
dont: Do not apply opsz 32 or negative tracking (-0.03em) to body copy below 20px or dense table cells, where tight kerning degrades character differentiation. | disagrees: codex: font and H1 settings for Linear's live site are UNKNOWN; a third-party template doc names Poppins as default, so these values are unverified.
values: observed: font-family: "Inter Variable", "Inter Display", sans-serif; font-variation-settings: "opsz" 32; font-feature-settings: "cv01" 1, "ss03" 1; font-weight: 510 or 590; font-size: clamp(2.75rem, 4.5vw + 1rem, 4.5rem) (44px to 72px); letter-spacing: -0.022em to -0.035em (-1.5px at 64px); line-height: 1.06 to 1.10.

rule: Enable the OpenType stylistic alternates cv01, cv02 and ss03 on Inter hero headings (these are Inter features, not Geist features) to replace ambiguous default glyphs with high-precision geometric forms.
do: Enable the OpenType stylistic alternates cv01, cv02 and ss03 on Inter hero headings (these are Inter features, not Geist features) to replace ambiguous default glyphs with high-precision geometric forms.
dont: Do not force ss03 or cv01 when rendering localized Cyrillic/Greek strings that lack matching alternate glyph tables in custom subsetted WOFF2 files.
values: font-feature-settings: "cv01" 1, "cv02" 1, "ss03" 1, "calt" 1; font-synthesis: none; -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased.

rule: Option: Configure Vercel-style hero headings with Geist Sans at weight 600-700, aggressive negative tracking, and balanced line wrapping.
do: Option: Configure Vercel-style hero headings with Geist Sans at weight 600-700, aggressive negative tracking, and balanced line wrapping.
dont: Do not apply -0.06em tracking to all-caps badges or monospace kickers (Geist Mono requires 0em to +0.05em tracking). | disagrees: codex: Vercel publishes Geist and type styles but the consulted source gives no single marketing H1 value; tracking -0.04 to -0.06em is not confirmed. | caveat: Do not deduce that every Vercel H1 uses the same size or tracking; the source gives no single value for the marketing H1.
values: observed: font-family: "Geist Sans", sans-serif; font-size: clamp(2.5rem, 5vw, 4.5rem) (40px mobile to 72px desktop, 60px/64px token); font-weight: 600 to 700; letter-spacing: -0.04em to -0.06em (-2.4px to -3.6px at 60px); line-height: 1.05 to 1.08; text-wrap: balance.

rule: Option: Pair dark hero headlines in Inter (or a system UI sans fallback) at 600 weight with a vertical luminance gradient fill and tight leading.
do: Option: Pair dark hero headlines in Inter (or a system UI sans fallback) at 600 weight with a vertical luminance gradient fill and tight leading.
dont: Do not use gradient text fills on low-contrast light backgrounds or headings longer than 3 lines, where the bottom line loses WCAG AA 4.5:1 contrast.
values: Option values: font-family: "Inter", -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, sans-serif; font-size: 64px (desktop) / 36px (mobile); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.03em (-1.92px); line-height: 1.08; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #FFFFFF 0%, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.65) 100%); -webkit-background-clip: text.

rule: Option: Use high-contrast editorial serif display headings (for example Domaine Display, a licensed face) at regular weight 400 with unit line-height for a developer-luxury positioning.
do: Option: Use high-contrast editorial serif display headings (for example Domaine Display, a licensed face) at regular weight 400 with unit line-height for a developer-luxury positioning.
dont: Never bold high-contrast editorial serifs (weight >= 600 causes ink-trap muddiness on screen) and never use below 32px. | licence: premium display families need a commercial licence; Tiempos Headline or Inter Tight/Geist are suggested alternatives, not guaranteed matches.
values: Option values: font-family: "Domaine Display", Georgia, serif; font-weight: 400 (never bolded); font-size: clamp(3rem, 6vw, 6rem) (48px to 96px); letter-spacing: -0.01em to -0.015em; line-height: 1.00; pair with a neutral sans for H2 and body.

rule: Option: Deploy a bold geometric display face (for example Cal Sans) at 600 weight with -0.04em tracking for bold scheduling/workflow heroes.
do: Option: Deploy a bold geometric display face (for example Cal Sans) at 600 weight with -0.04em tracking for bold scheduling/workflow heroes.
dont: Do not use Cal Sans for multi-sentence paragraphs or subheadlines smaller than 24px because its tight apertures reduce reading speed.
values: Option values: font-family: "Cal Sans", "Inter", sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: clamp(2.5rem, 4.8vw, 4.5rem) (40px to 72px); letter-spacing: -0.035em to -0.045em; line-height: 1.05 to 1.10.

rule: When substituting Fontshare-licensed Satoshi for proprietary geometric grotesques, dial back negative tracking because Satoshi is natively spaced tighter than Inter.
do: When substituting Fontshare-licensed Satoshi for proprietary geometric grotesques, dial back negative tracking because Satoshi is natively spaced tighter than Inter.
dont: Do not apply aggressive -0.05em tracking to Satoshi or use it for dense numerical data tables without enabling tabular-nums (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums). | disagrees: gemini internal: Satoshi needs -0.015 to -0.025em versus -0.04em on Inter/Geist.
values: font-family: "Satoshi-Variable", "Satoshi", sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: clamp(2.75rem, 5vw, 4.5rem); letter-spacing: -0.015em to -0.025em (vs -0.04em on Inter/Geist); line-height: 1.12 to 1.18. [Disagreement Note]: Unlike Geist/Inter rules that prescribe -0.04em to -0.06em, applying -0.05em to Satoshi causes glyph collisions on lowercase 'a', 'e', and 't'.

rule: Option: Use General Sans (Fontshare) as the closest free structural substitute for Klim's Söhne in enterprise B2B heroes, keeping tracking between -0.015em and -0.025em.
do: Option: Use General Sans (Fontshare) as the closest free structural substitute for Klim's Söhne in enterprise B2B heroes, keeping tracking between -0.015em and -0.025em.
dont: Avoid pairing General Sans with another neo-grotesque like Inter for body copy; use General Sans across both heading (600) and body (400) to avoid near-miss visual conflict. | disagrees: codex: optical similarity of Inter Display, Geist, Satoshi or General Sans to a branded face was not measured; treat substitutes as candidates. | caveat: Do not present a substitute as an exact equivalent of a branded face; optical similarity was not measured. Third-party scans of branded headline values are not official brand rules (they vary by breakpoint and over time).
values: observed: font-family: "GeneralSans-Variable", "General Sans", sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: clamp(2.5rem, 4.5vw, 4.25rem) (40px to 68px); letter-spacing: -0.02em; line-height: 1.10 to 1.15.

rule: Constrain hero subtitle (deck) typography to 18px-21px, weight 400, neutral tracking, and 55ch-65ch measure to contrast against tightly compressed H1s.
do: Constrain hero subtitle (deck) typography to 18px-21px, weight 400, neutral tracking, and 55ch-65ch measure to contrast against tightly compressed H1s.
dont: Never allow hero subheadlines to span the full 1200px container width or use tight line-height (< 1.4), which causes eye-tracking line drops.
values: font-size: clamp(1.0625rem, 1.2vw, 1.3125rem) (17px to 21px); font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: -0.005em to 0em; line-height: 1.55 to 1.65; max-width: 58ch (approx 540px-640px); text-wrap: pretty.

rule: Match fallback font metrics by computing size-adjust, ascent-override and descent-override per font pair in @font-face (for example Inter to Arial is about 107%, not 100%) to minimise layout shift during the webfont swap.
do: Match fallback font metrics by computing size-adjust, ascent-override and descent-override per font pair in @font-face (for example Inter to Arial is about 107%, not 100%) to minimise layout shift during the webfont swap.
dont: Do not use uncalibrated font-display: swap on hero H1s without size-adjust fallback descriptors, as reflowing a 72px headline causes visible layout shift.
values: font-display: swap (or optional); size-adjust: ~107% (Inter -> Arial; compute per font pair, never copy a value across fonts); ascent-override: ~90%; descent-override: ~22%; line-gap-override: 0% (these overrides belong to the Inter -> Arial pair only).

rule: Build pinned scroll-driven product stories by pairing an outer tall track container (250vh-400vh) with an inner position: sticky stage (height: 100dvh; top: 0) driven by view-timeline-name on the outer track.
do: Build pinned scroll-driven product stories by pairing an outer tall track container (250vh-400vh) with an inner position: sticky stage (height: 100dvh; top: 0) driven by view-timeline-name on the outer track.
dont: Never apply overflow: hidden, overflow: auto, or overflow: scroll to any ancestor between the sticky stage and the scroll container, which silently breaks position: sticky.
values: Outer track: height: 300vh; view-timeline-name: --story-track; view-timeline-axis: block; Inner stage: position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100dvh; overflow: hidden; Child animation: animation-timeline: --story-track; animation-range: contain 0% contain 100%; animation-fill-mode: both; animation-timing-function: linear.

rule: Use timeline-scope on a shared ancestor container to hoist named view-timelines so sibling sticky product mockups can react to scrolling text steps in an adjacent column.
do: Use timeline-scope on a shared ancestor container to hoist named view-timelines so sibling sticky product mockups can react to scrolling text steps in an adjacent column.
dont: Do not declare duplicate view-timeline-name identifiers within the same timeline-scope subtree without unique naming, as name collisions invalidate timeline resolution. | codex (MDN): timeline-scope hoists a NAMED timeline to a common ancestor; it does not work with anonymous timelines created by view() or scroll().
values: Shared parent: timeline-scope: --step-1, --step-2, --step-3; Scrolling step items: view-timeline-name: --step-1 (etc.); Sticky UI visual layers: animation-timeline: --step-2; animation-range: entry 20% cover 50%.

rule: Use animation-range: contain 0% contain 100% for animations that must run strictly while the sticky container is pinned, and exit-crossing 0% exit-crossing 100% for stacking cards that scale down as the next card overlaps.
do: Use animation-range: contain 0% contain 100% for animations that must run strictly while the sticky container is pinned, and exit-crossing 0% exit-crossing 100% for stacking cards that scale down as the next card overlaps.
dont: Do not use default animation-range: cover 0% cover 100% on pinned sticky tracks, because the first 100vh of entry motion executes before the element even sticks to top: 0.
values: Pinned range: animation-range: contain 0% contain 100%; Stacking card scale-down: position: sticky; top: 32px; transform: scale(0.92); opacity: 0.65; animation-range: exit-crossing 0% exit-crossing 100%.

rule: Restrict scroll-driven keyframe properties to compositor-friendly properties (transform, opacity, and filter only where tested); use clip-path only for one-shot reveals, never scrubbed by scroll.
do: Restrict scroll-driven keyframe properties to compositor-friendly properties (transform, opacity, and filter only where tested); use clip-path only for one-shot reveals, never scrubbed by scroll.
dont: Never animate top, left, width, height, margin, padding, or box-shadow inside a scroll() or view() timeline, which forces synchronous main-thread layout and paint on every scroll tick. | disagrees: codex (Chrome): animate mainly transform and opacity (compositor-friendly); avoid repeatedly animating width/height in scroll-driven animations; CSS does not make an animation cheap by itself.
values: Allowed properties: transform (translate3d, scale, rotate), opacity; filter only after profiling; clip-path: one-shot reveals only, never scrubbed; keep scroll-driven work off the main thread.
