rule: Gate all CSS scroll-driven story styles and 300vh track heights behind @supports (animation-timeline: view()) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) so unsupported browsers render an accessible static stacked layout.
do: Gate all CSS scroll-driven story styles and 300vh track heights behind @supports (animation-timeline: view()) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) so unsupported browsers render an accessible static stacked layout.
dont: Never apply opacity: 0 or height: 300vh outside the @supports block, which leaves older browsers staring at 300vh of blank space or unrevealed content. | codex (MDN/Chrome): declare animation-timeline AFTER the animation shorthand because the shorthand resets it to auto; if the animation is decorative and support is missing, leave content in a fully visible static state; never hide content by default or rely on animation to reveal necessary information. | codex (Chrome): detect with @supports ((animation-timeline: view()) and (animation-range: entry)) since checking animation-range filters out partial implementations; for functional effects build an IntersectionObserver or scroll-listener fallback; purely decorative effects need no JS fallback; do not use the scroll-timeline polyfill automatically (Chrome says it is incomplete with known issues). | codex (web.dev): respect prefers-reduced-motion; remove or reduce decorative motion and provide the final static state; parallax and independent layer motion can cause dizziness, so never make it the only way to understand the product story.
values: Feature query: @supports (animation-timeline: view()) { @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .track { height: 320vh; } .panel { opacity: 0; animation: reveal linear both; animation-timeline: --track; } } }; Fallback state: height: auto; position: relative; opacity: 1; transform: none. Browser status (belief, unverified): scroll-driven animations ship in Chromium 115+ and Safari 26; Firefox default-on status is UNKNOWN, so @supports gating is mandatory.

rule: Cap individual pinned scroll story sections at 250vh-350vh (3 to 4 discrete steps at 75vh-90vh scroll distance per step) to prevent scroll fatigue and mobile touch-swipe exhaustion.
do: Cap individual pinned scroll story sections at 250vh-350vh (3 to 4 discrete steps at 75vh-90vh scroll distance per step) to prevent scroll fatigue and mobile touch-swipe exhaustion.
dont: Never chain back-to-back pinned 400vh scroll stories or exceed 5 steps in a single sticky lock, which causes scroll fatigue on mobile touch screens.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): Step distance: 75vh to 90vh per narrative beat; Max section height: 350vh (3-4 steps); at most 1 pinned section per landing page.

rule: Ensure keyboard Tab navigation through interactive controls inside a pinned scroll story automatically scrolls the timeline container to the corresponding animation-range position or keeps all focusable elements reachable in DOM order.
do: Ensure keyboard Tab navigation through interactive controls inside a pinned scroll story automatically scrolls the timeline container to the corresponding animation-range position or keeps all focusable elements reachable in DOM order.
dont: Never place interactive CTAs inside an overlapping sticky layer with opacity: 0 and pointer-events: none without also managing inert or scrolling the container on focus, which traps sighted keyboard users on invisible focus rings. | codex (CORRELATED, product rule to validate): keep native scrolling and make the story keyboard-navigable through ordinary document content; do not hijack keys or wheel to force scene order; the source prescribes no specific keyboard technique.
values: Focusable steps must stay in natural DOM flow (never display: none or visibility: hidden during inactive scroll ranges if they contain focusable links/buttons; use scroll-margin-top: 20vh or IntersectionObserver focus synchronization).

rule: Collapse pinned multi-column scroll stories into natural vertical cards (position: static; height: auto) on viewports narrower than 768px or shorter than 640px height.
do: Collapse pinned multi-column scroll stories into natural vertical cards (position: static; height: auto) on viewports narrower than 768px or shorter than 640px height.
dont: Do not keep a split sticky stage active on 390x844 portrait phones where a sticky 50vh graphic leaves insufficient vertical space for 4 lines of step copy.
values: Media query: @media (max-width: 767px), (max-height: 640px) { .story-track { height: auto; } .story-sticky { position: relative; height: auto; } }; Mobile card gap: 32px.

rule: Use scroll(nearest block) or scroll(root block) only for continuous page-level progress indicators, and always prefer view() timelines for component-level product stories.
do: Use scroll(nearest block) or scroll(root block) only for continuous page-level progress indicators, and always prefer view() timelines for component-level product stories.
dont: Never tie a mid-page feature story to scroll(root), because dynamic content height changes (e.g. expanding an FAQ or banner above) shift all percentage keyframes out of alignment. | codex (MDN): use scroll() for scroll-position progress, view() or a named view-timeline for progress while an element crosses the scrollport; use a named timeline when the animated element is not a descendant of the controlling element; do not use view() if progress must follow a scroller other than the nearest scrollable ancestor.
values: Page progress bar: animation-timeline: scroll(root block); Component story: view-timeline: --feature-card block; animation-timeline: --feature-card.

rule: Limit active GPU composited layers inside a pinned scroll story and avoid will-change: transform on more than a handful of elements simultaneously.
do: Limit active GPU composited layers inside a pinned scroll story and avoid will-change: transform on more than a handful of elements simultaneously.
dont: Never apply will-change: transform, opacity to every word, card, or SVG path in a scroll story (`* { will-change: transform }`), which can exhaust mobile GPU memory and crash the tab.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): keep concurrent composited child layers to a handful; avoid permanent will-change on many nodes; no memory budget figure is sourced.

rule: Provide a visible step progress pill or clickable tab anchor alongside any pinned scroll story exceeding 200vh so users can see progress and click to jump directly to any step.
do: Provide a visible step progress pill or clickable tab anchor alongside any pinned scroll story exceeding 200vh so users can see progress and click to jump directly to any step.
dont: except: omit the progress indicator on simple 1-step entrance reveals (< 120vh) where it adds visual clutter without aiding navigation. | note: NN/g prescribes no progress pill; this is a design choice, not a documented requirement.
values: Indicator size: 4px-6px track width or clickable step tabs; Step transition on click: element.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth' }) mapped to each step's scroll offset; Contrast of active indicator: >= 3:1 against background (WCAG 1.4.11).

rule: Keep interactive UI and micro-text reveal animations under 300ms (150ms-250ms), while restricting hero display mask reveals to 450ms-650ms with a fast initial velocity ease-out curve.
do: Keep interactive UI and micro-text reveal animations under 300ms (150ms-250ms), while restricting hero display mask reveals to 450ms-650ms with a fast initial velocity ease-out curve.
dont: Never use durations > 300ms on repeated app interactions, dropdowns, or command palettes; high-frequency actions should stay at 0ms-150ms. | disagrees: codex: no source gives durations, easing or stagger for text reveals.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): Micro/UI text reveal: 180ms to 250ms; Hero line-mask reveal: 450ms to 650ms; Easing: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) (Custom Expo Ease-Out) or cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) (Quint Ease-Out); Y-translation inside mask: translateY(100%) to translateY(0%). [Note]: functional UI elements should stay under 300ms so interfaces feel instant, whereas theatrical marketing hero reveals are a design choice that can run longer with a steep ease-out curve.

rule: Use strong ease-out deceleration curves for text reveals so text arrives immediately upon trigger and settles gently.
do: Use strong ease-out deceleration curves for text reveals so text arrives immediately upon trigger and settles gently.
dont: Never use ease-in or linear timing for text reveals. | except: use linear timing when the reveal is tied 1:1 to the user's scroll position (animation-timeline: view()) or for continuous marquee loops.
values: Recommended curves: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) (Expo Out), cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1) (Cubic Out), or cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1) (iOS sheet/drawer curve). Prohibited: ease-in, cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 1, 1).

rule: Stagger masked hero text reveals by line (40ms-70ms delay per line) or by word (20ms-35ms per word), capping the total stagger cascade across the entire hero block at <= 250ms.
do: Stagger masked hero text reveals by line (40ms-70ms delay per line) or by word (20ms-35ms per word), capping the total stagger cascade across the entire hero block at <= 250ms.
dont: Never stagger character-by-character on blocks longer than 3 words or let cumulative stagger delays exceed 400ms, which forces fast readers to wait for words to appear. | disagrees: codex: no source gives per-line/per-word stagger values.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): Line stagger step: 50ms to 70ms (e.g., Line 1: 0ms, Line 2: 60ms, Line 3: 120ms, Subtitle: 180ms, CTA: 240ms); Word stagger step: 20ms to 35ms; Max cumulative delay before final element starts moving: <= 250ms.

rule: Add bottom padding (0.15em to 0.22em) and matching negative bottom margin to line-mask overflow wrappers so descenders on g, j, p, q, y are not sliced off by overflow: hidden.
do: Add bottom padding (0.15em to 0.22em) and matching negative bottom margin to line-mask overflow wrappers so descenders on g, j, p, q, y are not sliced off by overflow: hidden.
dont: Do not apply tight overflow: hidden directly to an element with line-height: 1.00 without descender padding compensation, or lowercase descenders will be visibly clipped even after the animation finishes.
values: Mask wrapper: overflow: hidden; padding-bottom: 0.18em; margin-bottom: -0.18em; display: block; Inner line element: transform: translate3d(0, 105%, 0) -> translate3d(0, 0%, 0); will-change: transform.

rule: Render the hero H1 text in the initial HTML so it is visible without JavaScript; never hide the H1 behind JS.
do: Render the hero H1 text in the initial HTML so it is visible without JavaScript; never hide the H1 behind JS.
dont: Never hide the hero H1 with .js-loading { opacity: 0 } waiting for React hydration or an external animation library, which delays LCP. | codex (web.dev): keep the H1 text in the initial HTML and do not hide it until an animation runs; do not let a JS-dependent reveal delay or suppress the visible headline.
values: H1 text present in the initial HTML; no JS-gated opacity: 0 or zero-area clip-path on the H1.

rule: When using clip-path: inset() for single-element text or card reveals without extra wrapper divs, keep at least a non-zero initial paint or trigger synchronously via CSS @starting-style.
do: When using clip-path: inset() for single-element text or card reveals without extra wrapper divs, keep at least a non-zero initial paint or trigger synchronously via CSS @starting-style.
dont: Do not animate complex SVG polygon clip-paths with >12 vertices on large text blocks on low-end mobile devices, as path interpolation is more expensive than compositor translate3d inside an overflow: hidden mask.
values: Starting state: clip-path: inset(0 0 100% 0); End state: clip-path: inset(0 0 -15% 0) (negative bottom inset preserves descenders); Transition: clip-path 500ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1).

rule: Preserve screen-reader accessibility on split-text animations by setting aria-label with the full unfragmented sentence on the parent heading and aria-hidden="true" on all generated line/word/character span wrappers.
do: Preserve screen-reader accessibility on split-text animations by setting aria-label with the full unfragmented sentence on the parent heading and aria-hidden="true" on all generated line/word/character span wrappers.
dont: Never split text into DOM <span> nodes per character or word without aria-hidden="true", which causes VoiceOver and NVDA to stutter letter-by-letter.
values:
Parent:

; Split children wrapper: ...; Or include a visually-hidden (.sr-only) span alongside aria-hidden="true" visual spans. [Disagreement Note]: W3C/Deque accessibility practitioners note that aria-label on non-interactive headings can prevent some translation tools or braille displays from navigating word-by-word, so pairing a single Full text with ...split spans... is preferred over aria-label on

when machine-translation compatibility is required.

rule: Revert split-text DOM wrappers back to a single plain text node on animationend (or ResizeObserver width change) so native user text selection, copy-paste, and browser Find-in-Page (Ctrl+F) work seamlessly.
do: Revert split-text DOM wrappers back to a single plain text node on animationend (or ResizeObserver width change) so native user text selection, copy-paste, and browser Find-in-Page (Ctrl+F) work seamlessly.
dont: Do not leave hundreds of nested line/word/char <span> wrappers permanently in the DOM after a one-time entrance reveal if the animation will not replay.
values: Event hook: element.addEventListener('animationend', () => revertToPlainText()); Resize debounce: 150ms.

rule: Option: Combine subtle gaussian blur decay with upward translation on hero text reveals for a softer optical emergence than hard edge clipping alone.
do: Option: Combine subtle gaussian blur decay with upward translation on hero text reveals for a softer optical emergence than hard edge clipping alone.
dont: Never animate filter: blur() with radius > 12px or across > 6 simultaneous elements on mobile viewports, as real-time Gaussian blur shaders drop frame rates below 30fps on integrated mobile GPUs.
values: Option values: Initial keyframe: opacity: 0.01; filter: blur(8px); transform: translateY(12px); Final keyframe: opacity: 1; filter: blur(0px); transform: translateY(0px); Duration: 500ms; Easing: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1).

rule: Short-circuit all mask, translate, and blur text reveal animations immediately under @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), rendering text at final position and full opacity on frame 0.
do: Short-circuit all mask, translate, and blur text reveal animations immediately under @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), rendering text at final position and full opacity on frame 0.
dont: If motion conveys essential state change (e.g., swapping two words in a rotating headline), replace the sliding translation with a gentle 150ms opacity crossfade rather than broken overlapping text.
values: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .reveal-line, .reveal-word { animation: none !important; transition: none !important; transform: none !important; filter: none !important; opacity: 1 !important; clip-path: none !important; } }.

rule: Option: In a centered-stack hero at 1440x900, cap total top chrome + copy + CTA height at <= 380px so at least 520px (58% of the 900px viewport) remains above the fold for the product UI stage.
do: Option: In a centered-stack hero at 1440x900, cap total top chrome + copy + CTA height at <= 380px so at least 520px (58% of the 900px viewport) remains above the fold for the product UI stage.

values: Option values: Viewport: 1440x900; Sticky header: 64px; Top hero padding: 48px-64px; Announcement pill: 28px (+16px margin); H1 (2 lines max): 136px (+16px margin); Subtitle (2 lines max): 56px (+24px margin); CTA row: 44px (+40px margin); Total copy block bottom Y-coordinate: <= 440px from top; Visible product UI height above fold: >= 460px.

rule: Option: On mobile 390x844 viewports, keep the entire copy + CTA block within the top 420px-460px so at least 380px-420px (45%-50% of the 844px screen) displays the product UI above the fold.

rule: Replace or art-direct the wide 16:10 desktop screenshot on 390x844 mobile viewports using <picture> or a dedicated focused component crop (4:3 or 1:1 ratio, or a 130%-width left-anchored focal crop) instead of scaling a 1200px desktop dashboard down to 342px width.

rule: Option: Use negative margin overlap (-24px to -48px) with a backdrop-blurred glass badge or floating command palette card overlapping the top edge of the hero product frame to anchor copy to UI and save vertical pixels.
do: Option: Use negative margin overlap (-24px to -48px) with a backdrop-blurred glass badge or floating command palette card overlapping the top edge of the hero product frame to anchor copy to UI and save vertical pixels.

rule: Option: Strip redundant browser chrome (URL bars, bookmark bars, heavy OS window frames) from hero product mockups, using at most a minimal 28px-32px header bar with 3 subtle 8px window dots at 20% opacity.
do: Option: Strip redundant browser chrome (URL bars, bookmark bars, heavy OS window frames) from hero product mockups, using at most a minimal 28px-32px header bar with 3 subtle 8px window dots at 20% opacity.

values: Option values: Minimal header bar height: 28px to 32px; Traffic-light dots: 8pxx8px, gap 6px, background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.15) (monochrome) rather than saturated macOS red/yellow/green unless showing a native macOS app app; Outer frame border-radius: 12px to 16px; Inner padding: 1px specular border wrapper.

rule: Construct dark mode foundations using cool obsidian or warm carbon near-blacks (#08090A to #0F1012) stepped in perceptual OKLCH lightness increments rather than flat #000000 with harsh drop shadows.
do: Construct dark mode foundations using cool obsidian or warm carbon near-blacks (#08090A to #0F1012) stepped in perceptual OKLCH lightness increments rather than flat #000000 with harsh drop shadows.
dont: except: use pure #000000 canvas only when embedding black-background WebGL/video renders where a #0A0A0C background would expose the video bounding rectangle. | disagrees: codex: a third-party scan reports a pure #000000 background for one named brand; hex values for named brands were not verified by official sources.
values: Linear Obsidian Palette: Page Canvas #08090A (oklch(14% 0.007 265)), Level-1 Surface #0F1011 (oklch(17.5% 0.007 265)), Level-2 Elevated Card #141517 (oklch(20% 0.008 265)), Level-3 Popover/Modal #1C1D21 (oklch(23.5% 0.01 265)); Primary Text #F7F8F8, Secondary Text #8A8F98, Muted Text #5E626A (about 3.2:1 on #08090A, not text-safe: decorative or disabled elements only). [Disagreement Note]: Linear, Raycast (#07080A), and Supabase (#121212 / #171717) avoid pure #000000 to preserve surface depth and prevent OLED smear, whereas Vercel (#000000 with #0A0A0A cards) and Resend (#000000 void canvas with #06060A surfaces) deliberately use pure #000000 as a theatrical stage so 3D specular objects disappear seamlessly into the viewport background.

rule: Replace dark-mode drop shadows with 1px translucent hairline borders (rgba(255,255,255,0.06) to 0.12) and a top-edge specular highlight gradient to define card elevation.
do: Replace dark-mode drop shadows with 1px translucent hairline borders (rgba(255,255,255,0.06) to 0.12) and a top-edge specular highlight gradient to define card elevation.
dont: Do not apply bright 1px specular borders to every minor table cell or secondary badge; reserve the top specular highlight for primary feature cards and modal containers.
values: Base card border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.07) (or Resend frost tint: rgba(214, 235, 253, 0.19)); Hover border: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.16); Top specular rim: background: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0%, rgba(255,255,255,0.22) 50%, transparent 100%) on a 1px top pseudo-element (or box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.10)).

rule: Option: Restrict saturated brand accent colors to <= 5% of visible viewport pixels (primary CTA, active status dot, focus ring, or subtle ambient light bleed), keeping 95% of the dark UI achromatic.
do: Option: Restrict saturated brand accent colors to <= 5% of visible viewport pixels (primary CTA, active status dot, focus ring, or subtle ambient light bleed), keeping 95% of the dark UI achromatic.
dont: Never color entire section backgrounds, multiple competing cards, or long body copy in saturated brand accent hues in dark mode. | disagrees: codex: hex values and accent roles were not verified by official sources; the 5% figure has no source. | codex (CANDIDATE, design hypothesis): assign the accent to a single action or semantic category per surface and use hue/saturation variation instead of competing glows; effect on conversion or perceived quality is not demonstrated.
values: Option accent tokens by hue family (examples only): indigo #5E6AD2 (hover #7170FF); emerald #3ECF8E on charcoal #0F0F0F / #171717 with #2E2E2E border; coral red #FF6363 or blue #55B3FF; purple #6C47FF on #111113 and #212126; amber #FF801F or blue #3B9EFF; off-white #EDEDED primary CTA with blue #0070F3 / #3291FF secondary.

rule: Option: Eliminate the "AI-generated template" look by avoiding the cliché cyan-to-magenta (#00F2FE to #FF0080) or purple-to-pink (#8B5CF6 to #EC4899) multi-stop text gradients and giant unmasked radial blobs.
do: Option: Eliminate the "AI-generated template" look by avoiding the cliché cyan-to-magenta (#00F2FE to #FF0080) or purple-to-pink (#8B5CF6 to #EC4899) multi-stop text gradients and giant unmasked radial blobs.
dont: Do not use multi-hue rainbow gradients unless specifically depicting a color-picker feature or a mesh-shader WebGL art directed as a distinct background canvas.
values: Option values: Anti-patterns to ban: linear-gradient(90deg, #8B5CF6, #EC4899, #3B82F6) on H1 text; unclipped filter: blur(120px) neon circles at 50% opacity; saturated neon 2px borders. Studio replacement: Monochrome metallic text gradient linear-gradient(180deg, #FFFFFF 0%, #A1A1AA 100%) (or subtle single-hue tint #FFFFFF to #C7D2FE), and Conic/Radial ambient lighting capped at 8%-14% opacity (e.g., radial-gradient(ellipse 60% 40% at 50% 0%, rgba(94, 106, 210, 0.14), transparent 70%)) masked behind a 1px structural grid.

rule: Option: Use high-contrast off-white primary buttons (#F4F4F5 or #EDEDED with #09090B dark text) on dark hero backgrounds for maximum focal punch, or tactile single-hue gradient buttons with an inset top highlight.

dont: Never use a flat neon fill button with white text if the WCAG contrast ratio between white (#FFFFFF) and the bright accent fill drops below 4.5:1 (for example white on #3ECF8E emerald is 2.05:1, so use dark text there). | note: white on #6875F5 is about 3.9:1 at the top of the gradient and fails 4.5:1; darken the gradient start or use dark text.
values: Option values: Option A (Monochrome High-Contrast Primary CTA): background: #EDEDED; color: #0A0A0A; hover: #FFFFFF; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.2), 0 4px 14px rgba(255,255,255,0.12). Option B (Tactile Brand CTA; white text on the #6875F5 stop is ~3.9:1, below 4.5:1): background: linear-gradient(180deg, #6875F5 0%, #5E6AD2 100%); color: #FFFFFF; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.25), 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.4).

rule: Option: Layer subtle monochromatic SVG fractalNoise texture (1.5%-3% opacity) or 1px structural grid lines (rgba(255,255,255,0.03) to 0.05) over dark canvases to prevent 8-bit gradient banding and add physical material tactility.
do: Option: Layer subtle monochromatic SVG fractalNoise texture (1.5%-3% opacity) or 1px structural grid lines (rgba(255,255,255,0.03) to 0.05) over dark canvases to prevent 8-bit gradient banding and add physical material tactility.
dont: Never exceed 4% opacity on noise overlays or use animated film-grain canvas loops that burn CPU/battery on laptops.

rule: Cap primary text luminance at #F0F0F2 to #F7F8F8 rather than pure #FFFFFF for multi-line body paragraphs on dark surfaces to prevent astigmatism halation (fuzzing/bleeding of white text on dark backgrounds).
do: Cap primary text luminance at #F0F0F2 to #F7F8F8 rather than pure #FFFFFF for multi-line body paragraphs on dark surfaces to prevent astigmatism halation (fuzzing/bleeding of white text on dark backgrounds).
dont: Never drop muted metadata or placeholder text below #52525B on a #0A0A0B canvas (which falls below 3.0:1 and becomes unreadable on non-OLED monitors in bright rooms). | note: #6E7178 on #0A0A0B is about 4.1:1, below 4.5: not for body text.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): Display H1: #FFFFFF to #F4F4F5; Body/Paragraph primary text: #E4E4E7 to #EDEDED (contrast ratio ~13.5:1 to 15.5:1 against #0A0A0B); Secondary body text: #94969C to #A1A1AA (contrast ratio ~6.8:1 to 7.8:1, passing WCAG AAA 7:1); Muted/caption text: #6E7178 (about 4.1:1 against #0A0A0B, below 4.5: not for body text; captions at large size or non-essential metadata only).

rule: Encode interactive surface states (hover, active, selected) using translucent white alpha steps (rgba(255,255,255,0.03) -> 0.06 -> 0.09) rather than opaque hex overrides so underlying ambient lighting and tint bleed through naturally.
do: Encode interactive surface states (hover, active, selected) using translucent white alpha steps (rgba(255,255,255,0.03) -> 0.06 -> 0.09) rather than opaque hex overrides so underlying ambient lighting and tint bleed through naturally.
dont: Do not use translucent alpha backgrounds on sticky headers or floating dropdown menus without pairing backdrop-filter: blur(12px-20px) and at least 75%-85% base surface opacity (#0A0A0BCC), otherwise scrolling text underneath collides visually with menu labels.
values: Resting card/row: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.02); Hover state: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05); Active/Pressed state: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08); Selected state: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.07) + 1px border rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.14).

rule: Choose the WAI-ARIA APG Disclosure Navigation pattern (<button aria-expanded="true|false" aria-controls="nav-list"> inside <nav>) when the mobile menu is an inline or non-blocking dropdown of navigation links that does not obscure the entire viewport or require focus trapping.
do: Choose the WAI-ARIA APG Disclosure Navigation pattern (<button aria-expanded="true|false" aria-controls="nav-list"> inside <nav>) when the mobile menu is an inline or non-blocking dropdown of navigation links that does not obscure the entire viewport or require focus trapping.
dont: Never use a non-trapping Disclosure pattern if the mobile menu is position: fixed; inset: 0 covering the entire screen with body { overflow: hidden }, because Tab will move focus to invisible background links behind the full-screen overlay (violating WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured). | codex (APG): disclosure keyboard model is Tab/Shift+Tab across buttons and visible links, Space/Enter toggles, Escape closes and returns focus to the opener; arrows/Home/End are optional in the APG example. | codex (APG): disclosure is the default for ordinary navigation and the dialog model is reserved for truly modal interfaces; these answer different interactions, not a contradiction.
values:
HTML structure:
  • ...
; Focus trap: NONE (users Tab naturally through links and into the page); Escape key: closes disclosure panel and returns focus to the toggle button. [Disagreement Note]: WAI-ARIA APG favors non-trapping Disclosure for simple link lists so keyboard users are not trapped, whereas Radix UI / Vercel / Linear implement full-screen mobile menus as modal Dialogs/Sheets (role="dialog" aria-modal="true") with strict focus trapping and body scroll-lock because the overlay visually covers 100% of the 390x844 viewport. Both are valid only when visual presentation matches semantics (inline panel = Disclosure; full-screen scroll-locked overlay = Modal Dialog).

rule: Implement full-screen or backdrop-dimmed mobile navigation overlays using native <dialog> opened with .showModal() (which already makes the rest of the page inert), or role="dialog" aria-modal="true" on a div with strict focus trapping and manual inert on the background content.
do: Implement full-screen or backdrop-dimmed mobile navigation overlays using native <dialog> opened with .showModal() (which already makes the rest of the page inert), or role="dialog" aria-modal="true" on a div with strict focus trapping and manual inert on the background content.
dont: Do not apply role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" without also trapping keyboard focus and marking background content inert, as screen reader virtual cursors (VoiceOver swipe / NVDA down-arrow) will otherwise escape into the background page. | disagrees: gemini internal: rule 51 (non-trapping disclosure) vs rule 52 (modal dialog with focus trap) apply by visual presentation; codex agrees they are different interactions. | codex (APG): use a modal dialog/sheet only when the overlay is truly modal (move focus in, trap Tab, close on Escape, return focus to invoker); do not trap focus on a link list that must stay navigable with the page.
values: Container: <dialog aria-label="Navigation menu"> opened via showModal() (page already inert, no manual inert needed) or <div role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="Site navigation"> (manual inert on <main> and <footer> siblings required); overflow: hidden on document.documentElement; Focus trap: Tab from last interactive element (e.g. "Sign Up" CTA) wraps to first interactive element (Close button); Escape key: closes dialog immediately.

rule: Use plain <nav><ul><li><a> link semantics for marketing site navigation (desktop or mobile) and reserve role="menu", role="menubar" and role="menuitem" for OS-style application menus.
do: Use plain <nav><ul><li><a> link semantics for marketing site navigation (desktop or mobile) and reserve role="menu", role="menubar" and role="menuitem" for OS-style application menus.
dont: Never apply role="menu", role="menubar", or role="menuitem" to marketing site navigation links, as those ARIA roles hijack Arrow keys and disable standard link interactions. | except: use role="menu" and role="menuitem" for in-app action menus (like a "More actions..." context menu or command menu widget) where ArrowUp/ArrowDown navigation and single-tab-stop composite widget behavior are expected. | codex (APG): for ordinary site navigation use disclosure buttons that show/hide link lists; do not use role=menu just because the UI is informally called a menu.
values:
Correct semantics:
  • Pricing
; Prohibited roles on marketing nav: role="menu", role="menubar", role="menuitem".

rule: Programmatically manage focus across mobile menu lifecycle: on open, move focus to the Close button or first interactive element (for modal dialogs); on close (via Close button, Escape key, backdrop tap, or route change), return focus to the exact hamburger trigger button.
do: Programmatically manage focus across mobile menu lifecycle: on open, move focus to the Close button or first interactive element (for modal dialogs); on close (via Close button, Escape key, backdrop tap, or route change), return focus to the exact hamburger trigger button.
dont: Never mount the close button at a different screen coordinate than the open hamburger button (keep both pinned at top-right, e.g., top: 12px; right: 16px, 44x44px) so double-tapping in place toggles the menu effortlessly. | codex (APG): for a large modal sheet, focus a static heading with tabindex=-1 when that helps reading; on close return focus to the invoker unless it no longer exists; do not auto-focus the first link if that hides relevant context.
values: Open focus latency: synchronously after DOM mount / requestAnimationFrame; Close focus target: triggerButtonRef.current.focus(); Minimum touch target size for hamburger/close buttons: 44x44px (48x48px recommended, comfortably exceeding WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 24x24px minimum).

rule: Option: Animate floating popover mobile menus from the top-right trigger corner using transform-origin: calc(100% - 24px) top, scale(0.95) -> scale(1), and opacity 0 -> 1 over 180ms-220ms.
do: Option: Animate floating popover mobile menus from the top-right trigger corner using transform-origin: calc(100% - 24px) top, scale(0.95) -> scale(1), and opacity 0 -> 1 over 180ms-220ms.
dont: Never animate height: 0 to height: auto with JavaScript height polling on 60Hz mobile devices when a compositor scale(0.95 -> 1) + opacity transition achieves 60fps with zero layout reflow.
values: Option values: Initial closed state: opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.95) translateY(-6px); transform-origin: calc(100% - 24px) 0%; pointer-events: none; visibility: hidden; Open state: opacity: 1; transform: scale(1) translateY(0); visibility: visible; Transition: transform 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), opacity 160ms ease-out; Container margin: 12px inset from viewport edges, border-radius: 16px.

rule: Option: Build nested product sub-menus inside mobile navigation (e.g., "Products", "Developers") as inline vertical accordion disclosures (<button aria-expanded="false">) rather than sliding multi-page drill-down carousels.
do: Option: Build nested product sub-menus inside mobile navigation (e.g., "Products", "Developers") as inline vertical accordion disclosures (<button aria-expanded="false">) rather than sliding multi-page drill-down carousels.
dont: Avoid horizontal nested drill-down views with "< Back" buttons unless the site has > 30 navigation items across 3 hierarchy levels (for example a full product catalog), as hiding top-level links behind drill-downs slows navigation on SaaS sites with <= 12 links.
values: Option values: Sub-section toggle: <button aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="sub-products">Products <svg aria-hidden="true">...</svg></button>; Sub-menu items: 2-column compact icon+label grid or indented vertical list (padding-left: 16px, min row height: 44px); Accordion animation: CSS grid-template-rows: 0fr -> 1fr over 180ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1).

rule: Option: Pin the primary conversion CTAs ("Start Building" / "Sign Up" and "Log In") inside a sticky bottom footer bar or top action cluster within the open mobile navigation sheet so the user never has to scroll past expanded sub-menus to convert.
do: Option: Pin the primary conversion CTAs ("Start Building" / "Sign Up" and "Log In") inside a sticky bottom footer bar or top action cluster within the open mobile navigation sheet so the user never has to scroll past expanded sub-menus to convert.
dont: Never omit the primary Sign Up / Log In actions from the mobile menu when collapsing desktop header buttons at < 768px.
values: Option values: Mobile nav CTA footer: position: sticky; bottom: 0; padding: 16px 24px calc(16px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)); background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(10,10,11,0) 0%, #0A0A0B 25%); Button height: 48px, full-width or 50/50 split row (gap: 12px).

rule: Auto-close the mobile navigation overlay and restore body scroll on viewport resize above the desktop breakpoint (>= 768px or >= 1024px) via matchMedia change listener.
do: Auto-close the mobile navigation overlay and restore body scroll on viewport resize above the desktop breakpoint (>= 768px or >= 1024px) via matchMedia change listener.
dont: Never leave body scroll-lock (overflow: hidden) or focus traps active based solely on a click state without cleaning up on breakpoint transitions or SPA route changes.
values: Breakpoint listener: window.matchMedia('(min-width: 768px)').addEventListener('change', (e) => { if (e.matches) closeMobileMenu(); }); Also remove document.body overflow: hidden lock on unmount.

rule: Replace a "Trusted by" logo bar of unrecognizable startup logos or monochrome filler badges with a concrete, verifiable usage or performance metric bar right below the fold.
do: Replace a "Trusted by" logo bar of unrecognizable startup logos or monochrome filler badges with a concrete, verifiable usage or performance metric bar right below the fold.
dont: Never display a "Trusted by" logo bar populated with unrecognizable startup logos or monochrome filler badges. | Do not display vanity cumulative counters that feel unverifiable or inflated without context, or small total user counts (< 100 users) which trigger negative social proof ("nobody uses this yet"). | codex (NN/g): too few displayed supporters can signal lack of approval; no numeric user threshold is given by the source; offer context or more relevant proof such as a measured result or identifiable testimonial.
values: Early-stage metric bar: 3 to 4 concrete counters taken from real data, each with a specific label, method and date plus a verification link; Numeral typography: 32px-44px font-weight 600, font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, paired with a 13px-14px label. Use no placeholder or invented counters.

rule: Pair every customer testimonial with a real human avatar photo (minimum 40x40px), full name, exact role title, company link, and a bolded quantifiable outcome phrase inside a quote capped at 25-40 words.
do: Pair every customer testimonial with a real human avatar photo (minimum 40x40px), full name, exact role title, company link, and a bolded quantifiable outcome phrase inside a quote capped at 25-40 words.
dont: Never use stock photography, AI-generated faces, initials-only circles, or anonymous attributions ("- VP of Engineering at Fortune 500"), which read as fabricated. | disagrees: codex: measured benefit of testimonial formats for an early SaaS is UNKNOWN; do not promise conversion lift without your own experiment. | codex (NN/g): show the testimonial source identity and context (name, role/company or verifiable detail); do not use anonymous vague praise as strong proof. | codex (NN/g): tie the testimonial to a concrete person/source and, when possible, to the original publication or case; do not publish quotes without permission or verifiable context. | caveat: Do not promise a conversion lift from a specific social-proof tactic (logo row, testimonial, founder note, integration, metric) for an early SaaS without your own experiment; a secondary lead-gen case study does not establish the same effect for other audiences. Do not quote third-party lift figures as expected results.
values: Quote length: 25 to 40 words (2-3 lines max); Highlighted outcome: 1 bolded phrase of 4-8 words (e.g., **"cut CI build times from 18m to 2m"**); Avatar: 40x40px to 48x48px WebP/AVIF rounded-full with 1px inner border; Attribution: Full Name + Specific Title ("Staff Infrastructure Engineer at [Company]") + clickable verification link (X/LinkedIn post or case study).

rule: Use an Ecosystem & Integration Architecture Strip ("Works seamlessly with your stack: GitHub, Postgres, Stripe, Next.js, Slack") with live code/webhook snippets to borrow visual familiarity ethically when you lack customer logos.
do: Use an Ecosystem & Integration Architecture Strip ("Works seamlessly with your stack: GitHub, Postgres, Stripe, Next.js, Slack") with live code/webhook snippets to borrow visual familiarity ethically when you lack customer logos.
dont: Never omit the "Integrates with" / "Compatible with" label above ecosystem logos, as passing off integration partners (like AWS, GitHub, or Stripe) as paying customers destroys buyer trust upon discovery (NN/g deceptive pattern guidelines).
values: Integration grid: 6 to 10 monochrome or dark-adapted ecosystem icons (24x24px to 32x32px) inside interactive tabs or cards that reveal a real 6-10 line integration snippet or 1-click connect preview; Explicit heading label: "Integrates in 5 minutes with" or "Built on battle-tested infrastructure".

rule: Place an authentic Security, Compliance & Architecture Posture Row (linking directly to your Trust Center, Vanta/Drata live monitor, or concrete security architecture specs) adjacent to enterprise CTAs and signup forms—never use self-made "100% Secure" badges.
do: Place an authentic Security, Compliance & Architecture Posture Row (linking directly to your Trust Center, Vanta/Drata live monitor, or concrete security architecture specs) adjacent to enterprise CTAs and signup forms—never use self-made "100% Secure" badges.
dont: Never display a SOC 2 or ISO 27001 badge if you have not completed the audit (or explicitly label it "SOC 2 Type I Audited / Type II In Observation via Vanta" with a link to your security whitepaper). | codex (NN/g): show security/credibility signals and company information when they resolve a relevant buyer doubt; do not show certifications, logos or compliance claims the product does not hold.
values: Verified trust signals: SOC 2 Type II (with "Request Report ->" link to trust.domain.com), GDPR / CCPA DPA ready, HIPAA BAA available, AES-256 at rest / TLS 1.3 in transit, SSO/SAML & RBAC, and live 90-day uptime percentage fetched from Statuspage; Placement: within 120px of primary signup form or pricing table. [Note]: Baymard's trust-seal findings concern consumer checkout pages, not SOC 2 or B2B security posture; self-made generic padlock graphics are a weak signal, while verifiable specs and a linked trust centre are stronger. Treat Baymard as a weak analogy only.

rule: Option: Showcase live open-source or community velocity signals (GitHub stars, weekly npm downloads, contributors, Discord members, or public changelog cadence) as dynamic proof of product momentum.
do: Option: Showcase live open-source or community velocity signals (GitHub stars, weekly npm downloads, contributors, Discord members, or public changelog cadence) as dynamic proof of product momentum.
dont: Do not display a public changelog snippet if the most recent entry is stale, which signals an abandoned product to SaaS evaluators.
values: observed on live site: Live badge metrics: GitHub stars count, weekly npm downloads, a "releases shipped in the last 90 days" count (linked to /changelog with dated entries); Changelog preview row: 3 most recent shipped features with exact dates.

rule: Position micro-proof and risk-reversal copy directly below or beside the primary CTA button ("Free up to 10,000 emails/mo · No credit card required · 2-minute setup") to resolve action anxiety at the exact point of click.
do: Position micro-proof and risk-reversal copy directly below or beside the primary CTA button ("Free up to 10,000 emails/mo · No credit card required · 2-minute setup") to resolve action anxiety at the exact point of click.
dont: Do not place vague marketing slogans ("Join the revolution") beneath the CTA button where users look for pricing/commitment terms.
values: Micro-copy typography: 12px to 13px, color: #8A8F98 (dark mode) or #64748B (light mode), margin-top: 10px-12px below primary CTA; Content: 2 to 3 concrete friction reducers separated by middle dots (·): [Free tier quota] · [No credit card required] · [Setup time or live interactive demo link].

rule: Option: Embed an interactive, zero-signup product sandbox or live code/UI playground above or immediately below the fold (Clerk component switcher, Resend live email sender, Supabase SQL editor) so the product proves itself directly.
do: Option: Embed an interactive, zero-signup product sandbox or live code/UI playground above or immediately below the fold (Clerk component switcher, Resend live email sender, Supabase SQL editor) so the product proves itself directly.
dont: Never gate an interactive landing page preview behind an email capture modal before the user can click at least 2-3 interactive states.
values: observed on live site: Sandbox responds instantly client-side; Pre-populated with 3-4 clickable preset scenarios (e.g., "Dark theme", "MFA prompt", "Webhook payload"); Zero auth required to test.

rule: Design SaaS benefit data cards around the 3-Second Preattentive Hierarchy: 1 hero numeral (36px-52px), 1 semantic delta badge (+42% or -180ms), and 1 single-variable visual encoding with <= 5 data points.
do: Design SaaS benefit data cards around the 3-Second Preattentive Hierarchy: 1 hero numeral (36px-52px), 1 semantic delta badge (+42% or -180ms), and 1 single-variable visual encoding with <= 5 data points.
dont: Never embed a full multi-axis production BI chart with 4 data series, 12 monthly ticks, and dual Y-axes inside a 360pxx280px marketing bento card. | disagrees: codex: no study establishes a universal 3-second threshold, optimal chart type or mandatory labelling for SaaS benefit cards; treat as a test requirement.
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): Card reading budget: <= 3.0 seconds (verified by 5-second usability test); Max data series per card: 1 primary + 1 baseline comparison; Max discrete bars/nodes: 4 to 5; Hero KPI numeral: 36px-52px, font-weight 600-700, letter-spacing -0.03em, font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; Delta pill: 12px-13px medium, e.g. background: rgba(62, 207, 142, 0.14), color: #3ECF8E; Supporting title: <= 6 words (14px-15px).

rule: Eliminate detached color legends on benefit cards; use direct on-chart labeling placed within 8px-12px of the line endpoint or inside/beside the bar.
do: Eliminate detached color legends on benefit cards; use direct on-chart labeling placed within 8px-12px of the line endpoint or inside/beside the bar.
dont: Never place a color key at the bottom of a card requiring users to saccade back and forth between colored dots and chart lines, which adds cognitive lookup overhead.
values: Legend count: 0 detached legends; Direct label placement: right-aligned at line terminus (x + 8px) or inline on horizontal bar; Label font-size: 12px-13px (font-weight: 500, matching line/bar color or high-contrast #F4F4F5 on highlighted series, #8A8F98 on baseline series).

rule: Match chart geometry strictly to the benefit claim type: use 2-bar Horizontal Bar Charts for speed/cost reductions ("5x faster"), Slopegraphs or 2-point Delta Bars for Before/After transitions, and smoothed Area Sparklines with an highlighted terminal dot for growth/latency trends.
do: Match chart geometry strictly to the benefit claim type: use 2-bar Horizontal Bar Charts for speed/cost reductions ("5x faster"), Slopegraphs or 2-point Delta Bars for Before/After transitions, and smoothed Area Sparklines with an highlighted terminal dot for growth/latency trends.
dont: Never use pie charts, 3D donut charts, radar/spider charts, or stacked area charts with > 2 segments on marketing benefit cards—human eyes judge 1D horizontal length faster and more accurately than 2D angles or arc areas (Cleveland & McGill / NN/g). | disagrees: codex: no study establishes an optimal chart type for benefit cards.
values: Speed/Latency comparison: 2 horizontal bars (Top bar: Your Product in brand accent #3ECF8E or #5E6AD2 at 20% width labeled "42ms"; Bottom bar: Legacy/Baseline in muted #27272A at 100% width labeled "240ms"); Growth trend: SVG cubic-bezier sparkline (stroke-width: 2px) with subtle gradient fill below (opacity 0.18 -> 0.00) and a 6px glowing terminal circle at the final data point.

rule: Option: Visually polarize Before/After comparisons by styling the "Before" state in low-contrast desaturated gray (#27272A fill, #71717A text, dashed 1px border) and the "After" state in high-contrast surface elevation with the single saturated brand accent and a callout multiplier badge ("-82% latency").
do: Option: Visually polarize Before/After comparisons by styling the "Before" state in low-contrast desaturated gray (#27272A fill, #71717A text, dashed 1px border) and the "After" state in high-contrast surface elevation with the single saturated brand accent and a callout multiplier badge ("-82% latency").
dont: Never assign two equally bright saturated colors (e.g. bright blue for "Before" and bright purple for "After"), which forces the viewer to read labels carefully to tell which bar is the winner.
values: Option values: Before series: fill/stroke #2E3035, text #8A8F98, optional stroke-dasharray: 4 4; After series: fill/stroke brand accent (e.g. #5E6AD2 or #3ECF8E) or #FFFFFF with 12px ambient glow, text #F7F8F8 font-weight 600; Multiplier pill positioned directly between or at the end of the two bars.

rule: Strip chart gridlines down to at most 2-3 ultra-faint reference lines (rgba(255,255,255,0.04)) and omit X/Y axis tick labels unless an explicit threshold benchmark (e.g., "SLA target: 100ms") is being crossed.
do: Strip chart gridlines down to at most 2-3 ultra-faint reference lines (rgba(255,255,255,0.04)) and omit X/Y axis tick labels unless an explicit threshold benchmark (e.g., "SLA target: 100ms") is being crossed.
dont: Do not omit axis baselines or zero-anchors on bar charts (bar charts must always start at a 0 baseline so bar length ratios remain honest; line sparklines may crop the Y-axis range to show trend shape).
values: heuristic (not source-documented numbers): Gridline count: 0 to 3 horizontal lines max at rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.04); Axis tick labels: omitted or limited to 2 endpoints (Start / Now); Threshold line: 1px dashed rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.25) with direct inline pill label.

rule: Write the benefit card headline as the conclusion ("Deploy previews build 4.2x faster") rather than a neutral chart title ("Build Duration Over Time (Seconds)"), and pair green/red delta colors with directional arrows (↑/↓) for color-blind accessibility.
do: Write the benefit card headline as the conclusion ("Deploy previews build 4.2x faster") rather than a neutral chart title ("Build Duration Over Time (Seconds)"), and pair green/red delta colors with directional arrows (↑/↓) for color-blind accessibility.
dont: Never rely on green vs red color alone to distinguish "Before/Bad" from "After/Good" without directional icons, text prefixes (+ / - / ↓), and luminance contrast difference (violates WCAG 1.4.1 for deuteranopia/protanopia users). | codex (CANDIDATE, hypothesis): put the conclusion title and main value next to the chart, label units and periods directly, use before/after only with identical baseline and interval; do not use a decorative chart unrelated to the claimed benefit.
values: Conclusion-first title: 15px-18px font-weight 600 (#F4F4F5), <= 7 words stating the takeaway; Redundant encoding for WCAG 1.4.1 (Use of Color): pair green (#3ECF8E) or red (#EF4444) with explicit symbol + sign (e.g. "↓ 78% build time" or "+34% conversion ↑").

rule: If the hero product image is the LCP candidate, include it in the initial HTML (or preload it when referenced only from CSS), use fetchpriority=high and never lazy-load it.
do: If the hero product image is the LCP candidate, include it in the initial HTML (or preload it when referenced only from CSS), use fetchpriority=high and never lazy-load it.
dont: Do not raise priority on several images without reason; that reduces the value of prioritisation.
values: fetchpriority="high"

rule: Derive one signature motif from the product's own data transformation, fix its geometry as tokens, and reuse it in at least 5 places (logo, headline accent, product frame, section labels, chart, rail, final CTA).
do: Derive one signature motif from the product's own data transformation, fix its geometry as tokens, and reuse it in at least 5 places (logo, headline accent, product frame, section labels, chart, rail, final CTA).
dont: Do not use decorative shapes that are not the motif (blobs, waves, orbs, glows).
values: Motif geometry fixed once as tokens (angle, stroke width, radius, spacing); reuse count >= 5; decorative non-motif shapes: 0.

rule: Show one causal input->output story in the product frame with specific data (>= 3 named speakers or entities, mono timestamps, >= 2 highlighted sources each visibly linked to its output row), rendered text >= 12px.
do: Show one causal input->output story in the product frame with specific data (>= 3 named speakers or entities, mono timestamps, >= 2 highlighted sources each visibly linked to its output row), rendered text >= 12px.
dont: Do not use lorem ipsum, and do not add floating chips that contradict the copy.
values: Named entities >= 3; highlighted sources >= 2, each linked to an output row; timestamps in mono; rendered text >= 12px.

rule: Use at most 3 families with fixed jobs: a display face only for H1/H2 and hero numerals, a UI sans for everything read, and mono only for machine data (timecodes, counts, labels); keep the H1:body size ratio >= 4.5 and set tracking per face.
do: Use at most 3 families with fixed jobs: a display face only for H1/H2 and hero numerals, a UI sans for everything read, and mono only for machine data (timecodes, counts, labels); keep the H1:body size ratio >= 4.5 and set tracking per face.
dont: Never copy tracking across faces, and do not use mono for prose or display faces for body text.
values: Families <= 3; H1:body ratio >= 4.5; tracking defined per face.

rule: Use hue-bearing neutrals (canvas and text share one hue family, OKLCH chroma 0.008-0.02) with one accent at OKLCH C <= 0.15 that has a semantic job; the primary CTA may use the text colour as fill, and a greyscale screenshot must keep the hierarchy.
do: Use hue-bearing neutrals (canvas and text share one hue family, OKLCH chroma 0.008-0.02) with one accent at OKLCH C <= 0.15 that has a semantic job; the primary CTA may use the text colour as fill, and a greyscale screenshot must keep the hierarchy.
dont: Do not use grey-blue black plus neon, and do not add glow.
values: Neutral chroma 0.008-0.02 (single hue family); accent OKLCH C <= 0.15; glow: none; greyscale test passes.

rule: Give adjacent sections different archetypes (e.g. split, strip, pinned scene, asymmetric bento, inverted band, list, statement), with at most 1 card grid and 1 inverted band per page and section padding from 3 tokens only (128/96/72), symmetric.
do: Give adjacent sections different archetypes (e.g. split, strip, pinned scene, asymmetric bento, inverted band, list, statement), with at most 1 card grid and 1 inverted band per page and section padding from 3 tokens only (128/96/72), symmetric.
dont: Never let adjacent sections share an archetype, and do not use more than 1 card grid or 1 inverted band per page.
values: Section padding tokens: 128 / 96 / 72 px, symmetric top and bottom; card grids <= 1; inverted bands <= 1.

rule: For editorial/product-led pages use 3 radii (12 frame, 8 inner, 6 control), pills only for status tags, hairlines carrying structure and shadows only on overlays.
do: For editorial/product-led pages use 3 radii (12 frame, 8 inner, 6 control), pills only for status tags, hairlines carrying structure and shadows only on overlays.

values: Radii: 12 (frame) / 8 (inner) / 6 (control); pills: status tags only; shadows: overlays only.

rule: Attach a source to every counter, logo and face; each metric carries method, sample and date in mono, integrations appear as "Works with" text, and a concept page states that its data is illustrative.
do: Attach a source to every counter, logo and face; each metric carries method, sample and date in mono, integrations appear as "Works with" text, and a concept page states that its data is illustrative.
dont: Do not show counters, logos or faces without a source.
values: Per metric: method + sample + date in mono; integrations labelled "Works with"; concept pages carry an "illustrative data" note.

rule: Tell the product story twice: once as a one-shot hero sequence (<= 2.5 s, then rest, with a Replay control) and once scrubbed on scroll, with reveals complete by entry 100%.
do: Tell the product story twice: once as a one-shot hero sequence (<= 2.5 s, then rest, with a Replay control) and once scrubbed on scroll, with reveals complete by entry 100%.
dont: Do not use infinite decorative loops.
values: Hero sequence <= 2.5 s then rest, Replay control present; scroll-scrubbed story; reveals complete by entry 100%; infinite loops: 0.

rule: At 25% zoom with the logo hidden the page must still be identifiable; if another brand name could be dropped in unnoticed, the art direction fails.
do: At 25% zoom with the logo hidden the page must still be identifiable; if another brand name could be dropped in unnoticed, the art direction fails.
dont: Do not ship art direction that stays identical when the brand name is swapped.
values: Test: view at 25% zoom, logo hidden, then swap the brand name; the page must still read as this product.
